We take this into account in order to assess monetary conditions and the expected impact. This is one of the factors for us to take into account when determining the optimum path of monetary policy. I understand that was the last question. Thank you for your time.

Title: Governor of the Bank of Russia presented to the State Duma deputies the draft Guidelines for the Unified State Monetary Policy for 2016 and for the period 2017 and 2018
text: Governor of the Bank of Russia Elvira Nabiullina presented the draft to the State Duma deputies The main directions of the unified state monetary policy for 2016 and for the period 2017 and 2018 November 3, 2015 Performance Speech by E. Nabiullina at the joint meeting Financial Market Committee, Budget Committee and Taxes, Committee on Entrepreneurship Colleagues, today we are submitting for your consideration the draft Main Directions of Monetary Policy for 2016-2018. The Working Group has already considered it. In my speech, I will dwell in detail on the forecast scenarios that are described in the Guidelines, as well as on key monetary policy measures. First, just two words about the situation. If we describe it not in figures (indicators), as we are accustomed to, but qualitatively, then we can say that 2015 was the year ofthe primary adaptation of our economy to new conditions. The new conditions are, first of all, the fall in oil prices and the closure of many external financial markets. There was not just a drop in oil prices, but, apparently, a structural transformation of oil is taking place. This will lead to the fact that prices may remain low for a long time. Many even talk about the end of the so-called commodity supercycle. Why? Because demand from emerging markets, primarilyKi-tai, is not going to grow as fast as it used to; second, there are innovations in production that change both the nature of capital investment and payback parameters; and third, there are changes in pricing. Now oil producers are mostly fightingfor market share, not for maintaining prices. Thus, we expect oil prices to remain at a low level in the foreseeable future. If the prices are higher, great. The risks from the policy, which will be based on inflated oil prices, are much greater than the risks if we rely on low prices in our forecasts, and the reality turns out to be slightly more favorable. Therefore, it is extremely important to be balanced and conservative in the budget policy and in the Monetary Policy during this period of uncertainty and a period of volatile difficult situation inthe world markets. including in forecast estimates. Global uncertainty is also due in part to a lack of clarity about the timing and pace of monetary adjustment in key developed economies, including the winding down of unprecedented quantitative easing measures in recent years. In addition, another major factor that has been gaining more and more weight lately is concerns about the growthprospects of developing economies, primarily China, and such concerns affect the expectations for the development of the entire world economy. External conditions will largely determine the outline of the development of the situation in the Russian economy. But in order forour country and our economy to enter a growth trajectory in the next three years, regardless of the constantly changing external conditions, it is necessary, according to the Central Bank, to combine three elements of economic policy: - conservative fiscal policy (but with the restructuring of the structure of expenditures in favor of expenditures that stimulate growth, and not just redistribute national income through taxes, and with a real start of work to improve the efficiency of spending); - the second is a balanced Monetary Policy, which takes into account the balance of inflation risks and risksfor economic growth. I will talk about this in more detail; - and most importantly, a strong agenda of structural reforms is needed to accelerate the diversification of the economy, to increase productivity, which is unacceptably lagging behind many developed countries. It is necessary to make investments and business activity attractive. Therefore, we see the Ost as part of the overall economic policy. The downturn in the Russian economy is now due to a combination of so-called cyclical and structural factors, while the roleof structural factors will gradually increase, and therefore the possibilities of monetary policy to stimulate economic growth are limited. We understand that the level of credit rates is high, and for many industries, or, for example, segments of SMEs , loans are inaccessible, however, we must take into account: - limited monetary stimulus measures, because the restrictions are largely structural; - and, again, the balance of risks to inflation and growth. The latter is especially important, since the specifics of the current situation are a high level of accumulated inflation and high inflation expectations. For example, about two-thirds of the population believes that inflation will not decline. For the public and for businesses, unfortunately,high rates of growth in prices, costs, and wages have become habitual. And in order to adjust expectations, we must first show in practice that these rates can be low, convince people that we are doing what we promise. Namely, that we will actually be able to reduce inflation tothe lowest target value of 4% by the end. 2017. According to sociological surveys about the main problems that concern Russians, inflation is the No. 1 problem. And it was the leading problem last year (70% of respondents said so), this year the number ofRussians who put the problem of inflation in the first place has increased to almost 80%. This is the most important social problem, not only economic. And its solution largely determines people's confidence in economic policy as a whole. That is why the central bank is so focused on the problem of inflation and inflation expectations. Moreover, world experience shows that in countries with so-called anchored inflation expectations (when people's expectations that inflation will be low, persistently low and stable), central banks can pursue softer monetary policy. Unfortunately, our inflation expectations are very high. Our monetary policy is based on forecasts of economic growth. So I'm going to go into a little bit more detail on our forecast. We're looking at three possible scenarios, depending on oil prices. But I want to emphasize that in any scenario, in all scenarios, we are able to control inflation and achieve our goal of reducing it to 4%, as I said, by the end of 2017. The baseline scenario assumes an oil price of 50 per barrel over the entire three-year period. In it, as in all other scenarios, we lay down the preservation of financial sanctions,the current restrictions on the import of certain types of imported goods throughout the forecast horizon. The downturn in the economy will largely be the result of the fact that the economy needs time to adapt to a significantly reduced level of income from foreign economic activityand. According to our estimates, the loss of foreign exchange earnings to the country, both from lower prices for traditional goods of our exports, and from a sharp reduction in external borrowing, amount to about 200 billion US dollars in annual terms, That is, it's about a 40-cent, fairly large-scale decline, and adjusting the economy to such large-scale external changes, of course, will take time. In the baseline scenario, we expect that the growth rate of the Russian economy for the year as a whole will remain negative andin the next year, in 2017, will reach small positive values, and in 2018 - may reach 2.0-3.0%. Consumer demand will continueto be weak against the backdrop of declining real incomes, and the propensity of the population to save more than to spend in such difficult times, and along with consistent Monetary Policy aimed at achieving price stability, this will lead to a gradualreduction in inflationary pressures in the economy. As inflation declines (if it declines in line with our forecast, and now we give forecasts at every meeting of the Board of Directors for inflation for 12 months - such a rolling forecast, unlike how we used to make a forecast for the end of the year), and if inflation continues to decline, and inflation expectations will not grow, then we see an opportunity to continue to reduce our key rate. The second scenario is optimistic. In this scene, oil prices gradually rise to 70-80 per barrel by 2018. There is also a risk scenario with a price of 40 per barrel or lower in 2016-2018. In the optimistic scenario, the constraining effect of external factors on the economy will beless pronounced. And therefore we expect growth to recover in 2016. Inflation, as in the baseline scenario, will gradually decline. At the same time, the potential for lowering the key rate in this scenario will be slightly greater. In the face of heightened uncertainty about the prospects not only for the oil market, but for the global economy as a whole, we believe that it is important to be prepared for the most adverse developments. That is why we are considering a risk scenario. And in the event of an increase in risks, we are ready to use the entire arsenal of tools and measures available to us, including the implementation of foreign exchange sales to maintain financial stability. increasing the volume of currency refinancing. We already have such tools, and we are ready to use them in the event of such an unfavorable combination of circumstances. Last year, when we faced an unfavorable combination of a sharp decline in the price of oil, the effect of financial sanctions, and the peak of payments on the externaldebts of Russian companies and switched to inflation targeting, to free floating of the exchange rate, we experienced a certain crisis of confidence on the part of the market - the market did not immediately believe that we would be able to adhere to the principles of monetary policy. But the measures that we took at the end of last year, in our opinion, we consider justified. Inflation has stabilized, financial markets have also stabilized, and this has allowed us to reduce, among other things, the key rate, including the reduction frompros to foreign exchange liquidity. Now there are no problems with foreign exchange liquidity. During the first half of the year, we consistently reduced the rate, as I have already said, but in September and at the last meeting, which took place literally on Friday, we decided to keep the rate at 11%. This temporarily narrowed the space for easing the monetary policy. Lower inflation is a priority of our monetary policy, but we understand that not only the deterioration of the foreign economic situation can affect the inflationrate, inflation may also accelerate if the growth rate of tariffs of natural monopolies is revised. the pace of indexation of various payments and, in general, there will be a softening of the budget policy. In our opinion, it is impossible in any caseto unleash an inflationary spiral by measures of tariff and budget policy. In the current environment of tight monetary policy, its impact on different sectors is very different. There are industries that have benefited from devaluation, received income and are less dependent on borrowed funds. Butthere are those that have been actively modernized in previous years, they have less need for investment lending. But there are those that have accumulated an excessive debt burden before, and new additional lending at high rates cantear up their already not very stable financial situation. Therefore, the situation in different sectors is very different, we monitor the situation in the real sector of the economy, monitor the situation in individual sectors. And from the point of view of the further development ofloans, we are, of course, concerned about the level of the debt burden and the growth rate of overdue debt both in the economy as a whole and in the sectoral context. The total level of the debt burden of the non-financial sector, including both external loans and bond loans peryam, is now about 80% of GDP. This, although lower than in many developed countries, but higher than in a wide range of emerging market countries, with which we compare ourselves, for example, in the Czech Republic, Turkey, India, Poland, South Africa, Mexico, Indonesia and so on. e. Of the BRICS countries, the debt burden of the non-financial sector is higher only in China, but at the moment it is the high debt burden that is considered by many experts to be a factor that can lead to a further slowdown in economic growth in this country. And so we need to look not only at the growth of the debt burden, but very importantly, at attracting direct investment in certain sectors so that there is an increase in investment. And therefore we need to develop capital. There are sectors where you can increase the levelof debt financing without compromising financial stability, for example, this is high-quality mortgages. And here the government program to support mortgages also played a role. and we are changing our regulatory system to ensure that high-qualitymortgages develop. Small and medium-sized businesses at this stage of the transition to growth in the new conditions will be a priority, because it is there that reserves are laid down to diversify the economy. So far, lending in SMEs is declining, and banks are reluctant to finance thissegm business. We are trying to find ways to support it - both through the recapitalization program and through our special tools. We are also now considering the possibility of reducing the risk ratio for SME loans from 100% to 75%. And at the end, there are literally two questionsabout our special refinancing mechanisms. Given that the rates are high, and there are market failures when there are no sources of long-term money, we have a whole set of programs that allow us to use these special tools, point tools. I will give you fresh figures. I gave figures some time ago on how these tools are used. For example, project financing: out of 100 billion rubles, 40.8 billion rubles have been selected today; for SMEs: out of 50 billion - 33.4 billion rubles; support for non-primary exports: out of 50 billion rubles, 16.3 billion rubles were used; and on military mortgages: 20 billion rubles were used from the limit of 30 billion rubles. These instruments are in demand as long as there are limits that allow us to use them, and we apply them in such a way that our Monetary Policywill exceed the goals stated in the main directions of the Monetary Policy and we would be able to ensure, on the basis of a balance of interests, taking into account the balance of inflation risks and economic risks, the goals that are set before us in terms of both price and financial stability. Thank you very much for your attention! Press Service of the Bank of Russia

Title: Speech at the press conference: financial stability review for the IV quarter of 2020  I quarter of 2021
text: Ksenia Yudaeva's speech at the press Conference: Financial Overview Stability for the IV quarter of 2020 - I quarter of 2021 May 27 , 2021 Performance Good afternoon, dear colleagues! Today we publish the Financial Stability Review for the fourth quarter of 2020 - the first quarter 2021. Since we discussed the last review, the situation in terms of financial stability risks has changed significantly. The main factors affecting the situation in global markets are still related to the coronavirus pandemic. But the nature of its influence on the markets is different now. On the one hand, spikes in infections (say, the latest case inYidiya) and the emergence of new strains of the virus remain uncertainties. However, the impact of these factors on the market is decreasing, and markets are paying more and more attention to the fact that, in general, the global economy is recovering steadily, which is also due to the success of mass vaccination programs in developed countries. As a result, if last year we primarily talked about disinflationary risks, as well as high risks for the banking sector, which are associated with the quality of loan portfolios and the inability of borrowers to service loans, this year the balance of risks has shifted towards pro-inflationary, and the assessment of risks for the banking sector is also decreasing. Fiscal and monetary policy supports high demand, and the offer is limited. The acceleration of inflation and the growth of inflation expectations have already caused a wave of increases in rates or yields in a number of countries, there are noticeable discrepancies in the assessment of the situation between markets and regulators. Low interest rates and soft policies increase the risks of financial stability in this situation. The situation in the US markets traditionally requires the greatest attention. If the acceleration of inflation in this country becomes a stable trend, then the tightening of policy may occur earlier than planned now. This can cause sharpvolatility and capital outflows from emerging markets. However, compared to last year, some emerging markets have reduced room for maneuver due to high debt burdens. It should be noted that in recent years, such problemsin some economies have not led to the effects of infection on other countries. Nevertheless, the situation requires observation in terms of possible risks to financial stability. Around the world, there is now a dilemma related to the search for an optimal schedule for the abolition ofsupport. Their accelerated withdrawal may slow down economic growth. But the extension of measures is fraught with a further accumulation of vulnerabilities. Postponement of work with bad debt, massive (not targeted) business support programs, acti buyback programs They can lead to an increase in the number of so-called "zombie companies" in both developed and developing economies. Stock indices of many countries are now at historical highs, bubbles are forming in real estate markets (in particular, a real increase inhousing prices is observed in the USA, Holland and some European countries). These vulnerabilities can increase volatility in markets during times of stress. The Bank of Russia assesses the recovery of the Russian economy as sustainable. This gave us the opportunityto complete the relaxations and gradually return to pre-pandemic regulation. At the same time, our assessment of credit risks as the main risks for the banking sector in the current situation has improved. Against the backdrop of the economic recovery, the situation is developingaccording to a fairly favorable scenario. Despite the fact that in 2020 the net debt burden indicator of the largest companies increased from 2.0 to 2.9, this growth cannot be considered a stable trend. Its main cause was a decrease in profits, and against the background of a recovery in external and domestic demand, we can expect an increase in profits and an improvement in the debt metrics of companies. On the restructured loans of large large loans. The relief ended on April 1, and we have not yet seen a spike in the share of the "bad" withthe court. Positive trends can be observed in almost the entire set of affected industries. We expect an improvement in the financial situation of oil and gas companies due to the return of oil prices to pre-pandemic levels. The situation in commercial real estate is on the background. The absence of mass quarantine restrictions in Russia in the period under review is also developing according to a moderately positive scenario. Recovery is relatively delayed only in the aviation industry, which is due to the low volume of international traffic. However, the industryis constrained by state support. The SME sector, which was severely affected by the crisis, is recovering unevenly. In such areas as tourism, the hotel business and the catering industry, in the fourth quarter of 2020, the turnover of enterprises was still 30% less than a year earlier. However, a monthly study of small business sentiment conducted by OPORA RUSSIA together with Promsvyazbank, shows a steady increase in business activity in the spring of 2021. Surveys of enterprises by the Bank of Russia also showa gradual recovery in this sector. Credit risks in consumer lending have also decreased significantly compared to last year. By July 1 of this year, regulatory relaxations on restructured loans providedto small and medium-sized businesses and citizens will end. According to our estimates, this will not be a problem for banks. By the beginning of 2021, for most of the restructured debt of citizens (75%), the term of the credit holiday was completed. Nevertheless, in order to further smooth out For banks to get out of regulatory relaxations, we decided to dissolve the macroprudential buffer on consumer loans for 124 billion rubles from June 30. Banks also have a significant margin of safety in the form of a capital buffer, which is 6 trillionrubles. In addition, in 2020, credit institutions earned about 1.6 trillion rubles of profit. All this suggests that banks are able to fully cover losses on restructured loans, moreover, these losses will be stretched over time. Thus, the problem of credit risk caused by the pandemic is gradually being addressed, with other vulnerabilities more pronounced, many of which are related to economic recovery and credit growth, rather than to the risks of credit crunching andbankruptcy, as was the case a year ago. We divide vulnerabilities into short-term vulnerabilities, which in many respects have formed and can carry risks in the near future, and vulnerabilities that are only emerging and will be able to affect financial stability in the medium or longterm. The first challenge is the risk of a bubble in the real estate market. Inthe first quarter of this year, housing prices continued to grow rapidly. According to Rosstat, the growth of prices in the primary market for the first quarter amounted to 17.6% in annual terms, in secondary terms -13.6%. In some regions, price growth exceeded 20%, despite a decrease in real incomes of the population. To assess the risks, we monitor lending standards - the borrower's debt burden and the level of the ratio of the loan amount to the value of the collateral (this is thereverse of the down payment). These indicators correlate with the frequency of defaults and characterize the solvency of the borrower. The down payment on mortgage loans also reflects the degree of security of the loan with collateral and limits the risks of the bank Related to a possible adjustment in housing prices. In the primary mortgage market, the share of loans with a down payment of less than 20% in the total volume of loans provided increased from 24% in the second quarter of 2020 to 45% in the first quarter of 2021, in the secondary market forsuch loans increased from 30 to 33%. At the same time, we see that the share of loans with high PIT has reached a pre-pandemic level. Thus, whereas in the last Financial Stability Review we considered the risks of a bubble to be hypothetical and need to be observed, regulatory measures are now required to prevent the formation of a bubble. Last week, the Bank of Russia announced an increase in macroprudential surcharges on mortgage loans with an initial payment of 15-20% from August 1. If credit standardscontinue to decline or if the accelerated rise in house prices continues, we will consider an additional increase in the surcharges. The latest data also indicate an active recovery of unsecured consumer lending: as of May 1 , the annualized growth rate over the past three months was about 19%. The growth of lending to the population is not accompanied by a commensurate increase in income and leads to an increase in the debt burden. The population on average now directs to servicing loans. about 12% of disposable cash income. In this regard, from July 1, we are returning to the pre-pandemic level of macroprudential surcharges on new consumer loans. The second vulnerability is the interest rate risk of the banking sector, which may be partiallyrealized in the context of the Bank of Russia's transition to a neutral monetary policy. Expansion of lending to legal entities at floating rates and the purchase by banks of government bonds with variable coupons, as well as the growth of the interest rate derivatives market in the last two years the ode contributed to its decline. At the same time, the increase in the share of short-term liabilities, primarily the balances of funds in the savings accounts of the population, while increasing long-term assets, contributed to the increase in vulnerability. According to our estimates, the increasein the key rate of the Bank of Russia will have a moderate negative impact on the net interest income of the banking sector. To limit sensitivity to interest rate risk in the future, banks first of all need to increase the share of long-term funding, including bonds. And lending at floating rates should be treated with great caution, remembering that shifting interest rate risk to the borrower leads to an increase in credit risks. It is important to assess the financial situation of borrowers inthe sense of raising rates. In this regard, we are particularly concerned about the initiative to develop lending at floating rates to citizens. Many of them are already initially characterized by a high debt burden. It is also important that citizens may simply not be fully aware ofthe risk that they take on by agreeing to floating rates. The Bank of Russia is working on a bill, aimed at protecting the interests of citizens in the case of lending at floating rates. The third vulnerability, which is significant in the short term,is linked to the continued dependence of the Russian financial market on external financing. On the one hand, the absolute size of non-residents' investments in the Russian public debt is relatively stable, and the share of non-residents has decreased significantly: from a maximumnominal value of 34.9% as of March 1, 2020 to 18.9% as of May 20, 2021 (according to NSD operational data). First of all, this was due to large purchases of OFZ by Russian banks last year. On the other hand, In April, the US Treasury Announced its budgetfor the purchase of new ofZ issues, which once again reminds us that we need to remain prepared for increased geopolitical risks. Note that, according to our estimates, in the event of a tightening of sanctions, their negative impact is likely to beratto-term and rather limited. This is due, firstly, to the fact that Russia is characterized by strong fundamental indicators: low public debt relative to GDP, a significant amount of gold and foreign exchange reserves in relation to external debt. omics. Secondly, Russian investors still have sufficient potential for the growth of investments in public debt. So, as of April 1, the Russian banking sector owned OFZs worth 8.1 trillion rubles, which is 7.5% of the sector's assets. If we assume that by the end of the year banks will buy out the entire planned volume of placement of the Ministry of Finance of Russia, then this figure will grow by only 1.8 percentage points, to 9.3%, which is also a moderate level. Finally, the entire amount of public debt in the hands of foreigners is less than the volumes to which theMinistry of Finance placed a year ago. Now let's move on to the risks of medium- and long-term periods. I will start with the risks of citizens' investments in foreign securities. This vulnerability is not yet significant, it has just begun to form. Household investments in securitiesduring 2020 and the first quarter of 2021 increased by more than 600 billion rubles. So far, the absolute volume of investments is low: the share of investments in non-resident shares in the total volume of household investments in shares is 16%, the similar figure for entitiesis about 24%. People buy foreign securities in order to increase the diversification of their investments, and this is generally part of the process of market development. However, this trend carries risks, both at the micro and macro levels. Among the risks, first of all, it is worthnoting the risk of high expectations of return on investments, especially for investors who have recently entered the market. This can lead to disappointment in investments as in foreign ones. and in Russian assets. At the macro level, the risks are similar to the risks of currencyization of deposits. Note that so far these risks are low, since in 2020 we observed a flow of citizens' funds into foreign shares mainly due to a reduction in foreign currency deposits, despite the fact that the overall level of currencyization of savings remained unchanged at 22%. including by providing tax benefits for IIS. One of the consequences of the increased interest of citizens in the stock market is the growing systemic importance of non-credit financial institutions, primarily brokers. In these conditions, the Bank of Russia plans to introduce short-term liquidity and capital adequacy ratiosand switch to new requirements for the financial stability of insurance companies. Finally, another, fifth vulnerability, which is certainly one of the most important in the medium and long term, is related to climate change. Sincethe day of the year, the world's focus on the climate agenda has increased dramatically. Countries, companies and investors are stepping up their efforts to transition to a low-carbon economy, setting targets to achieve carbon neutrality. The EU is preparing to introduce a transboundarycarbon tax, investors are redistributing portfolios in favor of "green" assets. These trends create risks for countries with a high share of the oil and gas sector, metallurgy and other industries with a high carbon footprint. A stress test of the impactof the introduction of a coal tax on exports from Russia, conducted by the Bank of Russia, shows that most exporters after its introduction will maintain an acceptable financial position and the potential losses of banks as a result of increased reserves will be insignificant. At the same time, it should be noted that the stress test used rather soft prerequisites - in particular, the amount of the tax was taken into account at the level of 30 euros per ton of CO2 emissions. A moderate assessment of the short-term impact of the tax in this amount should not create false confidence - after all, if taxes do not lead to a change in the policy of exporters in terms of reducing emissions, then they will continue to rise. In addition to the risk of higher taxes, from the point of view of financial stability, one of the most important risks is already achange in the strategies of global investors, who massively announce the refusal to invest in "brown" assets (primarily coal) and limit the financing of the oil and gas sector. This can lead to difficulties in refinancing external debt companies to sensitive sectors and reorient them to the domestic financial market. The dependence of such companies on external financing is not very high now, however, such risks can be quite significant. The growth of borrowing by high-emission sectors from the Russian financial sector, in turn, may increase the so-called transition risks for the financial sector itself. In the longer term, climate risks for Russia are associated with a changein the structure of environmental policy, a decrease in demand for non-renewable energy sources, and the inaccessibility of conventional technological solutions and equipment. All of this points to the fact that, despite good stress test results, financial institutions should take climaterisks into account in their activities and help borrowers carry out the "green" transformation of their business. We plan to prepare recommendations for banks to take into account climate risks. It is also necessary to develop markets for "green" investments and carbonwaste. Summing up, I will once again note the change in the risk profile recently. They are increasingly associated with the formation of bubbles and the accumulation of vulnerabilities against the background of economic recovery and the preservation of soft policies in the largest economies. The Bank of Russia isclosely monitoring the situation, we have at our disposal a sufficient set of tools to control risks, and we are ready to apply them in a timely manner to maintain financial stability.

Title: Governor of the Bank of Russia spoke at a meeting of the Board of the Ministry of Finance of the Russian Federation
text: Governor of the Bank of Russia Elvira Nabiullina spoke at the meeting Board of the Ministry of Finance of the Russian Federation January 22, 2016 Performance Good afternoon, dear colleagues! The most important thing is macroeconomic stability, this is the number one priority. But it is necessary to have a positive agenda of measures that will create conditions for economic growth in the new conditions, we already recognize them as a new reality. Of course, there should be such a positive agenda in the financial market and finance. There are a lot of overlapping tasks between the government, the Ministry of Finance and the Central Bank as a mega-regulator. I welcome the fact that we are discussing this now. But I would liketo note that this positive agenda, structural measures should not be to the detriment, but on the basis of macroeconomic stability. Now the current situation poses a common challenge to both fiscal and monetary policy. This challenge is to maintainmacroeconomic stability in the face of a sharp deterioration in the markets for Russian exports. What is macroeconomic stability? These are low deficits, low debt and low inflation. Only on this basis can we talk about structural changesthat will create conditions for economic growth. In many ways, our ability to maintain macroeconomic stability in adverse external conditions is a test of maturity and of what will create conditions for economic growth. In many ways, our ability to maintain macroeconomic stability in unfavorable external conditions is a test of maturity and of what that we are able to make difficult but correct decisions in difficult conditions. This will allow us to maintain the confidence of both business and the population in our policy, in our budget policy. I must say that the Ministry of Finance has always followed this principle in recent years, and the result of these initiatives was that in previousyears a safety cushion was created - the Reserve Fund and the National Welfare Fund. It is important to preserve all these gains. I understand that there is a very difficult task - while maintaining control over the budget deficit, to ensure the optimization of the structure of races. budget moves. This optimization of the expenditure structure should be linked to prioritizing those expenditures that yield the greatest return on economic growth. I must say that monetary and fiscal policy are interrelated. Ifthere is an unbalanced budget and an uncontrolled growth of public debt, this will lead to an increase in long-term interest rates and inflation expectations. Under such conditions, it will be more difficult for the Central Bank to keep inflation under control,the conditions for private investment will worsen. With the same factors, at the same fundamental values, the pressure on the exchange rate will increase. By the way, I would like to say a few words about the situation in the foreign exchange market. We see that since the beginning of the year there has been a surge in volatility in the world markets, and in the Russian market in the past few days the growth of volatility has increased. I would like to say that the Bank of Russia is closely monitoring the situation on the market. We are monitoring the indicators of both realized and expected volatility. We strive to prevent their excessive growth, not due to fundamental factors, and those related to the situation with foreign exchange liquidity and other violations in the work of the market. And we have the whole set of tools to actproactively and prevent threats to financial stability in advance. Of course, everyone is interested in what will happen next. The reason for the volatility in the global and Russian markets are investors' concerns about the situation in China and For our economy, the situation on the oil market is the main factor. Here Anton Germanovich correctly said: there may be a rebound in oil prices, but it is impossible to expect that oil prices will return to the high level that was several years ago. But there are positive moments in this regard. The growth of the share of oil exports in total Russian merchandise exports has already decreased from 67% in December 2013 to 48% in December 2015. The dependence of the economy and the ruble exchange rate on oil is decreasing. And finally, we need all the efforts, structural measures, in order to influence the diversification of the economy and further reduce this dependence on oil prices. In conclusion, I would like to say that the coordinated actions of the Central Bank and the Ministry of Finance in 2015 made it possible to keep the situationunder control. The economy began to adapt to the fall in oil prices, inflation began to slow down, the volatility of the exchange rate became lower than the volatility of oil. Acting in concert, we will be able to overcome the challenges. And once again I will return to the initial formulation of the question: it seems to me very right that we are concentrating not only on purely monetary and fiscal policy, but also on such transformations that will give us the conditions for economic growth. Thank you.

Title: Statement following the meeting of the Board of Directors of the Bank of Russia
text: Statement by Elvira Nabiullina, Governor of the Bank of Russia, following the meeting of the Board of Directors of the Bank of Russia on February 28 , 2022 February 28, 2022 Good afternoon! The Bank of Russia today decided to raise the key rate to 20% per annum. Conditions for the Russian economy have changed dramatically. New foreign sanctions have led to a significant change in the exchange rate of the ruble, limited the ability of us to use gold and foreign exchange reserves. This requires us to use a wide range of tools to maintain financial stability. The dynamics of the exchange rate is an additional proinflationary factor. It both affects the current prices of goods, and leads to a sharp increase in devaluation and inflation expectations. To maintain the attractiveness of deposits and protect citizens' savings from depreciation, it is necessary to raise interest rates to thelevels that compensate citizens for increased inflation risks. Further decisions on monetary policy will be made on the basis of changes in the actual situation, risk assessment, primarily in terms of external conditions. Monetary policywill be aimed at maintaining financial and price stability. Now about the other measures that we are implementing now. Our financial system and economy are now facing a completely non-standard situation, and the Bank of Russia will be very flexible in using any necessary tools. In terms of liquidity of the banking sector. The Bank of Russia continuously provides banks with cash and non-cash liquidity in rubles. Due to the high demand for cash, the banking sector has moved intoa liquidity deficit. Banks have sufficient collateral to increase the volume of liquidity from the Bank of Russia if necessary. In terms of the foreign exchange market. On Thursday and Friday, the Bank of Russia conducted currencyinterventions and: on Thursday - in the amount of 1 billion US dollars and in a smaller volume - on Friday. Due to restrictions on the use of gold and foreign exchange reserves in dollars and euros, we did not intervene today. The government announced a decision to introduce a mandatory sale of 80% of export earnings. This measure will ensure an even supply of foreign currency in the domestic foreign exchange market to meet the needs of importers and citizens. At the same time, we are implementing a number of steps aimed at limiting the export tothe capital by non-residents. We constantly monitor exchange trades and, if necessary, take action. In particular, restrictions have already been imposed on the sale of securities by non-residents. We are in constant contact with banks and are ready to quickly take the necessarymeasures to support them. For example, a number of regulatory relaxations have been adopted, and we will continue to monitor the needs of banks for mechanisms that make it easier for them to work in the new conditions. We gave banks the right not to revalue their investments in securities, as well as grossassets and liabilities, in order to calculate the standards, which will give them the opportunity to gradually adapt to the changed situation. We will not apply measures for non-compliance with the limits of open foreign exchange positions to banks against which foreign sanctions have been imposed . We have taken a number of measures to allow banks not to increase reserves during the year. As part of a countercyclical macroprudential policy, we have dissolved the accumulated buffers for all types of loans: both foreign currency loans to companies and loans to citizens. These measures are equivalent to an increase in the capital of banks by 900 billion rubles. It is very important in the current situation to support not only banks, but also their customers. Citizens and companies are also facing a deterioration in their financial situation as a result ofthe imposed sanctions on borders. In this regard, we recommend that banks meet customers halfway: to restructure loans, not to impose penalties and fines on such loans. This applies to loans to both citizens and businesses. At the same time, banks can not worsen the assessment of the financialsituation of borrowers and the quality of debt service. In the context of the growth of the key rate, payments on loans with floating rates increase. In retail, there are practically no such loans: there are no mortgages at all, in consumer lending is minimal. And I would like to emphasize that for existing loans issued at fixed rates, banks cannot change the conditions. If there are no floating rates in retail, then in corporate lending, banks in recent years have actively increased the share of such loans to limit their interest rate risk. Nevertheless, we assess the risk of a possible transformation of interest rate risk into a credit risk as limited: as a rule, borrowers on such loans are large companies with high creditworthiness. If the borrower isexperiencing difficulties with a floating rate loan and the bank is ready to restructure such a loan, we are also ready to provide regulatory relief on reserves. In the current situation, it is important to preserve lending opportunities for both citizens and businesses. Bankstraditionally become conservative in a crisis and slow down lending. Therefore, we have already provided banks with flexibility, temporarily suspending the restriction on the full cost of consumer credit. Also, the Bank of Russia will soon correctmacroprudential premiums on unsecured loans and mortgages, leaving allowances only for the most risky loans: with the highest level of PSK, with a high debt burden, and in a mortgage - with a high I_T?. For the remaining loans , surcharges are planned to be canceled to support the availability of credit. All banks fulfill and will continue to fulfill all obligations to their customers. All funds on the accounts are saved, all operations are available to customers. We have introduced regulatory relaxations for insurance companies, professional market participants. We will also consider other relaxations to ensure the fulfillment of all obligations to customers. We have developed an internal financial infrastructure, so it willwork smoothly. So, we have a Financial Messaging System (SPFS), which can replace 5?IET within the country, it can be joined by participants from abroad. The national payment card system processes all domestic traffic. by payment cards. Cards of international payment systems issued by banks that have fallen under sanctions will continue to work within the country as usual. The Bank of Russia will take all necessary measures to protect financial and price stability, supportthe Russian financial sector and protect the well-being of citizens and the economy as a whole. Thank you!

Title: Statement following the meeting of the Board of Directors of the Bank of Russia
text: Statement by Elvira Nabiullina, Governor of the Bank of Russia, following the meeting of the Board of Directors of the Bank of Russia on March 18 , 2022 March 18, 2022 Performance Hello. Today we decided to keep the key rate at 20% per annum. At the end of February, we raised the key rate primarily in order to counteract the risks to the financialsituation in the face of new unprecedented sanctions. Other stabilization measures were taken. What do we have today? The banking system is working without failures, the liquidity situation has stabilized. We provide banks with the necessary funds in full . Volume. At the peak, the volume of liquidity provided reached 10 trillion rubles. The structural liquidity deficit of 7 trillion rubles that arose in early March has now been more than halved. At the end of February, banks experienced a large-scale outflow offunds from the accounts of the population, but in the last two weeks this money is returned to term deposits. The rate increase played a key role in this. As for lending, its growth has continued in recent weeks, but, most likely, this is due tothe use of previously approved credit limits. In the future, we expect a weakening of credit activity. I would like to note that such an increase in rates is a temporary anti-crisis measure. When the situation stabilizes sufficiently, rates will decrease. Now about what is happening now with the economy and inflation. The acceleration of inflation in late February - early March was caused by a rush demand, primarily in the non-food segment. People actively bought household appliances, cars, electronics, furniture, fearing thatthe range and availability of these goods will be greatly reduced due to the sanctions imposed, the withdrawal of some foreign companies from the market and the weakening of the ruble. In the second week of March, the consumer rush slightly decreased. Another segment where thereis a high consumer activity is long-term storage products: cereals, flour, pasta, sugar. Most of these goods are produced in Russia, from domestic raw materials. There are enough stocks of these products, and their production continues. Asthe rush demand cools, their price dynamics normalize, the prices of individual goods may even decrease. Further dynamics of inflation will depend on the speed of adaptation of the economy to new conditions. Today, almost all companies are faced with interruptions in production and logistics chains, in settlements with foreign counterparties. We receive this information from our divisions in the regions. At the same time, there is domestic demand, the need for goods remains. In the context of reduced imports and the closure of part of foreign markets, this demand will be redirected to Russian products. In the current situation, it is extremely important to restore supply as soon as possible. Companies have already begun to start Looking for new opportunities: new markets, new suppliers of equipment, technicalnogues, components for production. And if earlier the production of certain goods was unprofitable within the country, now it becomes more interesting for business. This is how the economy adapts to changing conditions. And this is inevitably accompanied by a change in relative prices in the economy and a temporary increase in inflation. At the same time, it is important not to introduce manual price regulation. Their artificial containment will inevitably lead to a shortage and a decrease in product quality. I would like to emphasize that administrative measuresto regulate prices will slow down the rate of adaptation of the economy to new conditions. At the same time, it is important to prevent the abuse of companies' dominant position in the market, cartel agreements. Adjustment of relative prices cannot happen at once. This means thatat some point inflation will remain elevated, but we will not allow the inflationary spiral to unwind. Specific figures of the forecast are now very difficult to name. Inflation this year and most likely next year will be higher than previous estimates. GDP will decline in the coming quarters. We plan to present a new macroeconomic forecast at a reference meeting in April. The key uncertainty is the external terms of trade with increased sanctions pressure. The restrictions imposed affected a significant part ofexports and imports. In addition to official sanctions, the decisions of foreign companies to suspend work in our market can also have a serious impact on the situation. To smooth out the adjustment of the economy will be the availability of stocks and materials of components accumulated by companies. Now they support the current activities of enterprises. The ability of companies to replenish these reserves, including replacing retired imports with Russian analogues, will determine the timing of adaptation of the economy. What measures have we taken to stabilize the situation and what more do we plan to take? First, elements of capital controls were introduced. This was a forced decision in the face of the limited capacity of the Central Bank to dispose of international reserves. Mandatory sale of foreign exchange earnings and a number of other measures ensure the necessary inflow of currency into the domestic market for foreign trade operations. Secondly, we have adopted a wide range of anti-crisis measures to support the financial sector. In recent years, we have worked hard both to increase the autonomy of the internal financial infrastructure and to strengthen the stability of the banking system. As a result, the payment infrastructure in Russia, even in the face of restrictions, ensures the continuity of payments. And banks have the opportunity to meet customers, those companies and citizens who are in a difficult situation, restructuring their loans. Thirdly, as for the real sector, we are working together with the Government to support lending to companies. An additional500 billion rubles have been allocated to programs to stimulate lending to small and medium-sized businesses. This will enable small and medium-sized businesses to obtain working capital loans for up to one year, as well as investment loans for up to three years. In addition, we are now working with the Government and banks on measures to mitigate the consequences of a sharp change in the conditions for servicing loans at a floating rate for companies. We have suspended trading on the Moscow Exchange to avoid sharp fluctuations in the value of securities at the time of an unprecedented change in the economic situation. We are now ready to gradually resume them. On Monday, the Federal Loan Bonds will open in the stock section of the Moscow Exchange. In order to preventexcessive volatility and ensure balanced liquidity in this segment during the resumption of trading, the Bank of Russia will make purchases of OFZs. They Will be carried out in the amounts necessary to prevent risks to the financial stability. After the financial markets stabilize, we plan to fully sell this bond portfolio in order to neutralize the impact of this operation on monetary policy. Now about the prospects for monetary policy. When making decisions, we will take into account the need for large-scale structural adjustment of the economy. We will conduct monetary policy in such a way as to allow time for the economy to adapt to the new external conditions, but taking into account the need to return inflation to the target in 2024. The support measures taken by the Bank of Russia and the Government will help Russian companies and citizens to go through this difficult period. Thank you.

Title: Speech at the XV International Banking Forum
text: Speech by the Governor of the Bank Russia Elvira Nabiullina at the XV International Banking Forum September 14, 2017 Performance Good afternoon! I am pleased to welcome all the participants of the forum. These autumn meetings in Sochi have already become traditional, although this year there are important events in the life of the Association, and Anatoly Gennadyevich [Aksakov has already said this. Yesterday, at an extraordinary meeting of the Association, you decided that the Association will expand the range of its activities - both regional and major federal banks will be represented. This is a very important step not only for the Association itself, but also for the development of bankingsectors. And in our opinion, it is very important that market participants - conscientious, whose goal is the long-term successful development of their business in competitive conditions - decide that the Association will become a platform for dialogue between majorand small banks, helping to find a balance of interests of different players, as well as to be an effective platform for interaction between the bank and the regulator. This should be a positive factor for the development of competition in the banking sector. In my remarks today, I would like to focus on three points. The first is our assessment of the current state of the banking sector and the conclusions that we can all draw from the events of recent months in the banking market. The second is the development of competitionin the banking sector as well. And the third is that against the background of your decision to develop the Rossiya Association, I would like to raise the question of the prospects for strengthening the role of banking associations. I will start with the current dynamics of the banking sector. The main indicators of activitiesand banks show growth. For eight months of this year, the assets of the banking sector increased by 4.5%; loans to the economy - by 3.5%; loans to non-financial organizations - by 2.3%. Loans to individuals increased by 7.0%. And in general, we can confidently talk about the restoration of retail lending while stabilizing its quality against the background of the transition of banks to the use of more conservative scoring models. And the Bank. Russia will continue to pay increased attention to this segment. In general, I must say that it was possible to stabilize the quality of the loan portfolio. At the same time, the share of overdue debt for corporate loans increased slightly (within 0.1%), for retail loans it decreased slightly. The changes are very small, and, rather, we can talk here about the stabilization of overdue debt. Deposits of the population continue to grow and for eight months increased by 5.0%, to almost 25 trillion rubles; more modest - by 0.9% - was the increase in deposits and funds of organizations in the accounts. For thebanking sector, the share of household deposits in banks' liabilities has exceeded the share of corporate funding. For a long time, the trend was reversed. Profit growth continued. The eight-month profit of RUB 997 billion has already exceeded the 2016 financial result. Profit is a source of capital growth. And we believe that this is how it should be used first. Now I will move on, probably, to the hottest topic - the events of this year. In the middle of the year, we decided tointroduce an interim administration, and then revoke the license from UGRA Bank. This case is one of the extremely unpleasant in a series of reviews due to the irresponsible behavior of the owners, who created a "pocket" bank to finance primarily theirown projects, but at the same time actively, in the case of UGRA, extremely aggressively, bypassed the regulator's restrictions, attracting depositors' funds. The loan portfolio was of poor quality, and most of the collateral was issued with signs of overestimation of the costof the bridge. The rescue plan proposed by the owners did not meet the requirements of the law. Moreover, it implied long-term (ten-year) subsidization by the state, in fact, of business projects of a group of individuals in certain sectors. And the revocation of the license was a logical result of the actions of the owners and management of the bank. I very much hope that the banks present here understand that the risks to the business of owners and management should be strictly limited and not try to deceive the regulator throughsecret ownership schemes and informal agreements. The banking business should be banking, not investment. If the owners of banks want to engage in a different business, let them finance it not from the funds of depositors of their own banks, otherwise we get anasymmetric distribution of tops and stubs: if the business is successful, the owners get richer, and if not, then the DIA must pay insurance compensation to depositors. This approach, of course, is unacceptable for us. Now about the biggest event of the summer - the financialrehabilitation of the Otkritie Bank group. The question is often asked: why was the license revoked from UGRA, and Otkritie was sanitized? First. UGRA is not a systemically important bank, but Otkritie is. It is one of the largest banks in the country. UGRA isnot practically integrated into the financial system, its ties with other financial institutions are weak, while the situation in Otkritie affects many banks, and not only banks - pension funds, insurance organizations. And the second thing. UGRA has not beencovered with a business model, as I have already said, which even with additional capitalization could become viable. This is a model for attracting funds mainly from the population and financing business projects related to the owner. With all the flaws and riskiness of the Otkritie business model, it can be "cured", "repaired" and developed. Nevertheless, business miscalculations in Otkritie led to the fact that the bank could no longer maintain financial stability on its own. And the Central Bank was forcedto intervene. At the end of August, we decided to restore the financial stability of Otkritie, for the first time we used a new mechanism for financial recovery - direct entry into the bank's capital of the Banking Sector Consolidation Fund. This mechanism allows us to solve problems even in large banks without creating risks to financial stability. Now we can state that the negative effect of the reorganization of Otkritie Bank on the financial system was minimal: there is no outflow of deposits from other banks , there is a slight increase in bond yields - by 100-150 basis points. But it has no systemic risks, and the stock market practically did not react to this event. Thus, the escalation of the problems of one bank into a systemic problemwas avoided, but from this story, of course, it is necessary to draw conclusions and change the policy in such a way as to minimize the likelihood of a repetition of such cases in the future. What caused the problems in the bank? I would like to say this again,because it is important that we all learn lessons together. The root cause was too risky, based on constant expansion and large-scale risky operations, business model. At the same time, the bank did not pay enough attention to managingtransactions. I note that three years ago, before the bank became a sanatorium of TRUST Bank. its position roughly corresponded to that of many other large banks. The reorganization of trust was a serious, complex project, but if it was the only such complex and risky project in the bank, the bank would probably be able to carry it out. However, further expansion and a large number of other risky transactions made the bank vulnerable to risks and ultimately led to such serious problems thatthe Bank of Russia had to intervene in the situation. Among the risky projects, of course, I note the purchase of Rosgosstrakh, which was almost forced, because the bank by that time was already a major creditor of this insurer. In its actions, the bank often focused onshort-term benefits without understanding the long-term consequences of its actions. This behavior was also noticeable in the well-known discussed transaction for the acquisition of Rizzia-30 Eurobonds to participate in currency repo auctions with the Bank of Russia. In general, this operation did not lead to a deterioration in the financial performance of Otkritie, and, having seenthe oncentering of such securities on the balance sheet of one participant, we lowered the limits in 2015 and raised rates. But what is worrying and what should be a lesson for the entire banking sector: on the balance sheet of Otkritie, these securities were at an inflated price, which made it possibleto embellish the financial condition of the bank. There was a certain manipulation of the market price. Of course, we understand that our bond market is not deep enough, such opportunities remain for individual market players - conducting several transactions on the stock exchange and showing that it seems to be a market transaction. But for us, as a regulator, it is important that they do not lead to an understatement of capital. Therefore, as part of the work to increase risk control, which I will talk about in more detail now. In cases wherealmost the full amount of a security is concentrated on the balance sheet of a bank with a concentration - this creates additional risks, we may require the creation of additional reserves. I ask banks to take this into account in their actions. The bank carried out many operations solely for opportunisticreasons, without making a full-fledged risk analysis, which, of course, led to these sad results. The process of recovery of Otkritie, as we have already said, will take several months, after which the bank will be recapitalized, the financial groupand Otkritie will agree with the Central Bank on the strategy of sustainable growth of the group's companies. Although the Chairman of the Board will be appointed only at the end of the work of the interim administration of the Management Company of the Banking Sector Consolidation Fund, I would like to announce today that both customers and counterparties of the bank have greater certainty, greater understanding that Mikhail Mikhailovich Zadornov, who is present here, agreed to take this position in the bank at our invitation. And there is a question that weoften hear: does the new model of reorganization carry the risks of nationalization of the banking sector? No, it does not. We plan to quickly put in order the financial institutions that receive funds from the Bank Consolidation Fund, and, if necessary, restructuresuch banks, including merging and bringing them to the market, not necessarily by finding a strategic investor. and by selling in parts, not at random or by conducting IRO. On the contrary, our task is to ensure that healthy and successful private banks with a viable and profitable business model operate in the Russian market. From the topic of risks assumed by a particular bank, Otkritie, which eventually ended up withthe nation, I would like to move on to the issue of risk management in banks as a whole. This is an issue that we plan to solve systematically. By November 1 of this year, all banks with assets above 500 billion rubles must submit to the Central Bank special reports on risk management systems and procedures for assessing capital adequacy. By the end of this year, the Bank of Russia will conduct a full assessment of the quality of risk management systems and capital adequacy assessment of the largest credit institutions. The Bank of Russia will also assessthe quality of corporate assessments, how they manage risks and how they plan capital, the amount of capital that would allow banks to cover all accepted and potential risks, the amount of which should be determined taking into account stress testing. If we determinethat the amount of the bank's available capital is insufficient to cover the risks assumed or the level and quality of risk management procedures is insufficient and in the future the bank may face a shortage of capital, then individualincreased capital adequacy requirements will be established for such organizations. This is a fundamentally new approach to supervisory actions for our system. That is, the Central Bank will analyze not only the individual transactions made and the decisions of the management of banks, but willcomprehensively assess the quality of risk management and internal control in banks. Supervisory requirements will be imposed not after the fact (after the inspection of actual violations, for example, reserve requirements), but preventively - if the Central Bank states a low quality of risk management in a credit institution. The Bank of Russia may also apply other serious supervisory response measures, such as restricting and prohibiting the implementation of certain operations in case of violationof individually established increased standards by a credit organization. This year, we are starting such supervisory work with the largest banks, as I have already said, those with assets of more than 500 billion rubles, but all other credit institutions will be subjected to such an assessmentnext year (2018). What I said is about continuing our work to improve oversight and regulation that we are doing. But there is another side of the problem - supervision should not and will not replace the management and owners of the bank and should not make decisions on specific operations and be responsible for them. We believe that in this regard, it makes sense to consider the issue of material incentives to reduce the level of risk-taking by bank managers, namely, thatthe regulator could postpone the payment of bonuses and dividends in those banks that experience problems, until such problems are corrected. After all, if the activities of managers lead to the fact that the bank leaves the market or is sanitized using the state. It is unlikely that the work of the management of this bank can be recognized as effective and worthy of bonuses. By the way, as for Otkritie specifically, we plan to challenge in court the payment of bonuses by managers to themselves for the first half of 2017. The decision to issueincreased bonuses and dividends a month and a half before the revocation of the license or reorganization can be interpreted, among other things, as a withdrawal of assets. Therefore, we believe that the restriction on the payment of bonuses and dividends in problem banks is justified, and we considerit entirely appropriate to raise this question. Now to the second topic - one of the key topics for us - about the development of competition in the financial market. Competitive environment is a necessary condition for effective functioning and development. Ofcourse, we will work closely together to compete in the financial market. Of course, we will work closely together. and we are already cooperating with the Federal Antimonopoly Service in this area. I believe that the Association can make its contribution in this area, especially since the Association has always raised the issue of developing competition very loudly. We are focused on creating a stable and transparent competitive environment. And that means fair pricing, distributive efficiencyof markets, and the protection and satisfaction of financial institution customers and investors. I would like to share with you some of the findings of the empirical study of competition in the banking sector that we conducted. And a pronounced trend in our countryis the geographical concentration of the head offices of credit institutions not even in million-plus cities, but exclusively in Moscow. The share of Russian banks with head offices in Moscow exceeds 50%. There is no other comparable financial center in the country - even in St. Petersburg it is less than 5%. Despite the fact that in the Moscow region the quantitative indicators of competition are at an acceptable level, the quality of competition is not as high as it would seem. With a large number of banks operating inthe Moscow region, only two players have real market power. All this testifies to the fact that even the Moscow market requires attention and measures aimed at improving the competitive environment. Competition is not measured only by the number of players in a particular market. At the same time, we see a number of "desert regions", mainly depressed regions, where there are very few banks and bank offices. But there are, of course, regions (there are few of them) with a developed competitive environment. We are on this land, and I wantto use the example of the Krasnodar Territory. With a sufficiently large number of banks, both federal and regional, market players in the region are comparable in terms of market power, which provides the consumer with a wide range of opportunities for thedevelopment of certain financial instruments. This, in turn, should provide more comfortable conditions for the development of small and medium-sized businesses. which is one of the priorities for the development of the banking sector. Another conclusion that we can draw from the empirical material of the study: the policy of cleaning up the banking sector does not lead to a decrease in competition. The withdrawal of weak and unscrupulous players from the market leads to the fact that the number of market participants who have market power increases. This also leads to the elimination of those business models with which law-abiding business is not able to compete, which creates the prerequisites in general for attracting high-quality capital to the banking sector. What measures are we taking and consider it necessary to take further to develop competition in the banking sector? First and foremost. Completion of the process of cleaning the banking system and increasing the effectiveness of supervision, including the development of behavioral supervision. Behavioral supervision is, in a sense, a novelty in the central bank's activities. It is aimed at creating conditions in which financial market participants are forced to provide the consumer with comprehensive information - namely, they are forced to provide comprehensive information - about the product being purchased, on the one hand, and offer the consumer the products that he really needs. Not to impose on him what creates risks for consumers. Behavioral supervision is designed to not only to increase customer satisfactionin the financial sector, but also to help the consumer make the right competitive choice in favor of the best offer. The second direction is proportional regulation of the banking system, its own niche for players with different business models and with differentscales of business. Examples of individual regions eloquently indicate that in an effective competitive environment, players of different types, different sizes find their market niches, and ultimately the saturation of the regional economy with financial resources is improving in general. Ursami. We consider proportional regulation to be one of the key factors in stimulating and lending to small and medium-sized businesses. We expect that this category of customers will have expanded access to financial resources, and banking products willbe more adapted to the needs of entrepreneurs, primarily small and medium-sized businesses. A few words about how ready banks are for the transition to a new type of license. We believe that the transition to proportional regulation should be and will besmooth, and this is what the law orients us to. As of September 1, 222 credit institutions had a capital of less than 1 billion rubles. At the same time, almost all of these banks have a volume of operations. Not provided for by law for banks with a basic license, does not exceed10% of assets and only eight banks account for more than 30% of assets for such operations. That is, the transition to proportional regulation will not be associated with a breakdown in the business models of banks. According to our estimates, the capital of the main part of banks that can be transferredto the category of banks with a basic license is in the range of 300-500 million rubles (more than 60% of banks with a capital of less than 1 billion rubles). 13.5% of banks with a capital of less than 1 billion rubles have this figure exceeding 700 million rubles. This means that these banks will be able to choose a strategy to increase capital to the level of a universal license. The third factor of competition is digital technologies. This is also a factor of increasing financial inclusion, reducing the cost of processing information and saleschannels, improving customer satisfaction and entering new markets. Digitalization is a powerful trend, we can now see it perfectly. This is a trend that will only increase, making the Russian financial market more and more extraterritorial and, therefore, competitive. tnym. Market advantages will be received primarily by banks with developed technological platforms and business models, which will be focused on the use of elements of artificial intelligence, a high degree of robotization in business processes, on remote servicing of their customers in the mode of minimal response time. Conversely, banks that are "late" in the digital revolution risk losing customers and, as a result, income. I will not dwell on the issues in detail, In October, we will be able to see each other again here in Sochi at the Eiporoiz forum to talk in detail about new technologies in the financial sector, about their advantages and about the risks that need to be managed. The fourth directionof the development of competition is the standardization of products, the introduction of cooling periods so that the client, the consumer can come to his senses, the development of financial consulting mechanisms, including those based on modern information technologies, as well as ensuring financial inclusion, when consumers can compare different products and choose the right one. And another private, but important issue that was raised at almost all of our meetings is the competition of banks for the placement of funds of statecompanies and state corporations. Taking into account the fact that the rating industry is completing its formation, we believe that in the near future it is worth translating into practice the use of credit ratings as a sufficient cry. Access to liquidity, abandoning the criterion of the size of the bank. Now we are discussing with the Ministry of Finance the timing of such a transition, and, in our opinion, of course, we have always said that the size of the bank is not a criterion for its reliability, so we must move on to the criteria that will really describe the reliability of banks. And the last, third topic, which I would like to briefly dwell on, is the role of banking associations in the development of the financial industry. This issue is closely relatedto the development of competition in the financial market, because without the market forming a demand for fair competition and actively participating in clearing the environment of unscrupulous practices, the quality of competition simply cannot improve. We reallylook with optimism at what steps the Association is taking towards its own institutional development. Now in the banking sector, unlike other sectors of the financial market, there is no practice of self-regulation. We have to consider the prospects for its development and implementation. But nevertheless, we already see that the Association is ready to take on more functions in its activities. In particular, we see serious potential for the development of relations between the Bank of Russia and banking associations. Whatare we talking about? 1. We see that associations could combine the efforts of participants, different participants of different sizes, to share costs in achieving certain goals. when implementing projects that may be costly for one participant. It'sbuilding information databases, training staff, marketing, compliance -- "know your customer" -- procedures, cloud computing, reporting. And of course, associations could play a big role in that. 2. Assessing the regulatory impact ofRussia's financial market regulatory initiatives. We're interested in that. We're in constant contact. we post all our draft documents on the website, receive comments, discuss, but, of course, a more formalized assessment of the regulatory impact of our initiatives - we only welcome it. And as in the implementation phase of these initiatives, also we are interested in having an objective assessment by the banking industry We consider this important for the development of the competitive environment and the overall effectiveness of banking regulation and our interaction. 3. The third is, of course, the generalization of the best practices that exist in the activities of banks, the exchange of them and recommendations for the implementationof the comments among their members. And we expect that the Association will commit itself to the formation of standards of activity in the banking sector, which is done by self-regulatory organizations. This work has already begun, it cannot but rejoice us, and weagree that it will be continued. In conclusion, I would like to once again congratulate the Association on the choice not only of a new leadership, but also of a new model of development. I have no doubt that this step will contribute to the further development of a healthy, sustainable, transparent banking business. I wish you success in business and productive work at the forum! Thank you!

Title: Statement following the meeting of the Board of Directors of the Bank of Russia
text: Statement by Elvira Nabiullina, Governor of the Bank of Russia, following the Meeting of the Council Directors of the Bank of Russia July 22, 2022 July 22, 2022Note Speech Good afternoon! Today we decided to reduce the key rate by 150 basis points, to 8.00% per annum. Our decision is based on a comprehensive assessment of current conditions and an updated macroeconomic forecast. In May-July, inflation consistently slowed down. This is due to the strengthening of the ruble and the correction of prices for previously risen in price goods. In recent weeks, this slowdown has become broader, which indicates a disinflationary contribution from consumer demand. We have lowered the inflation forecast for the current year to 12.0-15.0%. The forecast for the next year is kept at the level of 5.0-7.0%. Our monetary policy takes into account the need for structural adjustment of the economy and is aimed at returning inflation to the target of 4% in 2024. I will dwell on the factors of decision in more detail. First. Price pressures continue to ease. The decline in prices has continued almost without interruption for nine weeks. And we still believe that the main reason for the decline in inflation is the price correction after the jump in March. Then there was a sharp weakening of the ruble, the costs of companies increased significantly. And the rush demand allowed them to transfer these costs into prices. Now the situation has changed. The ruble strengthened significantly. Producers and trade organizations see that some prices have been raised "with a margin".
