However, the price correction cannot occur in one day, it is stretched in time. And business is groping for a level of them that will be acceptable to buyers and cover rising costs. A significant strengthening of the ruble had an impact on the perception of prices and the attitude of the population to purchases. This is clearly visible in the dynamics of inflation expectations. In July, this figure fell to 10.8% - this is the minimum since March last year. People believe that the current prices of many goods are unreasonably high, and expect them to decrease. Short-term price expectations of enterprises continue to decrease. They returned to the level of the spring of last year. Now about how we see the impact of consumer demand on inflation. In recent months, it has been disinflationary, which, along with the strengthening of the ruble, has provided a faster slowdown in inflation. Currently, the propensity to save is high, although the situation may change. The high savings rate is partly due to the fact that due to external restrictions and the departure of foreign companies, people could not buy what they wanted, and put these funds in reserve. Further dynamics of consumer demand is one of the key forks in our forecast. On the one hand, a high propensity to save may persist. In the face of increased uncertainty, the population tends to save more as a safety cushion. This is a rational behavior that will allow you to feel more confident in case you have to face a shortened working week, forced vacation or problems with employment. In addition, the ongoing decline in prices and the strengthening of the ruble can be perceived as a signal to postpone large purchases now in order to buy cheaper later. On the other hand, we can get a repeat of the pandemic scenario. Then consumers first sharply reduced consumption, and then after the abolition of knockdowns just as quickly restored it. This was observed in Russia and in many other countries. Today's, essentially forced, accumulation of savings is a compressed spring in the economy, which, under certain circumstances, can give a sharp increase in consumption. With restrictions on the supply side of goods and services, this can quickly accelerate "demand" inflation. And some signs of growing consumer interest are already taking shape. I'll name three of them. First, according to surveys, in July, people began to evaluate much higher the favorability of the current moment for making large purchases. Secondly, deposit rates are decreasing, which increases interest in consumption. Thirdly, the reduction in the retail loan portfolio observed in April-May was replaced by its growth. And our monetary policy decisions will also depend on which scenario consumer activity will follow in the future - whether demand will grow faster or slower, how this growth will correlate with the possibilities of expanding output. Second. Incoming data indicate that the economic downturn will be more time-consuming and possibly less profound. If we talk about the current year, the decline in GDP is projected to be less largely due to a more moderate reduction in exports. This is primarily due to the redistribution of oil exports to new markets. At the same time, the dynamics of imports meets our expectations. After a significant decline, this indicator began to recover. Basically, consumer imports are increasing due to the establishment of new supply routes. In terms of intermediate and investment imports, so far there are no clear signs of recovery. Investment activity is constrained not only by difficulties with logistics for the supply of equipment and strong fluctuations in the exchange rate affecting the business plans of companies, but also by the general economic uncertainty in the conditions of structural adjustment, which forces business to be more cautious about the prospects for the implementation of long-term investment projects. The situation in the economy is determined by how companies adapt to changing conditions. This adjustment is very heterogeneous across regions, industries, and even individual companies within the same sector. In general, it can be noted that many companies managed to avoid the rapid depletion of stocks, which could lead to the cessation of production chains. To restore stocks, it is necessary to look for new suppliers within the country and abroad. It takes time. According to our monitoring of enterprises, over the past two months, the situation with reserves has not worsened, but also has not improved, which remains a factor of potential proinflationary risk. This topic is the subject of a sidebar in our latest regional economy report. The restructuring of the economy will be noticeable in the changes in the labor market. For us, this is one of the key indicators of the transformation process. I will give an example of companies that are experiencing sales problems. One group is fully export-oriented companies that worked mainly for European markets. The other group is the manufacturers of individual parts for automakers, furniture factories, assembly lines localized in Russia. household appliances. Due to the disruption of production chains, their products were not in demand. As a result, these companies will have to either change the range or reduce output. At the same time, there are industries where opportunities for import substitution are opening up. And new jobs will be created there. So far, the situation on the labor market is calm, and unemployment remains at historically low levels. Businesses use part-time mechanisms. But as we restructure, we will see increased labor flows between companies and sectors. Taking into account the continuing nature of the processes taking place in the economy, we have revised the GDP forecast. According to our estimates, the economic downturn this year will be less and will be 4.0-6.0%. Next year, for the year as a whole, the GDP indicator will decrease by 1.0-4.0%. The future dynamics is more indicative in the quarterly comparison. We expect that in the fourth quarter of next year, GDP will be 1.0-2.5% higher than in the fourth quarter of this year. Third. Monetary conditions are gradually softening. Interest rates in the credit and deposit market continued to decline, as well as the yields of short- and medium-term OFZs. Credit activity has revived somewhat, although it remains restrained. Mortgages are recovering the fastest, but mainly through preferential programs. Unsecured consumer lending has also begun to grow. Corporate lending is being restored, while foreign currency loans are being replaced by ruble loans. In a situation of increased uncertainty, savings sentiment remains strong. Despite the gradual decrease in profitability on deposits, the funds of the population remain in banks. At the same time, the share of term deposits is decreasing, and current accounts, which are the most liquid part of savings, are growing. And they can be quickly redirected to consumption when sentiment changes. A few words about the balance of payments and the ruble exchange rate. Under the new conditions of sanctions and restrictions on the movement of capital, as well as the absence of a fiscal rule, the exchange rate has become more volatile and is formed mainly by the current account. For monetary policy, this means that inflation under the influence of the exchange rate also becomes more volatile - and, accordingly, interest rates in the economy may become more volatile to maintain inflation on target. If the current account is reduced in accordance with ours The forecast is already from the third quarter and the level of the exchange rate will adapt to this, then its disinflationary effect will be smoothed out. As for the risks to the outlook, we talked about them in detail in the press release. In general, it can be noted that there are three main sources of uncertainty on the forecast horizon. These are external factors (risks from the geopolitical situation and the global recession), fiscal policy and changing propensity to save. The further trajectory of the key rate will depend on how the balance of risks develops for the trajectory we have outlined to achieve the target inflation rate in 2024. In accordance with our updated forecast and taking into account today's decision, the average annual key rate this year will be 10.5-10.8% per annum (this corresponds to the value until the end of the year in the range of 7.4-8.0%), next year - 6.5-8.5% and in 2024 - 6.0-7.0% per annum. The rapidly changing situation, which is characterized by a series of processes that are multidirectional in their impact on inflation and the economy, requires from us greater flexibility in decision-making and greater attention to operational information. QUESTION (??????): I would like to ask a question about the budget rule. I understand that the discussion continues and it is too early to talk about the parameters. But let me ask you to lift the veil on the sterilization of currency under the new budget rule. As for the labour market, I would like to clarify: what are your forecasts for the situation on the labour market for the autumn? E.S. NABIULLINA: As for the budget rule. How it works. Initially, the budget takes rubles from exporters - thus, it withdraws these rubles from the economy. And when currency transactions take place (we, in fact, mirror these operations for the Ministry of Finance), then these rubles are returned to the economy. This is how sterilization occurs. Therefore, yes, currency transactions, if a budget rule is introduced, then, most likely, such currency transactions should be. Alexei Borisovich, if you want, please comment. A.B. ZABOTKIN: Perhaps, I will simply clarify for the sake of clarity that the meaning of the currency part of operations under the budget rule is precisely related to the fact that by buying foreign currency for additional rubles - rubles that are collected in the form of additional revenues - these rubles should be returned to the economy. That is, the operation for the purchase of foreign currency in the budget rule is the operation that neutralizes the effect of the budget rule in terms of the impact on monetary aggregates. Therefore, there is definitely no need to take any additional actions. E.S. NABIULLINA: As for the possible shortage of goods. Yes, of course, certain products have disappeared from our market, brands have disappeared and so on. But we see that substitutes for goods are coming - of course, other brands, other manufacturers, if we talk about consumer goods. This process will continue, but we do not see any systemic problem here now. As for the labor market for the autumn. As I said, the situation is really stable, calm and unemployment is at historically low levels. But, of course, the situation on the labor market will largely be determined by the speed of structural transformation. What do we mean by that. Some enterprises will reduce output, optimize employment. Either new enterprises will appear nearby, or those enterprises that will need new employment, because they will find niches in the domestic market - there will be such a flow of labor. It will, of course, be reflected in unemployment rates in general when people are temporarily looking for work. Therefore, it is very important for us now to look at this situation - not only at the overall indicators, but also at how vacancies behave, what demand there is for labor in other sectors. Here, of course, questions may arise with the fact that it will be necessary to retrain people for new tasks. Government programs are also very important here. Therefore, much will depend on structural adjustment. We do not give any quantitative forecasts on this topic. QUESTION (IA "Tatar-Inform", Kazan) I have two questions for you. First question. During the pandemic, the key rate dropped to 4.25%. The current economic situation is hardly easy. Therefore, we are very interested in what is the red line of reducing the key rate for the Bank of Russia in the current conditions? And the second question. It's no secret that this year there is a good grain harvest. Don't you see the risk of food deflation in the country in the fall? And how will ostep react if this actually happens? E.S. NABIULLINA: As for the decline in food prices in the autumn. It's possible. And a good harvest is a disinflationary factor that will help reduce inflation. But fluctuations in food prices are a common thing in our country. And within the framework of standard seasonality, this is not the factor that affects monetary policy. Because monetary policy reacts to stable factors of inflation, when inflation deviations are due to stable factors and can affect, among other things, inflation expectations, secondary effects. And fluctuations in food prices are still factors that are reflected in the current price level, but these are usually factors of one-time, temporary action. As for the first question. You know, I'd like to start with the following. We do compare the situation to the pandemic in many ways, but in essence they are two different crises. Because the pandemic crisis could be called such a cyclical crisis, when in the beginning there was a demand shock due to a knockdown, because people simply could not consume the way they consumed. And we lowered the rate precisely to push this demand. And demand recovered very quickly, even faster than our expectations, but then supply problems began to appear, and they turned out to be longer-lasting. All these logistics, production chains, their rupture, it had an impact on the fact that demand grew, and the supply of goods did not grow accordingly. And this resulted in an increase in inflation in the second half of 2021 and in the unwinding of inflation expectations. Now , after all, the crisis is structural and has been largely catalyzed by supply shocks. This reduces the potential of the economy. And a rate cut, even a very large one, will not be able to compensate for the effects to the same extent as in 2020. We are therefore looking very carefully at what is happening with consumer demand and how much its dynamics correspond to the dynamics of supply. To compare directly these two episodes, maybe it shouldn't. That being said, you talked about red lines. There are no red lines for us to decide on the rate either from below or from above. The rate will be chosen based on the trajectory that should ensure the return of inflation to the target in 2024. After all, we have such a division on currency, as we hear that there are "friendly" currencies in which citizens can protect themselves from the devaluation of the ruble, for example. And I cannot but ask about the unblocking of foreign securities in the NSD. Is there any news here? E.S. NABIULLINA: Indeed, from the point of view of protecting the rights of unqualified investors, we propose that unqualified investors on the Russian market should not buy foreign securities, as far as I remember, still unfriendly countries. We will clarify the position on friendly and unfriendly countries. Because an unqualified investor often simply does not have information and understanding of the risk that these shares can be frozen. And now a large number of people find themselves in this situation. And we need the problems here not to increase. I think that those people who are now involved with this, they will rather understand the introduction of such a ban. As for the issue of freezing in the NSD, the Moscow Exchange is now actively engaged in this. An investor protection club has been created there, which includes representatives of the largest banks, brokers, management companies, and professional communities. And the purpose of this club is to jointly assert its rights and prepare lawsuits in order to challenge the decisions that were made against the NSD. QUESTION (Rgapk Mesia): I have three questions. The first clarifying question is about the sale by foreign banks of their Russian subsidiaries. Tell me, please, if the parties are at the stage of negotiations, do they need to cancel these negotiations and interrupt the transactions? Second question. The Central Bank is the only one who sees the reporting of banks. Tell me, how did they finish the first half of the year - better or worse than the expectations of the Central Bank? And one more thing. The Central Bank feared that the payment of dividends and various payments to management would negatively affect the financial stability of banks. Have the Central Bank justified these fears? And the third issue is related to NPFs and pension savings. You have always advocated a more thoughtful and conservative approach to investing pension savings and NPF reserves. However, now, as a large number of investors have left the market, proposals are increasingly appearing to invest pension savings in various projects. Tell me, please, has your opinion changed about this? And do you think that it is necessary to expand the tools and increase the risks when investing pension funds? E.S. NABIULLINA: As for the sale of Russian subsidiaries of foreign banks. If negotiations are underway, in any case, it seems to me that it is even necessary to obtain the permission of the government commission in advance, because the probability of obtaining these permits is small, let's say. As for the analysis of the financial condition of banks. Indeed, banks are not disclosing reports yet, but we are thinking about how they should start disclosing reports. And as we talked about the balance of payments, we also believe that banks should be transparent for their customers, depositors, for their partners. And this issue is now being actively discussed - in what format, when to start disclosing statements to banks. Qualitative assessment. Still , banks have better passed this crisis period than we expected. The conclusion at the moment is that in the systemic capitalization of the banking sector no need. Personally, in February and March, I thought that since the shock to the financial sector was of such magnitude that, despite the buffers created earlier, despite the achieved financial stability, systemic recapitalization of banks would be required. We don't see the need for that now. Yes, individual banks may need help from owners in order to improve the situation in banks. And we gradually want to get out of the regulatory relaxations (we see that the banks are already ready for this), not all at once, but, nevertheless, gradually do it. And as for dividends. Yes, some banks pay dividends, but our position was: if the bank is in good condition and at the same time it does not use regulatory relaxations, it can pay dividends. Indeed, some banks do not take advantage of the regulatory relaxations that we have provided, and in principle can even afford to pay dividends. Now the third question was about pension funds. That's a very good question. There are indeed many proposals for pension funds to start investing more actively, more broadly, contributing to the structural restructuring of the economy. This, of course, is wonderful, but for us, as a regulator, the task of preserving and reliably investing pension savings is a priority. Yes, you can look at some, perhaps, expansion of the toolkit, but not at the expense of the reliability and safety of pension savings. That's priority number one. We really lack a class of institutional investors. And we need to more actively develop all types of collective investments, private equity funds, and look at their regulation. We talked about the benefits that should be, perhaps, taxable. Of course, we need to develop this institutional form of investment - direct, collective investment. QUESTION (THREE "World of Belogorye", Belgorod): We have two questions. In recent months, the "mortality of business" in the country has increased in our region as well. Tell me, do you think that the measures taken to support entrepreneurship are sufficient? And are new mechanisms being prepared? And how do you assess the prospects for the business climate in our country in general? And one more thing. You have repeatedly said that you will not seek to reduce inflation at any cost. What inflation trajectory are you now willing to allow, given that credit must remain affordable? And is it possible for inflation to rise soon after it declines? And what, then, will be the monetary policy? E.S. NABIULLINA: As for "business mortality." Indeed, the closure of legal entities this year has increased compared to 2021. But here, probably, it is impossible to judge simply by the data year-on-year, because, for example, in 2020, the number of legal entities was closed more during the pandemic, if you compare the closure. But what is more important here is probably not even this, not the speed of closure of legal entities, but at the same time the emergence of new legal entities and the expansion of the scale of their activities, because structural adjustment, it will really mean that some enterprises will reduce output, maybe even close, others should expand output, new companies will be created. As for business sentiment. They are very different, there are different indicators. We also have our own indicator of business sentiment, we measure it by surveys. It's been showing some improvement in recent months. It's an optimistic signal. And inflation. Yes, we do confirm that in the conditions of structural adjustment after a sharp jump in inflation, there may be a period of increased inflation for some time, it may deviate from our goal. For next year, I repeat, we see an inflation forecast of 5-7%, that is, it is above our goal of 4%. Yes, in some periods inflation or the rate of price growth may increase. It is very important for us to look at whether this is under the influence of one-time factors or this is a steady increase. If this is a steady increase, we can and will respond with a rate in order to return inflation to the target, to 4%, because after all, confidence in price stability is the most important factor, including for lowering long-term interest rates on loans. With high inflation, there are no long-term loans available. Therefore, price stability has been and is a priority for us. QUESTION (TV channel "Russia 24"): In a number of liberated territories, for example, Kherson, Zaporozhye regions, the ruble has already been introduced into circulation. And when can we expect that the ruble will become a full-fledged currency in these and other liberated territories? E.S. NABIULLINA: The ruble does go in these territories along with the hryvnia. It's hard for me to talk about any deadlines. QUESTION (RBC newspaper): I will have a question about the NCC. In June, when the NSD came under sanctions, you preemptively recommended that banks reduce their foreign exchange positions in the NCC. Have banks followed this recommendation? How much have their currency positions declined this month since the recommendations? And in principle, has the open currency position of banks changed in any way after our demonetization intensified? E.S. NABIULLINA: The Bank of Russia sees positive dynamics in the process of reducing the value of foreign currency balances on the accounts of NCC and NSD. In general, in the banking sector, we have a long open currency position. It has grown slightly in recent months, but it is less than in March. Why is this happening. Because the demonetization of liabilities is happening a little faster than the demonetization of assets. That is, if you (banks - Ed.) have long-term foreign currency loans and so on, a lot of work is required here and, possibly, on conversion, into ruble assets. But in any case, demonetization on the passive part is faster than on the active part. And we see that not only under our influence, but also under the influence, unfortunately, of sanctions, banks continue to actively take measures to demonetize their balance sheets. They understand that this is a risk. Despite the fact that we have temporarily introduced regulatory relaxations on the currency position for banks that exist under sanctions, they should have plans to exit this currency position, because we have no intention to extend this regulatory relaxation after January 1, 2023. QUESTION (Kurskaya Pravda newspaper, Kursk): Over the past few months, the Central Bank has made diametrically opposed decisions on the key rate - from a sharp increase to a decrease to the level of last year. Do you think that such decisions of the Bank of Russia do not mislead the population and firms that are already in conditions of high uncertainty? Maybe it is worth immediately lowering the level of the key rate to a minimum value of 2-3%? E.S. NABIULLINA: We believe it doesn't. Yes, indeed, uncertainty is very high and the scale of changes in external conditions is unprecedented. But even in these conditions, in conditions of such uncertainty, we consider it very important to preserve the key elements of stability, namely price and financial stability. Therefore, our decision on the rate, its sharp increase was dictated primarily by the fact that we restore financial stability. And then its gradual decline in order to ensure price stability. In our opinion, these are key elements for business, for business planning. But if, as you say, the key rate was immediately reduced to 2-3%, what would happen? Most likely, what would happen would happen was that the money from the deposits would instantly leave. I have already said that now people have shifted funds from term deposits, where they are more fixed, to current accounts, savings accounts, from which you can easily spend. That is, it shows that people are more willing to withdraw money, reduce their funds in banks and direct them to consumption. If the deposit rate were 2-3% with double-digit annual inflation, of course, people would first of all go to buy goods and services so that money does not depreciate on deposits. And there would be no more goods at this time with such a fall, including imports. And we'd just get a lot of inflation. There would be no question of any price stability then. Therefore, of course, such actions to sharply reduce the rate to the minimum values would simply lead to an increase in inflation, people's savings would depreciate. And I must say that loans from this would not become affordable. Because when banks issue loans, yes, for short-term loans they are more guided by the key rate, but in long-term loans they are guided by what inflation will be. Of course, with a 2-3% key rate and, say, double-digit inflation, loan rates will definitely be double-digit. Therefore, it would not have such a positive effect. But our actions on the rate, on reducing inflation, they lead to the fact that long-term loans will be adequate, affordable at the level of rates. QUESTION (project Ipyez? ????): A little bit about the job market. Although you said that you do not comment on unemployment, but still. You said that the labor market will change. As a matter of fact, it turns out that the qualifications of workers will change. How will this ultimately affect wages, demand, inflation, and monetary policy? And the second question. He's like, a bit of a conspiracy theory. Given that today the interest rate was so sharply reduced. Is this due to the fact that, for example, the geopolitical situation is now tied to restricting, say, Russian oil exports? Plus the introduction of an oil price ceiling. How does the Central Bank assess this? In general, how does the Central Bank assess this? E.S. NABIULLINA: As for the labor market. Structural adjustment of the economy, of course, will be accompanied by structural changes in the labor market. Some specialties will be more in demand, others a little less. These are the movements that will happen. And salaries will also be very different (change - Ed.) in different sectors. By the way, after the pandemic, you remember when remote services began to develop very actively, there was just a sharp shortage of IT specialists, cybersecurity and so on. This is also an example of structural adjustment. How this will affect overall unemployment rates. It depends on how quickly, on the one hand, labor will leave, free up labor from those sectors or enterprises that are shrinking, and move to those that are growing. And the speed of this will still depend on how much your profession, your skills, knowledge, specialization will be in demand, whether you need to retrain, for how long. Of course, this is a complex process. Therefore, it is very difficult to make quantitative measurements. But this process will certainly take place. He will need to be watched. And, of course, overall aggregate unemployment rates will affect inflation. And we will take this into account in monetary policy. As for geopolitics and the possible ceiling on oil export prices. I don't even want to speculate now whether it's real or not. But if this is introduced in one form or another, in my opinion, this will obviously lead to an increase in world prices. And as far as I understand , we will not supply oil to the countries that set this price limit, and our oil and oil products will be reoriented to those countries that are ready to cooperate with us. And since this will happen against the background of rising world oil prices, even with a possible decrease in quantitative indicators, this may have a smaller effect on all indicators. let's just say, the exchange rate, the balance of payments. Of course, this is more of a matter for the Government. Rather, I commented on what it might look like - as an impact on the macroeconomy. QUESTION (Vedomosti newspaper): I have one clarifying question, if I may, and one complete question. As for the budget rule. In which currencies is it advisable to store additional oil and gas revenues under the new design? And, in fact, a question. Now the discussion and preparation for the second reading of the draft law on electronic archives is underway. Is this currently being discussed with the Bank of Russia? What objections or proposals does the Bank of Russia have on this issue? And what is the best option for digitizing bank documents that the Bank of Russia sees? And do you agree with it - respectively, is this taken into account in the bill? E.S. NABIULLINA: As for the budget rule. Within the framework of the budget rule, this will be the accumulation of the Government's assets and this, of course, is a question for the Government. We are ready to discuss this in consultation mode. But the set of assets is probably not very large, let's say, in which you can store. In particular, it is possible to discuss the currencies of friendly countries. Here we need to look at the stability, of course, of these currencies, at the liquidity of the markets. All these parameters are taken into account when placing assets. As for electronic archives. In principle, we support, of course, the transfer from paper to electronic form of all archives. We know, on the part of banks, how big the costs are precisely because of the storage of archives in paper form. In the end, they are included in some shares of interest on loans. Therefore, of course, the digitalization of everything is very important. We have created our own digitalisation programmes within the Bank of Russia. We have digitized a lot of processes and digitized documents. And what is allowed to be stored not in paper form, we digitize. But about the specific details of the bill, if necessary, we will clarify. I just don't have the information right now. QUESTION (Interfax news agency): The Central Bank always talks about the return of retail investors' confidence in the stock market. But, as far as we know, Gazprom's decision to abandon dividends has greatly shaken their confidence, they are upset. How do you regain that trust? In connection with this decision, perhaps some corporate actions of Gazprom would make it possible to regain this trust, for example, a buyback of shares? One more question. What national indices is the Central Bank currently working on? Is it just the benchmark of oil? Maybe some index on precious metals? E.S. NABIULLINA: I agree. The trust of retail investors is extremely important at the moment. And it will be necessary to take measures to increase the confidence of retail investors, because now there have been many events that have negatively affected the sentiment of retail investors, including those related to the introduction of external restrictions. It is difficult for me to comment on any corporate actions on the part of Gazprom. I'm not going to do that, but certainly one of the elements that retail investors are counting on is dividend yields. This will certainly need to be taken into account when we talk about regaining the confidence of retail investors. As for national indices. In principle, national price indices are very important for us, they are an important source of information about market prices in conditions when we can no longer rely on global indices that were actively used. We already have such a first wheat index, and we are working together with the Government on a whole set of such indices. This applies primarily to commodities, and not only to commodities, but primarily to all commodities. In order for these indexes to be launched, the interest of users in them is very important. For example, in agriculture, there was an active interest of potential users. Therefore, this work will continue actively, including precious metals, yes. Thank you very much.

Title: Bank of Russia Governor  spoke at the plenary session of the State Duma
text: Bank of Russia Governor Elvira Nabiullina spoke at the plenary session of the State Duma November 22, 2017 Performance Good afternoon, dear colleagues! Today I present the Main Directions of the Monetary Policy of the Bank of Russia - this is a basic document that describes our vision for the development of the economic situation and the measures that will ensure the implementationof the monetary policy to ensure price stability. We closely cooperated with the relevant committees of the State Duma to finalize the Main Directions, and I would like to thank my colleagues for their very constructive and professionalinvolvement. I will start with the characteristics of the general economic situation and our forecast. According to the Bank of Russia, the economy is growing at a rate close to potential. These are the growth rates that are determined primarily by the structure of our economy, and notoutside the factors. The consequences of the shock associated with the fall in oil prices in 2014-2015, our economy has practically overcome. According to preliminary estimates, the GDP growth rate in the fourth quarter will be almost the same as in the third, and our current estimates showthat the growth rate of the economy this year will be about 1.8%. According to our forecast, the economy will grow in the next 3 years by 1.5-2% - in the baseline scenario with oil prices of 42 per barrel and in the scenario with oil prices rising to 60 per barrel. 1.5-2% is, of course, a low growth rate, this is not at all what I think we would all like for our economy. Our economy can grow at a rate of 3% and 4% per year if structural measures are taken: to increase labor productivity,labor mobility, and improve the investment climate. I would especially like to emphasize that the new growth rate cannot be achieved by monetary policy measures. Monetary policy measures are only capable of Whether the Russian economy can overcome structural constraints and reach a different, higher potential level of growth depends on the complexity of economic policy measures. Nevertheless, monetary policy makes a significant contribution to the economic development of the country. And we consider monetary policy as part of the overall economic policy. Without low inflation, without macroeconomic stability in general, sustainable growth is not possible. Overthe past three years, we have pursued a policy of disinflation. We have consistently reduced inflation to the target level of 4%. Let me remind you that the peak inflation rate was almost 17% in the spring of 2015. At that time, few people believed that in principle it was possible to ensure that inflation in Russiawas at a sustainably low level. Now inflation in annual terms is 2.6%. Our forecast for the end of the year is 2.5-2.7%. We believe that inflation is near the target, near the target, and no special reaction is required from the monetary policy, since the current low value is due primarily to the action of temporary factors: these are relatively high oil prices (and the corresponding strengthening of the ruble) and a record harvest. We expect that during 2018 inflation will return to b lick to 4%. At the same time, we see the potential for a further reduction in the key rate, but the pace and scale of the reduction will be determined by the dynamics of economic indicators. The focus of our policy now is to keep inflation constantly close to the target value of 4% and reduce the volatility of inflation. The stability of inflation is very important both for a steady decline in inflation expectations of the population, and for a more confident planning by business of long-term projects. Inflation volatility is highly dependent on non-monetaryfactors. Managing them is now an important area of our interaction with the Government. We have prepared a special report on non-monetary factors of inflation, published it, discuss its conclusions with the Government and see the main non-monetary risks for inflationin the following: this is also the insufficient development of infrastructure (primarily logistics, storage agricultural products), tariffs of natural monopolies. I have already said that a record harvest also led to the current slowdown in inflation of 2.6%. But the prices of agricultural commodities have fallen not only because of just a good harvest, but because farmers, peasants are forced to sell it as quickly as possible andlow prices, because there is not enough infrastructure to store products. And if, due to poor storage conditions, crop stocks decrease, then again there may be an increase. prices for fruits and vegetables. This is the volatility of inflation. It'sa harm that we need to address, but it requires a joint effort with the Government. I'm going to talk a little bit more about inflation, because it's important for us to reach the target, the target, and stay in it. But what does that give to the economy? First. Low inflationis a necessary condition for the well-being of the population. A large increase in prices does not make it possible to plan the family budget, depreciates incomes and savings. Inflation hits the standard of living of people with low incomes the hardest. Last year, inflation at the end of theyear already fell to the levels of 2011-2013, but nevertheless, according to sociological surveys, it remained the number one problem for Russians. And only this year, when inflation reached the target level, in sociological surveys it began to give way to other problems. But what worries us is that citizens' inflation expectations remain high, although they are declining. Just for clarity, we counted two very simple indices - you can call them New Year's indices. We consider how prices for sets of products for traditional New Year's dishes, such as olivier salad and herring under a fur coat, are growing. Olivier salad has risen in price by 1.2% over the year - it costs about 312 rubles to cook, herring under a fur coat has fallen in price by 0.9% - costs a little more than 150 rubles. But people's sense of inflation is much higher. Andwe really want to achieve public confidence in our policy, to the fact that you can manage family money without constantly thinking about rising prices. Second. The positive effect of low inflation is an improvement in the business environment and benefits for theeffects of projects. Low inflation enables long-term planning. It stimulates efficiency gains by enterprises and does not allow shifting high costs into price increases, into citizens' expenses. That is, it forces enterprises to increase productivityand reduce their costs. Increasing the productivity of Russian enterprises is an important factor in the formation of a new growth model. If you answer the question of how the competitiveness of the Russian economy will increase - cheap labor and cheap resources or products with high added value, obviously the second answer is preferable, this is the path to a highly developed economy. Therefore, we often call low inflation a catalyst for structural changes associated with an increase inproductivity. Third. Low inflation contributes to the de-dollarization of the economy and the stabilization of the exchange rate. When people understand that inflation is under control, they do not buy currency for the future to protect themselves from the depreciation of the ruble, and do not try to sharply "turn over" the currency in the event of some external shocks, if they are sure that inflation will remain low. Fourth. Economic growth is fueled by financial resources. We have often been criticized in the past for the fact that the rigidity of our policyhinders the development of credit and, therefore, hinders the acceleration of growth. In fact, the development of lending is hindered not by our high key rate, but by high inflation. Let me remind you that in 2011-2013 the key rate was lower than it is now (5.5%), the interest rates on loans for loans for the united states. the reactions were even higher than they are now. Now they are declining precisely because inflation is decreasing. Healthy lending, primarily long-term, investment lending, can develop only on the basis of low inflation. We are already seeing that, following the investmentand our key rate, interest rates in the economy are also decreasing. Interest rates on loans have decreased by up to one year by 2 percentage points, and on long-term loans by 2.3 percentage points. That is, rates on long-term loans are decreasing at a faster pace. This meansthat economic agents are beginning to believe in low inflation. Rates on long loans, Important for investment and mortgage lending, decline faster. For 10 months of this year, credit to the economy grew by 4.7%. In the corporate sector in January-September, there was an increase in lending to many industries, including mining ( 14.0%), agriculture ( 9.0%), manufacturing ( 9.5%) and transport and communications ( 8.1%). Unsecured consumer lending has grownby 7.8%. In our opinion, this is moderate growth without the risk of any bubbles. Mortgage lending is growing convincingly ( 9.3% in January-September of this year). Mortgage growth is also evidence of confidence. economic agents in low inflation. In general, we believe that the banking system is able to further increase healthy lending. The profit of banks for 10 months amounted to 693 billion rubles, which is slightly lower than in the same period last year. But if it were not for the losses of NK and Otkritie, which are being sanitized by BINBA, the profit would have been greater. What is very important for us is that the number of profitable banks prevails (397 out of 572 credit institutions that operated on November 1 are profitable). According to our estimates, lending will grow at a rate of 5-7% next year, then 7-10% per year - this is higher than GDP growth, and lending will support economic growth. I would like to note that credit resources, of course, fuel economic growth. But you can't consider borrowed funds to be the main source of development. It is important that capital is formed in our economy, so that businesses are not afraid to invest their funds in the form of investments. Our problem is that we have low financing of investments by attracting capital, and excessive credit growthand excessive debt burden, which will then put pressure on the ability of enterprises to develop. We see right now, that it is precisely those industries that have accumulated excessive debts in previous years that are lame, and many enterprises are not able to repay them. We need a good investment climate, we need to develop corporate governance practices, transparency of enterprises. High interest rates are also a payment for the risks associated with the fact that some borrowers of enterprises do not have enough transparency. They have a confusing ownership structure (often offshore), a confusing, incomprehensible management structure. Therefore, of course, investors do not want to invest in these enterprises, and at best they are lended. These are also important factors in overcoming the structuralconstraints in the economy. Now a few words about what our policy will be on the forecast horizon. We will continue to reduce the key rate, but quite smoothly. In the absence of unfavorable external factors, a gradual reduction in the key rate from the current level of 8.25% to the equilibrium level of 6-7% within 1-2 years is possible. Now that inflation has slowed below 4%, we are often told that we can cut rates faster. But we have to weigh the benefits and the risks here. The economy will experience a short-term relief from faster rate cuts, which, in our view, is absolutely not comparable to the troubles that await it if inflation deviates from the target upwards and we have to reverse policy. And the foundations of the formationof sources of long money that are just beginning to form will be undermined. Too quick an exit to the equilibrium level of rates in the face of elevated inflation expectations, and the latest data on inflation expectations - 8.7% of the population, despite the fact that inflationis 2.6% ... And that, of course, is holding us back. And we believe that a predictable, consistent policy with a clear result is much more important so that business can plan, and therefore develop. Some other settings of our policy. We do not planto revise the inflation target. The level of 4% corresponds to the structure of our economy, it reduces the risks of deflation in certain sectors and at the same time prevents inflation from rising too fast for savings and investments to depreciate. We remaincommitted to the floating exchange rate of the ruble. And this is also noted in the document. The floating exchange rate allows the economy not only to overcome external shocks more easily, but also to be more flexible in the search for a new model of economic growth, to balance the interests of importers and exporters. We have almost completed the exit from all anti-crisis measures, the economy and the financial system are able to cope with the challenges on their own. In the near future, in the coming years, we will smoothly come out of the so-calledx special refinancing tools, who supported priority and vulnerable sectors during the crisis. But we will do it absolutely smoothly and measuredly. The situation is similar with foreign currency refinancing for banks. The need of credit institutions for refinancing operations in foreign currency by the Central Bank continued to decline in 2017, and in early November 2017, banks fully repaid the debt on such currency transactions. The volume of our gold and foreign exchange reserves will remain at a stable level throughout the forecast period. We maintain our target of increasing reserves to 500 billion, but we plan to buy foreign currency in reserves no earlier than weare sure that both inflation and inflation expectations are steadily low. My remarks today focus on monetary policy, but talking about monetary policy is always an inevitable conversation about the growth of the economy as a whole. Therefore, I would like to say a few words in conclusion about other areas of our policy on the development of financial markets, which, as we hope, also contribute to economic development. The country's financial system is generally stable , and this applies to both banks and the non-banking sector. We pay great attention to the development of the bond market as an alternative and complement to bank credit, improving the quality of corporate governance, developing the rating industry of the national,tightening the requirements for the use of pension savings. Each of these sectors of the financial market contributes to facilitating access to financial resources for competitive Russian companies. A separate focus of our work is to increase financialaccessibility for small businesses. We are moving to proportional regulation in the banking system, and thank you that the Duma adopted the relevant legislation. We very much expect that banks with a basic license, which will appear from the beginning of next year, will significantly support lending to small businesses. The fact that we are now seeing profits not only from the largest banks, but even in three-quarters of the banking system, it provides additional certainty of this. One last thing. A year ago, our economy was just emerging from recession. Today, on the one hand, we are optimistic that growth has recovered faster than many expected. On the other hand, we have very quickly approached the 1.5-2% rate of potential economic growth. And we now have no reason to refrain from structural changes: the economy is stable, we can and should grow faster. We very much hope That the decisions that will be made on structural measures will allow us to raise our forecasts for gross domestic product growth upwards, unlike what we are now considering. The Bank of Russia, for its part, will make every effort to maintain price and financial stability, ensure the health and development of the financial market in accordance with the needs of the pits of our growing economy.

Title: Speech at the Russian Stock Market 2018 Conference
text: Speech by the Governor of the Bank Russia Elvira Nabiullina at the conference "Russian Stock Market - 2018" April 24, 2018 Performance Good afternoon, dear colleagues! Thank you very much for the invitation to speak at today's conference. For the Bank of Russia as a mega regulator, the balanced development of various sectors of the financial market is very important, and the dynamics demonstrated by the securities market, collective investment markets, and trust management is generally encouraging. And I cannot first do without a few figures that, in my opinion, characterize this dynamic. For example, only in individualtrust management, the amount of funds under management over the past two years has increased 4 times - to more than 800 billion rubles. In the brokerage services market, there has also recently been a positive trend in the growth of the client base (absoluteclients - 372 thousand customers in two years) and asset management services (absolute growth - 64 thousand customers in two years). The value of assets under management in the collective investment market increased by almost 60% over 3 years (from 1.9 to 2.9 trillion rubles). In addition, the main volume is made up of closed-end funds, in which mainly qualified investors invest in individual projects. However, the volume of open mutual funds, intended mainly for investments of retail investors in the financialmarket, also increased significantly - to 216 billion rubles, actually doubling in 3 years. All these figures show that the dynamics are really quite positive. Perhaps the volumes do not satisfy us yet, but the dynamics in recent years are encouraging. The decline in inflation and, accordingly, rates on banking products makes alternative products increasingly interesting for retail investors. And the new technologies, which Oleg Vyacheslavovich (Vyugin - ed.) mentioned, they enableFinans intermediaries both to create new products and to extend to different types of customers those services that previously could only be offered to very wealthy clients. All this creates the prerequisites for further increase in these segments. In orderfor the market to grow confidently, it is very important to ensure the confidence of investors, and this means the stability of the financial institutions themselves, and a high level of protection of the rights and interests of customers. Trust is now the main thing for financial markets. Protection of investors' rights should bedealt with not only by the regulator, but also by the markets. Protection of investors' rights is a joint task of the regulator and the market, primarily a task for self-regulatory organizations. For qualified investors, in our opinion, maximum flexibility on the part of financial intermediaries, the ability to offer a product that meets the needs of the client, and for unqualified investors it is a high level of protection against losses and information transparency, elimination of pitfalls when using finanproducts, which, unfortunately, are many. What, in our opinion, are the main problems we must solve: First. It is necessary to increase information transparency, the availability of information on the profitability of financial instruments and the risks for them. Second. Rules should beestablished for the sale of financial instruments and services, which will be based on the principle of priority of the client's needs, and not only on the commercial interest of the intermediary or agent. Basically, both of these points are the fight against misselling at differentlevels, this task is very important for the development of the market. The cost of selling a product to a disappointed investor is much higher than the cost of selling to a new investor, and even higher than the cost of selling to an investor who has had a positive experienceof investing. Thus, disappointing the investor, the company harms not only itself - it harms the entire market. And we expect that the fight against unfair sales will take place, including at the level of self-regulatory organizations. Third. It is necessary to expand the availability of financial instruments and services. For some products, the offer is concentrated in selected regions and even in individual companies. Thus, 75% of clients on brokerage services and 86% of brokerage individual investment accounts are concentrated in the 5 largest brokerage houses; 85% of clients Asset management and 96% of individual investment accounts are managed by the 3 largest companies. The Bank of Russia, together with the Moscow Exchange, is now preparing to launch a financialmarketplace project, which, in our opinion, will contribute to solving these problems, as well as as well as increased competition among financial service providers. Many venues are currently discussing this project, many issues, but we nevertheless considerit important to promote it as a project that gives a choice to the consumer and develops competition in the financial market. Fourth. An effective mechanism is needed to segregate the own assets of a financial institution from the assets of its clients. In the event of bankruptcyof a financial intermediary, the investor's rights should also be reliably protected. Amendments to the Bankruptcy Law are being developed that eliminate legal uncertainty in the bankruptcy of professional participants in the securities market and extend to creditorganizations when carrying out professional activities in the securities market the obligation to separate client assets from their own assets. A significant role in increasing the transparency and comfort of the market as a whole for retail investors belongsto self-regulatory organizations. The development of the institution of self-regulation should lead to an increase in the competitiveness of the Russian financial market, the formation of an integral regulatory framework that meets the needs of both professional participants in the financial market and consumers of financial services. Today, the legislation provides for a new format of interaction between the industry and the regulator - the basic standard. Basic standards should consolidate the best market practices and ensure a flexible and rapid response to changing working conditions. Over the past year, it must be said, a large-scale work has been done: developed with the help of the market and SROs, agreed and approved several basic standards for forex dealers, brockers, managers and depositories. Now a large number of new standards are being prepared, including the most important standards for consumer protection and standards for corporate governance. We believe that this work is very important and will also increasethe credibility of financial market participants. Special attention should be paid to the issue of protecting the rights of investors in the collective investment market. The most important innovation in the field of investor protection is the introduction of fiduciary liability for pension funds, that is,the obligation to act in the interests of the client and reimburse the client for losses incurred or lost benefits in case of poor asset management. There was a lot of controversy on this topic, but the legislation was passed, and theobligations of pen zion funds to undergo stress testing, to have a developed risk management system and a good, reliable investment process - all together this represents the requirements for the quality of the pension product that is offered to citizens. To note the role of the stress testing tool. Yes, the passage of stress testing is a factor in the application of supervisory measures, but there is another side: after the stress test is tested in practice, we plan to once again look at thepossibility of expanding the objects available for investment by pension funds, after we understand that pension funds are stable enough even to pass unfavorable conditions. The introduction of the obligation to act in the interests of the client and have a good investment process allows you to expand the capabilities of the fund engaged in voluntary non-state pension insurance, independent investment of pension reserves without mandatory involvement ofmanagers. I will say right away that just as in the investment fund market we started small, checked the readiness of the market for an open list of expenses and only then, after receiving confirmation of the effectiveness of the chosen path, the practice expanded, so in the marketof pension funds we plan to test the rejection of a mandatory management company (so far only in the market of voluntary pension insurance). The possibility of applying such an approach in the market of compulsory pension provision will depend on of the results obtained . Management companies, of course, are not very pleased with this decision, but we are convinced that additional costs are always covered by the consumer in the end, which means that they need to be reduced. At the same time, we understand that the business models of the managementcompanies were calculated, among other things, on the basis of the mandatory nature of their service, so we expect to provide for a transition period. In conclusion, I would like to dwell on the issue of proportional regulation as a key regulatory innovation that we are preparing for implementation and want to discuss with market participants. In banking regulation, proportional regulation has already been adopted, and this year is a transitional year for the banking sector, during which small banks will have to decide whetherto choose a basic license that allows them to conduct a limited volume of transactions, but at the same time enjoy the benefits of simplified regulation (for them the amount of regulatory burden is reduced), or to choose a universal license, for which they do not have to. There are restrictions, but also higher regulatory burden and capital requirements. We believe that non-credit financial institutions should also move towards proportional regulation. And it's important to take the right approach here, because we think there are two approaches that you have to choose between. this is by analogy with banking regulation, it will require the delimitation of operations within the framework of certain types of licenses. Another option is to fix certain indicators ofthe organization's activity and the corresponding regulatory requirements at the level of regulatory acts of the Bank of Russia. The license will be uniform. With this approach, the organization has the opportunity to assess the amount of rights it needs to perform operations in comparisonwith the corresponding volume of regulatory requirements. We have to discuss all this with the market, we are going to publish an advisory report this year. And I want to say that the practice of the advisory report, which the Central Bankapplies, has proven itself, it allows us to listen to the opinions of the market at the early stages of promoting the concept, to listen to all concerns, to adjust, where necessary, the position. And we will adhere to the regulation, in proposing a new approach to tacos. The principle of openness to discussion. In our opinion, it is very important that the market develops steadily, that the regulatory environment is predictable for participants, that they understand what business models they can build and that these business models will beattractive. I hope that this and other issues of developing a market based on trust, high standards of customer service and healthy competition, in which we are all interested. we will be able to discuss today here, and on SRO sites in the future. Oleg Vyacheslavovich (Vyugin - ed.) has already asked some questions, and I hope that the discussion will be interesting both today and tomorrow. I wish you success in your work, success in business. I hope that the format of work in dialogue with the regulator will contribute to the successfuldevelopment of the business. Thank you!

Title: Governor of the Bank of Russia spoke at the XXVII International Financial Congress
text: Governor of the Bank of Russia Elvira Nabiullina performed at XXVII International Financial Congress June 7, 2018 Good afternoon, dear colleagues! I am pleased to welcome you to the International Financial Congress. This year's theme "The Financial System: Resilience for Growth." The theme was not chosen by chance. More than 10 years have passed since the beginning of the global financial crisis. 10 years have passed, and we still cannot say that the world economy has really moved on. to sustainable growth rates and able to grow independently, without relying on incentive measures. This, of course, is an occasion to analyze the reasons that led to such a long story. And whether the treatment was effective, it is too early to draw conclusions. I think that time will put everything in its place. In my view, it is quite right that the responsibility for the financial crisis, which had such a long and profoundimpact on the economy and the well-being of the people in many countries, rests largely with inadequate regulation in the financial sector. Regulation (or rather, its lack) has allowed the accumulation of risks in financial institutions - risks, which are not the same as the financial sector. these were then translated into the real economy and, due to globalization, affected almost all countries. And the fastest, and most of all, are the countries that have accumulated their own internal weaknesses. All of this suggests that the adequacy of regulationand the resilience (if you will, resistance) of regulators to calls for loosening regulation, enabling financial institutions to promote economic growth are all critical to keeping the risks from being discreet but often threatening toaccumulate. It is not surprising that the response to the crisis was a large-scale reform of financial regulation (its necessity at the time of its beginning was recognized by almost everyone). Tighter financial regulation has seriously changed, and continuesto change, the financial sector. It was a real response to a crisis that is a game changer and reduces the risks of a recurrence of the crisis. As for soft monetary policy, which literally everyone knows about, its main goal was to keep the economy and financial marketsafloat and prevent a slide into a depression. In other words, loose monetary policy is a policy of adjustment, and financial regulation reform is a policy of change. Clearly, financial regulatory reform alone is not enough. Soft andone-on-one policies were designed to buy time to carry out the necessary structural reforms, to correct internal imbalances. For each country, its own. Time has been won, but have these reforms been implemented? Apparently, the answer is to be found in lowlabor productivity, low investment, excessive accumulation of debt in many countries that threaten financial stability. Talk of a new crisis is coming up more and more often here and there. The accumulated imbalances are too large, and monetary policy is by no means omnipotent. So the acute phase of the crisis was followed by a long period of low growth. And only last year the global economy seems to have begun to emerge from this state. The rate of economic growth in the world approached 4% per year, unemployment in many developed countries reached lows in the last 40-50 years. But we must not forget, that this growth has so far occurred while maintaining the stimulating orientation of monetary policy. For example, the European Central Bank is stilllying to buy assets. And of course, now is the time to discuss the lessons we can learn from the post-crisis decade. Even if the indicators of productivity and investment do not allow us to say that the crisis has played its cleansing role, the economyhas come out of the crisis stronger than it was, but maybe we have still achieved sufficient stability of the global financial system? What consequences of the crisis still haunt us and what new problems have we already begun to face? Perhaps these questions are being asked in one form or another by regulators in both developed and developing countries. For Russia, where the financial market is very young by global standards, has many peculiarities and specific problems, these issues are also very acute. And yet , as a regulator, we can say with confidence that the financial system is more stable than it was 10 years ago. and moreover - more stable than it was 4 years ago, in 2014. And the question that we must ask ourselves is: what needs to be done to ensure that thegrowing stability of the financial system becomes a factor in economic growth? The development of the financial sector and how it will contribute to the economic growth that our country needs will be influenced by three main factors. The first is what will happenin the global economy. The second is the preservation of macroeconomic stability in Russia: low inflation, low debt and a balanced budget. And the third is, of course, the pace of structural reforms and the economic growth rates that depend on them. A little more about these factors. Last year, we saw a fairly prosperous picture of the development of the global economy. But the inevitability of the normalization of monetary policy in developed economies leads to the fact that capital flows, which during the period of cheap liquidity were practicallytied to fundamental factors, will tend to quiet harbor historically risk-free assets and will pay more attention to the fundamental weaknesses or strengths of certain economies. Rising interest rates, primarily in the dollarborrowing market, and the reversal of capital flows are already creating tensions in a number of vulnerable emerging economies. on macroeconomic parameters. And in general, the volatility of global financial markets is increasing. The situation, of course, is complicated by various kindsof political risks. The growth of populism in individual countries, the growth of protectionism with the risk of full-fledged trade wars, the intensification of the unilateral use of financial sanctions by individual countries - all this creates risks for stability in financialmarkets, increases the already increased market volatility. Experience shows that the only thing that a country with an emerging market can counter in such a situation in order to preserve opportunities for sustainable economic growth ismacro-economic stability, the absence of imbalances and excessive debt burden, a healthy financial system that has a good safety cushion in the form of capital and liquidity. In recent years, the Bank of Russia and the Government have paid specialattention to these issues, and the increased external risks are a signal not to neglect them further. macro stability, but on the contrary, to strengthen it. Last year, as we promised in 2014, when we switched to inflation targeting, we reached the inflation target for the first time . Now it is important to consolidate this result, to make low inflation the norm of our life. Therefore, the goal of the Monetary Policy of the Bank of Russia for the near future is to maintain inflation near 4%. As you know, inflationary consequencesof new policy measures are currently being discussed. Government. I have already spoken on this topic at the recent International Economic Forum. Therefore, I just want to emphasize once again that our monetary policy is set up in such a way that we will in any case cope with theinflationary consequences of these measures. In some cases, a short-term acceleration of inflation is possible, perhaps even slightly above 4%. And we understand that it is not always wise to try to avoid this, so as not to harm economic growth. But if there are any deviations, they will not be large-scale and will be short-term. Inflation will go back to 4%. The stabilization of inflation will be accompanied by a decrease in the volatility of interest rates as inflation expectations decrease and anchor . On this issue, especially in terms of anchoring, we still have a lot to do. We see from the data of the last month that the spikes in prices for certain goods (gasoline above all), the volatility of the exchange rate continues to have a serious impact on inflationexpectations. They're still not anchored. On the part of the Government, the budget rule is a serious contribution to macro stability. We believe that it protects budget expenditures from fluctuations in oil prices and enables the budget to financepriority areas on a stable basis. Provides stability and other macroeconomic parameters, including the real exchange rate. Thus, from the point of view of the macroeconomic background, we do not see noticeable risks for the financial system in the future. Now about the pace of economic growth. It is obvious that the development of the financial sector and the development of the economy are interrelated. Strong economic growth strengthens the financial system. And vice versa. When formulating monetary policy, we constantly assess potential economic growth, and we see that the 1.5-2% growth that we have now, with unemployment that has already fallen to a historic low, are approximately the growth rates that our economy can provide in the medium termwithout changing its structure. We see so far that the inertial scenario continues to be implemented and it has not been possible to reverse the current trends. Nevertheless, we expect and expect that the specific measures that the Government will proposeto implement the President's Address, to accelerate the pace of economic growth, in addition to increasing budget expenditures in priority areas, these measures will open up opportunities for private investment and private entrepreneurship and will allow raising the economy. ultimately, the potential for economic growth. Of course, the impact of these measures will manifest itself gradually, and our financial institutions should take this into account. What overall impact will this combination of external and internal factors have on the financial sector? Firstof all, while low economic growth rates and unclear specific growth points are, of course, a challenge for the financial system. Now the financial system has responded to it with rapid growth in consumer lending, as well as mortgage lending, this is the onlycredit market, in terms of development of which Russia is significantly lagging behind countries with comparable economies. But this process cannot continue for a long time without risk. the debt burden of the population is beginning to grow. We will be watching closely and, if necessary, take measures to prevent the formation of bubbles here. At the same time, the process of cleaning the balance sheets of companies from bad debts is taking place, this will gradually create conditions for the development of lending to manufacturing companies. And of course, it is very important that financial institutions are ready for this, so that they can take advantage of new opportunities. And for this we need to develop competencies in banks to assess the prospects of companies, new, small companies, evaluate new projects, developproject and investment financing tools. We believe that the financial sector should become a partner for business in the search for new growth points. New financial technologies, including technologies for working with big data, can becomean important tool for the development of such competencies and qualifications. At the same time, we see that state support measures are designed primarily for those financial institutions that already have such competencies and qualifications. Second. Neutralizing monetary policy, which is just around the corner, means slowing down, and ultimately stopping, the rate cuts. There may also be situations where rates could rise if there are proinflationary risks. Over the past few years, financial institutionshave been living in conditions of falling interest rates. It is important that the change in trend does not take the sector by surprise, does not lead to excessive interest rate risks. And now we need to think about whether how will the pricing of financial instruments be arranged in conditions when the movement of rates ceases to be Unidirectional. Further. High external risks mean that the period of low volatility is a thing of the past. And we are waiting for a more volatile situation in world markets. These risks also need to be managed. Do not try toshift them to the final borrower, as sometimes happens, or the investor. Experience shows that in the end this ends with the realization of credit risks for the financial institution itself. And of course, now the ability to constructinstruments taking into account such risks, to learn how to hedge risks, is becoming important. Finally, both the macroeconomic situation and the rapid progress in the development of new technologies will require the financial sector to better manage costs, improve its procedures and improveits resources. Changing the business models of financial institutions, and we believe that it will be influenced by these factors, all of this should also contribute to accelerating economic growth, and will also make financial institutions more resilient in theshort term. To accelerate this transition, we will make greater use of incentive regulation. Stimulative regulation is often contrasted with neutral regulation, saying that itmay not be safe for the financial system to use regulatory measures to influence the business model of financial institutions. But let's look, for example, at the banking system. When we see a situation in which banks, including large ones, are used to finance almost only the business of theirowners, to finance mainly mergers and acquisitions, and not effective projects in the economy, we must understand that this threatens both the economy and the stability of the financial market itself. And therefore, regulation that will stimulate Normal classical banking activities, of course, will only benefit. This is relevant right now, when the banking system has recovered, lending in all segments is growing steadily, and this trend will continue. Lending should be designed to promote sustainable economic growth and prevent societal losses from financing inefficient projects, which means that we will pursue regulatory policies that support marketgrowth and discourage practices that accumulate these risks. What practices are we talking about in the first place? First. We have already taken and will continue to take additional measures to demonetize banks' balance sheets. It is necessary to further reduce currency risk in the system as a whole. Second. The predominance of secured lending, in our opinion, creates risks that too large a volume of non-core or problem assets will accumulate on the balance sheets of banks. The fund of non-core assets that we are now creating,with a volume of about 2 trillion rubles, is a direct consequence of such a problem. When bank lending becomes pawnshop, banks, in fact, do not care who to lend to. Banks do not analyze the economic activities of the borrower - there would be collateral. As a result, access to creditditu is not received by the most competitive projects. And therefore, the collateral reform that we are discussing now, aims to reduce the share of pawnshop lending and will naturally stimulate lending to quality projects. And this is our obviouspriority. The third is the fight against lending to the business of bank owners. We have been waging this struggle for a long time and will continue. The time of pocket banks, which are unable to make any contribution to economic growth, is passing. Fourth. It's a risky situation when loans are issued not to operating enterprises, but to holdings. Or when the credit burden of changing ownership is hung on the enterprise itself, which must then "work out" its own sale. Such loans do not help, but on the contrary, they worsen the situation of enterprises, increase the debt burden, and the loan itself does not go to business development. By the way, this is why almost all assets, Which we received in the Fund of Non-Core Assets, excessively over-indebted: they changed the owner more than once and each change of ownership was accompanied by an increase in the debt burden. This vicious circle for the economy we must also break. Fifth. With the development of the financial market, the interconnection of financial organizations in its various segments, both regulated and unregulated: banks, insurance companies, pension funds, professional participants in the securities market, leasing companies, is increasing. They form groups, sometimes with formalized ownership relations, but often simply at the expense of stable informal businesses. c-links. Unscrupulous players use regulatory arbitrage both between sectors and between financial institutions of the same segment. Cross-investments, hidden financial support for organizations in one sector by another, transfer of risks, transactions in the centerof concealment from the regulator of real sources of financing or real investment objects, the use of confidence in the bank for mass sales of risky non-bank products - we also intend to eradicate this practice. There are several ways. Thisincludes the protection of banking and non-banking regulation in order to eliminate regulatory arbitrage, and the accelerated integration of supervision over the banking and non-banking sectors, the development of meaningful approaches and the practice of motivated judgment of the regulator. Taking into accountthe lessons of financial recovery, especially last year's ones, we intend to revise the concept of supervision over banking and financial holdings.
