For example, if the supervision and interim administration had powers over the entire Otkritie holding, and not onlyto the bank, it would be much easier to find and return the funds withdrawn through the holding, namely through the holding. Sixth. Fair value, exchange pricing, prevention of market manipulation. A separate block of issues that are now becoming more and more relevant is related to the correctness of the formation of exchange prices for traded securities. We see examples of price manipulation, and sublimation of the value of shares, and incorrect market making, transactions by agreement through the exchange ... And all of this means that there is an abuse of market mechanisms. And of course, we need to take certain measures here, because formally transactions look market-based, the price looks market-based, but it is not. And another problemis the high concentration of credit risk per borrower or a group of related persons. We have a corresponding standard, the well-known H6, which banks also sometimes skillfully resist. Many banks genuinely still believe that it is better to be the main or only creditor of a particular enterprise. And in fact, of course, the high concentration of risk per borrower, combined with its high debt burden, threatens the stability of the banks themselves. And in such a situation, the bank is alreadya hostage of the client. It is forced to agree to numerous restructurings. refuse the possibility of collecting pledges or using guarantees. Therefore, this year we will discuss with banks a revision of the approaches to risk concentration interms of identifying related parties and calculating the H6 ratio. The development of syndicated lending, and the legislative framework for this has already been created, the continued consolidation of the banking sector are, in our opinion, the right ways to reducethis serious risk and increase the resilience of banks. And the latter on the topic of regulatory development. We are well aware that that amplification of regulation at the international level, and the increase in regulation with national characteristics that is taking place, is, of course, a cost for banks. But in order to reduce the risks of the stability of the financial system, to get rid of accumulated problems, we have to do this. And we, of course, would like to stop engaging in "petty", "point" regulation, constantly from covering one or another loophole in the regulatory framework for unscrupulous bankers. Because the costs of closing loopholes in this way are borne by bona fide market participants. But this, in our opinion, will not be possible as long as the responsibility for violations in the financial market remains low, as long as unscrupulous bankers know that in case of anything they can hide abroad, and, as I have already said, retain their non-bank assets. For example, during the four-year period of the criminal article forthe falsification of reporting, only 4 people have been brought to justice. 30 criminal cases have been initiated. Therefore, we initiated amendments, which will make this article more effective. And the second is the right of professional judgment for the regulator, for the Bank of Russia, for making supervisory decisions. We have been raising this issue for several years and understand that without the right of professional judgment, we will always be in a catching-up mode: we must formally prove any violation,naturally, and all the time we will be in catching up mode. Unscrupulous players come up with a new trick, we "plug" this loophole, increase the costs of regulation for bona fide participants, all this is repeated again and again. Supervision, of course, will be quickand the damage to customers and society as a whole will be less if we have the right of reasoned judgment. Increasing the responsibility of owners and managers, the right of professional judgment, in our opinion, will lead to a reduction in costsassociated with regulation and supervision, and to the creation of conditions for real, advisory supervision and the formation of partnerships between the regulator and bona fide banks. I would like to turn from regulation literally briefly to another important topic: the competitionin the banking sector. It will be in the focus of attention of the Bank of Russia. But I would like to note that we are convinced that the quality of competition does not depend directly on the number of banks. Yes, a large number of banks were deprived of their licenses, but all of them are significantly deprived of their licenses. They were competitive, engaged in illegal operations, lending mainly to their own owners, attracting funds from depositors and creditors at inflated rates. This work is not yet fully completed, but it can already be said that mostof the banks operating today are working honestly and comply with the established rules. Playing by the rules is the basis of fair competition. It is important that market competition works within different categories of banks and financial institutions. So banks and financialinstitutions have to, of course, find their niches. It's hard for a small bank to compete with the biggest players without any support. And it is for the development of competition that the Bank of Russia has developed the concept of proportional regulation. Let me remind you that the 18th year is thetransition to a basic license for banks with a capital of less than 1 billion rubles. 150 of them announced their intention to switch to a basic license). But I want to note, all their combined assets are only about 1% of the assets of the banking system, they're really small banks. We will support the institution of small regional banks, since it is these credit institutions that can most effectively serve such an important segment for the economy as individualentrepreneurs and small businesses. Significant simplification of regulation and reporting for banks with a basic license is done precisely so that they can focus on this business segment. Further. Our actions in the field of financial recoveryare also aimed at improving the competitive field in the banking sector. The presence until recently among systemically important banks of organizations with chronic shortages of capital (almost with loss of capital) and liquidity not only disrupted competitivecompetition, but also significantly weakened the banking system. Since last summer, the Bank of Russia has applied a new reorganization mechanism to large banks, entering operational management for a very short period of time and temporarily becoming (I emphasize, temporarily) theircon trolling shareholder. Today we can say with confidence that the new reorganization mechanism allows in the shortest possible time (6 months, and not 10-15 years, as it was before) to improve even a large, systemically important bank for the entire economy or for the region or financial And to do so without the risk of destabilizing the financial system. Currently, all three major banks that we have taken out for recovery with the help of the Consolidation Fund have already been fully capitalized and continue to serve their customers. Inorder to ensure business continuity, recapitalization, restructuring of non-core and problem assets, strategies for the development of these banking groups have been developed, taking into account their capabilities and role for the economy. Thus, most of this difficult work to improve the health of the largest players in our banking system can also be considered completed. The Bank of Russia aims to maximize the return of funds that were allocated for financial recovery. And not only through the sale of the bank and work with industrialand non-core assets, we have repeatedly talked about this, but also by forcing the former owners to cover losses and return the withdrawn assets. Currently, the only mechanism provided for by law for the recovery of damage by the state in the financial recovery of banks is the mechanism of judicial recovery. We have proposed and are proposing a mechanism for subsidiary liability. So far, we have not met with understanding in this matter, but we will continue to convince our colleagues. Acting within the frameworkof the existing legal field, the Bank of Russia will continue towork with claims with former owners. Along with the possibility of recovering damages during reorganization (it is the other day that legislative changes come into force on the procedure for calculating such losses), we propose to discuss two additional mechanisms: - the first is a mechanism for blocking assets for the amount of claims of the Bank of Russia for the duration of litigation, litigation (so that assets are not withdrawn or liquidated during long courtproceedings); - and secondly, to implement an initiative to block the departure abroad of owners and top management of banks being rehabilitated (until the end of court proceedings). Unfortunately, the flight of financiers abroad and their reunification there withthe assets withdrawn in advance continues. But of course, I would like to conclude the banking part of my speech on a more major note. Although we have to talk about the unpleasant things that exist and with which we will work, and I consider it honest to say ba ba. What exactly are we going to do. But, fortunately, there are grounds for major notes too. Because, as I have already said, the banking sector is stable, developing, good profits, capital, liquidity, all opportunities For the development of lending, which is growing. And we really believe that as a result of the work to clean up the banking system, the bulk of unscrupulous banks have already been withdrawn from the market. And therefore we now have the opportunity, on the one hand, to expect thatthere will be fewer insured events for the insurance system, and on the other hand, it is possible to expand the capabilities of the deposit insurance system, since we are practically getting out of the situation. which many banks have told us about, when good banks are forced to pay for unscrupulousones. We consider it possible to expand the deposit insurance system in order to maintain the confidence of both citizens and businesses in banks. We consider it necessary to accelerate the adoption of the draft law on the extension of insurance to small businesses, it is now inthe State Duma. And as for individuals, we consider it expedient to increase the amount of compensation in those situations where the depositor objectively did not have the opportunity to manage risks. Moreover, in socially sensitive situations, and we see this in other situations. When an inheritance is received, an apartment is sold and bought, insurance payments and social benefits are received, the amounts on the account accumulate more than the insured one million four hundred. And here, of course, there is every reason in these cases to prescribe specificcases, to increase the sum insured. These joint proposals have been worked out with the Deposit Insurance Agency. Also, the Deposit Insurance Agency, following the results of an active public discussion of the practice of challenging transactions in the bankruptcyof credit institutions, and such a practice The challenge became sensitive for depositors, proposed changes to the legislation aimed at additional protection of bona fide depositors of banks. Namely, to raise the threshold of the amount within whichoperations for the payment of deposits to citizens in the event of bankruptcy will not mate to 10 million rubles. We support these proposals. And I'm going to move very briefly to other sectors of the financial market, we usually really have a conversation about the banking sector that takes longer. On the non-banking sector. I know that there were productive discussions yesterday, and all these topics will be discussed in detail on the sidelines of the congress. And I would like to talk only about a few general things. How do we see the development of non-credit financial aboutrganovization? This year, the first stage of the implementation of a unified strategy for the development of the financial market is being completed. And tomorrow at the plenary session, we will discuss the main directions for the development of financial markets for the next three-year period. But nevertheless, it is possible to sum up some results. In the past period, we have focused, it was natural, our work on cleaning up the market. There was a large "Clean Register" program, under which we withdrew from the market players who did not conduct real activities, unstable or engaged inillegal operations. We strengthened regulation where it obviously did not correspond to the level of risk. In the system of non-state pension funds, a guarantee of pension savings was introduced. In insurance on the basis of risk-oriented Regulation and supervision were significantly strengthened and measures were taken - special measures to stabilize the situation in OSAGO. In the field of microfinance, proportional regulation was introduced , microcredit and microfinance companies were allocated. We have been and will continue to work on the development of the bond market, and we see, by the way, how it is developing quite dynamically. In general, we are quite confident in the long-term stability of the financial market, its various segments, as well as in the fact that our regulation andour adsor will be able to reduce the risks of a possible proliferation of problems if they appear in individual financial organizations or market sectors. And now, when the situation in the financial market is quite stable, and rates are falling, this means that consumers in search of higher profitability are beginning to be more and more interested in alternative instruments to deposits, and we see this interest. And therefore, in the center of policy for the development of the financial market, of course, should be the consumer, his intermediary. S, rights, protection against excessive risk. Customer focus and trust should become, if you will, the ideological basis for the development of the financial market. In the Main directions of development of the financial market for the next three years, we lay the following priorities. First. This is the development of competition and financial inclusion. On the basis of modern technologies, the infrastructure solutions that we are creating with the market (this is primarily remote identification for consumers of financial services), the availability of financial serviceswill increase. And moreover, competition in the market will increase, as the role of traditional deterrents decreases, for example, such as networks of offices and branches. Marketplace of financial services, the prototype of which we will demonstrate today m, is one of the steps to increase and financial inclusion for customers and expand the possibility of entering new markets for financial organizations. Second. This, of course, is strengthening the atmosphere of trust in the financial market and protecting consumer rights. We wantboth citizens and companies to trust financial institutions. We're going to eradicate unscrupulous sales -misselling that leads to to the disappointment of consumers with the financial market, for this purpose we are building behavioral supervision, so that citizens would not bedisappointed that they have entered the financial market, the products that they have purchased. We will also expand the use of the institution of business reputation, increase the personal responsibility of management. The immediate task is to create alternatives. And the mechanism for resolving disputes between consumers and financial institutions: you know that just recently a law was adopted on the establishment of the institution of a financial commissioner. I have to say that what's important to build trust is the standards ofdoing things, the best business rules that all market participants adhere to, and that's where self-regulatory organizations play a very important role. It's the self-regulatory organizationsthat are participating, actively promoting those standards, and will have to be responsible for their compliance with them by their members. And, as I draw to the end of my statement, I would like to say a few important and difficult things for us. Every year at the FinancialOngress, we try to give you, the market, as complete information as possible about how we assess the situation, how and why we determine priorities, about the innovations that we plan to implement. Theoretically, my speeches should become shorter every year, because regulation should be stable, the pace of innovation must necessarily decrease. But there are several topics that which we have repeated repeatedly, both a year and two years ago, but their implementation, unfortunately, has been delayed. And I've repeated them again, andI've said it again, and I'd like to assure you that we're going to finish the unfinished business. I have already mentioned many of them. I will add only about the introduction of individual pension capital. It is critically important both for future pensioners and for the economy. We have worked a lot on this system, we are confident in its viability and will continue to work with the Government, with legislators for its adoption in the near future. I want to wish you that the work at the congress will be interesting, that you will benefit from the discussions and preferably, of course, an optimistic attitude, despite the problems that we are talking about, which are what we need to talk about, in order to move forward to remove these problems. Despite these problems, we certainly have every reason to do so. Tobe optimistic about the development of the financial sector and the role of the financial sector in the development of the economy. We have come a long way in overcoming difficulties. And now, of course, is the time to make an increasing contribution of the financial industry to the development of the economy, to increasing its growth rate. I want to thank you for your attention and almost immediately, without interruption, proceed to our panel session.

Title: Speech at the Plenary Session of the State Duma of the Russian Federation: Annual Report of the Bank of Russia
text: Speech by Bank of Russia Governor Elvira Nabiullina at the Plenary Session of the State Duma of the Russian Federation: Annual Report of the Bank of Russia June 19, 2018 Good afternoon, dear deputies! Today, I am reporting on the results of our work last year. It is very important for us that the Duma regularly and extremely constructively interacts with us, is attentive to our activities. Only as part of the consideration of the report, we received almost 100 questions from factions. And before today's plenary session, five meetings of the working group were held, a joint meeting of the relevant committees. I know you have already read the full report on our activities, so today I would like to focus only on those issues of our activity that are of social importance, and those that are particularly important for the implementation of the key task of the financial system - providing financial resources for economic growth. I would like to start with our monetary policy. As you know, over the past few years, the Bank of Russia has pursued a policy of combating inflation. Let me remind you that at the beginning of 2015, inflation wasabout 17%. And this was a real threat to both the well-being of citizens and enterprises. We pursued a policy of achieving the inflation target of 4%. This is the level that is suitable for our economy, protects the wallets of citizens, gives business the opportunity to plan, contributes to improving the efficiency of enterprises, because with low inflation, it is no longer possible to shift the growing costs of production into a price for consumers. Last year we reached the target, and we've been living with inflation near the target for almost a yearnow. In the years that follow, our policy should be no less prudent, because we have to keep inflation low, we have to anchor people's confidence. in the future. And it's not that simple. This does not happen automatically. Inflation is affected by inflationexpectations, and inflation expectations are affected by the structure of inflation. Thus, the rise in gasoline prices (we expect that the Government's decisions will stabilize the situation), the rise in prices for housing and communal services, even with low figures of general inflation, fuel inflation expectations. These are sensitivefactors. The increase in VAT will add, according to our estimates, about 1 percentage point to inflation. But I must say that now, when inflation is at the level of 2.5%, we will be able, with a high probability, quite calmly pass the moments of changing the VAT rate from thepoint of view of fulfilling obligations to society to keep inflation at 4%. According to our forecast, inflation can only temporarily rise slightly above the target - to 4.5% next year - and then return to 4%. We have always taken into account and will continue to take into accountthe capabilities of the economy in our policy, we are striving to act in such a way as not to have a negative impact on economic growth, on the contrary, to create conditions for it. And the economy has already grown at a rate close to potential. Interest rates on bankloans are consistently decreasing, and the volume of volumes lending is growing (over the past 12 months, the growth of lending to companies amounted to 4.3%, and to individuals - 18.3%). Rates on loans to corporate borrowers decreased from 11.3 to 8.5% on average, on loans to individuals - from 15.3 to 13.3%, mortgage rates - from 11.4 to 9.57%. I would like to emphasize in particular that the growth in loans,which is now taking place, would not have been possible if the banking system had not been cleansed of weak and unscrupulous players. This is probably the most painful and difficult area of our work for several years. We've withdrawn quite a few licenses: about 50 last year and 28 banks this year. We've had to allocate substantial amounts of money for capital and liquidity by reorganizing banks. But this work is yielding results. Weak banks simply could not increase lending and could not withstandall sorts of unfavorable external events. In cleaning up the banking system, we have already passed most of the way and last year, probably, we went through the most difficult part of it. We had to sanitize three large banking groups. The necessary (in order to solve the problems of large banks) new law on reorganization was adopted last summer, and in less than 2 months we first applied it to Otkritie, then about a month later - BINBANK and at the end of the year - Promsvyazbank. I would also liketo express my gratitude to the deputies for adopting the law on reorganization. Without it, solving the problems of large banks would have cost both society and the financial system much more. All three groups are large groups, they included non-state pension funds, a largeinsurance company, and other banks. They work both in the real sector and with the population. integrated with other financial institutions. And the reorganization allowed us to protect millions of citizens (8 million citizens, customers of these banks) and hundreds of thousands (5,63 thousand) enterprises from losses. I want to say for the future that we will rarely apply reorganization: only for those banks that are large, have systemic importance for the federal and regional markets. We expect to return most of the allocated funds as a resultof working with assets, selling them, working with non-core assets and returning liquidity on schedule, as well as selling the combined bank. Still, it's a very large amount, it's the price of unscrupulous and irresponsible behavior by the ownerswho control the banks. And the controlling owners, like the owners of many of the banks that we revoked their licenses, are not just at large, they're left with their assets unrelated to the banking business. It would be fair if they paid their bills. And we are counting on the help of deputies here in preventing the possibility for bankers to dispose of other people's money so irresponsibly (and banks are the disposal of other people's money). We look forward to your support with regard to the introduction of the subsidiary the responsibility of the owners and for the owners of banks (that is, that they respond with all their assets, and not only those on the bank's balance sheet), the seizure of assets at moments when banks are experiencing difficulties, restrictions on travel abroad for owners who led their bank to collapse and increased criminal liability for falsification of reports. The health of the banking system is a critical condition for the banking system to become a pillar of economic development, but, alas, itis not static. For many years, banks earned on activities that did not bring much real benefit to the economy. This is the financing of mergers and acquisitions, that is, the redistribution of property, this is collateral lending without a normal analysis of the borrower's economic activities - that is, the bank often thought not about the repayment of the loan, how the enterprise that took the loan would work, but about the fact that in extreme cases it would become the owner of the collateral, the owner of these enterprises. At the same time, financing the business of the owners of the bank themselves. We will continue to fight this, because this lending is ultimately at the expense of bank customers. To solve these problems, in addition to strengthening supervision, we are beginning to introducestimulating regulation: requirements that make unprofitable for banks those activities, for example, which I mentioned (they also include dollar lending), and on the contrary, increase interest in lending to enterprises of the real sector, project financing, small and medium-sized businesses. The key innovation here, of course, is the transition to a new model of the banking system - a three-tier one: based on the legislation on proportional regulation that you adopted last year, and we discussed this law a lot last year. The key goal is to create conditions for regional banks to lend to small and medium-sized businesses. This year is transitional. About a third of the banks, all the banks that exist, we believe, will work on a basic license, lending primarily to small businesses. For them, it will be easier to regulate and less accountable. For us, banks with a basic license are a very important type of bank. We are confident that as a result of these changes we will have an effective and useful for the economy, fora small number of people. and medium-sized business-class banks. Now about our work as a mega-regulator for the development of the financial market as a whole. We regulate the activities of about 13,000 market entities: insurance companies, non-state pension funds, mutual investment funds, microfinance organizations, pawnshops, credit consumer cooperatives, professional market participants, rating agencies. Each of these markets is small relative to the banking system, each of them is several times smaller, if not by orders of magnitude, but they are beginning to play an increasingly important role in the economy. As sources of long-term money, as sources of alternative banking instruments for placing funds of citizens and businesses, obtaining loans, and so on. We have worked to create an adequateregulatory and supervisory environment in each of these markets. As a result, we have a fairly healthy system at the moment in terms of the sustainability of business models. Of course, there are problems in each segment, there are problems, but in general, each segment is reliably stable. Now we are formulating for ourselves two key tasks in the financial market. The first is that, as in the banking sector, we are working to ensure that the resources that financial institutions have (and they do) are directed to the real sector of the economy. And the second direction is the protection of consumer rights and the development of financial inclusion, the development of financial literacy. A citizen should be able to get the financial product he needs anywhere, regardless of whether where he lives, and at the same time receive adequate, understandable information about the risks of this product, and about his responsibility, to have every opportunity to protect his interests if the financial service provider behaved in bad faith. I'll start with the first task: financingthe real sector. The key market, primarily for the development of long-term money in the economy, is the pension savings market. The assets of pension funds amount to almost 3.9 trillion rubles. Our task is to ensure that these large funds are transformed into long-term investments. We have consistently changed the regulation in such a way that non-state pension funds have more incentives to invest in the real sector. As a result, over the past two years, investments in the real sector in the portfolio of pension savings have almost doubled , from 530 billion to 958 billion rubles. And we will work on how to to reinforce this trend. We still believe that it is necessary to develop pension savings, to create a convenient system of deductions for citizens for theirown future pension. Pension savings for people are a guarantee of maintaining the quality of life after retirement, and for the economy - the development of long-term financing. Therefore, we will continue to promote the developed concept of individual ioncapital. We will continue to support the development of the bond market (its growth last year was about 20%, this is a dynamically developing sector; bonds are becoming a convenient way for enterprises to attract resources), as well as life insuranceand other forms of development of long money in the economy. On the basis of reducing inflation - consistently low inflation - our task as a mega-regulator is to create a source of long money for the economy. so that financial institutions work for the growth of the economy. The second task is to protect consumer rights and increase financial inclusion. I will start with the insurance market, the most popular product is OSAGO. And here because of In recent years, we have had to solve the most acute problems of the imbalance of the system as a whole: to fight for access toOSAGO policies (there were big problems with this), to change tariffs so that imbalances in the OSAGO system do not lead to paralysis of this market in certain regions. So, in 2017, electronic OSAGO was launched. This increases the availability of policies for grazhdan (insurance companies did not want to sell OSAGO in offices in unprofitable regions, it is no longer possible to refuse to sell through the site). In total, in 2017, more than 7.8 million electronic contracts were concluded (about 20% of the total number of OSAGO contracts), now electronicMTPL is already 25%, that is, the share of electronic OSAGO is growing. Also in 2017, preferential in-kind compensation for harm in OSAGO (that is, repair) was introduced. I remember how many discussions and disputes there were on this topic - in our opinion, this is important. Thisundermines the opportunities for fraudulent business of auto lawyers. Under the new contracts, already 15-20% of the reimbursement takes place in kind. We will carefully monitor that there are no complaints from citizens about the quality of repairs. But I can still call the situation with OSAGOstable. The main share of complaints about OSAGO now is the bonus-malus coefficient. And we propose to change this coefficient. We make it simple and understandable for car owners. We have also developed proposals to increase the flexibility of OSAGO tariffs,extending the policy price corridor by 20% down and up. In order to fairly take into account the characteristics of the risks of each driver, it is proposed to introduce 50 categories of drivers (now there are 5) according to the ratio of various criteria: length of service, age, accident rate, and so on. That is, every driver will be able to count on the most a fair price for yourself, and the tariffs for careful drivers, responsible drivers will not include the risks of drivers who often get into accidents. Increasing the flexibility of tariffs will lead to increased competition in this market - even in difficult regions, companies that refused and still refuse to work there will come, and consumers will first get greater availability of policies, and in the future, as a result of increased competition, andbetter price conditions. We are ready to discuss the parameters of the proposed changes with deputies, at our preliminary discussions there were many questions on this topic. And we are really open to dialogue here, we believe that such changes are overdue. Now aboutmicro-finance. Microfinance organizations are not such a large segment in terms of assets, more than 700 times less than the banking segment (about 113 billion rubles at the end of 2017), but microfinance services are of social importance. People should be able to makeshort small loans, there are different situations in life. Two years ago, we made a decision to combat usurious interest. The necessary restrictive measures have been taken. Debt burden limiters for citizens have been earned, and we,in our opinion, are already ready to further lower this bar and these restrictions. Now changes to the legislation are being discussed. Tightening the requirements for legal ones, we must ensure that people do not find themselves in the clutches of illegal creditbuildings. We are working together with the Prosecutor General's Office. and law enforcement. In 2017, 1344 illegal lenders were identified, and already in the first quarter of 2018, due to improving the efficiency of work to identify such creditors, about 1300. Now for another hot topic. Affordability in sparsely populated, remote locations. At almost every meeting of ours, it is raised by deputies. In our country, almost one-fifth of people live in settlements with fewer than 3,000 inhabitants. It is economically inefficient for banks to keep offices in such settlements, to maintain ATMs, but people should not be cut off from financial services. To coordinate work to improve the availability of financial services, the Bank of Russia has created a working group, which also includes the largest state-owned banks with a large branch network in the regions. A cooperation agreement has been concluded with a major operator of satellite Internet access, negotiations are underway with other operators. And a pilot projectto increase financial inclusion is now starting in the Far Eastern Federal District. where this situation is particularly acute. The main opportunities to support financial inclusion in sparsely populated areas are also related to the development of financial services based on the infrastructure of the Russian Post. Russian Post has over 42 thousand branches, and by the end of 2018, Russian Post expects to open 18 thousand points of presence of financial services. This is something that concerns the availability of services. We also have a special working groupto increase the availability of services for people with disabilities, people with limited mobility - this is also a vulnerable group of citizens, and we are working to ensure that banks do not discriminate against these groups of the population to receive financial services. Now briefly about protecting the rights of citizens. For several years now, the Bank of Russia has been actively working with the population: the Bank of Russia's reception offices are also working, you can file a complaint via the Internet, call the call center. And we look at what complaints we receive in order to respond more quickly to the most painful topics. We see that one of the most basic topics is the imposition of unnecessary and too risky products on citizens. when they take advantage of the low financial literacy of our citizens. In addition to the imposed sales, primarily for insurance, other products are also sold inthe banks' offices under the guise of bank deposits - bills of exchange, life insurance policies, and other products are also imposed. We would like to discuss with you a rather tough measure - we propose to prohibit the sale of bills to individuals. There was a lot of deception here. Speaking about the protection of rights, I would like to mention the deposit insurance system. You also raised this issue, and we support the expansion of the insurance system to small businesses, and we believe that it would be good to accelerate the adoptionof this law. But we also need to consider the possibility of extending insurance to charitable organizations, social organizations. And also to increase the amount of insurance compensation is proposed to 10 million rubles in some cases, when and citizens objectively could not manage risks by placing their funds. This applies to funds from the sale of real estate, a number of insurance payments, social benefits and some others. And we hope that these proposals, which we discussed together with the DIA, will besupported. And increasing financial inclusion should go in parallel with improving financial literacy. We are building a separate system of behavioral supervision that protects citizens when the company deliberately acts not in the interests of the client. Andwhether a person chooses the right model of financial behavior, whether he becomes an easy victim of scammers - depends largely on financial literacy. We are doing a lot of work together here. with the Ministry of Education, we introduce relevant courses in theprogram of educational institutions, hold events for older people; a special category - pupils of orphanages who leave orphanages and do not understand the risks of financial life; people with disabilities and many others. Last year we launchedeither the portal on financial literacy "Financial Culture", and our territorial divisions are very actively working in the regions to improve the financial situation. Literacy. And A few words in conclusion, I would like to say a few words about the development of the national payment system. Mir cards issued so far are 37 million cards. And it is very important for us that not only the number of cards issued is growing, but also the volume of non-cash transactions with the help of Mir is growing. This means that people use this card. And we do everything, that it is competitive and convenient. Last year, the transfer of public sector workers and pensioners to the Mir card was started. More than 95% of those who used the Mir card (because a person has a choice - to use the card or receive cash), who used the card of international payment systems, 95% have already switched to the Mir card. For pensioners, this will happen in the new order, when the previous card expires, expires, it happens free of charge for pensioners. And once again I want to emphasize that our activities to fulfill the tasks defined by law (maintaining financial and price stability, developing the national payment system) are all aimed at supporting our economy andimproving our well-being. Thank you for your attention! Photo on preview: Vyacheslav Prokofiev / TASS

Title: Bank of Russia Governor spoke at the plenary session of the State Duma
text: Bank of Russia Governor Elvira Nabiullina spoke at the plenary session of the State Duma November 21, 2018 Performance Dear Vyacheslav Viktorovich, dear deputies! Today I present the Main Directions of the Unified State Monetary Policy for 2019 and the period of 2020 and 2021. The draft document was first submitted to the Duma on October 1, andwas drafted with MPs and experts. As a result, a number of additions were made to the Main Directions, you can see them in the final version of the document. This document defines our vision of the development of the situation in the economy, our forecast for inflation and approaches to the conduct of policy. budget and state economic policy in general, which are laid down in the presidential decrees, the Government's plans, and the three-year budget. I will start with the current situation in the economy, the challenges that monetary policy is responding to, and then move on to the forecast. Now the economy is growing at a rate, in our opinion, close to potential. According to our estimates, this year the growth will be 1.5-2%. Of course, a country like ours cannot be satisfied with this growth rate. Today, all of us - the Government, the Bank of Russia, the parliament, business, and Russian society as a whole - must do a lot of work to increase the pace of labour productivity, potential growth. The Central Bank has developed measuresfor the development of the financial market, which will be presented in the Guidelines for the Development of the Financial Market for the next three years. We believe that taking into account all these measures, GDP growth may accelerate to 3% in 2021. What should be the monetary policy in suchconditions? Low inflation is still a policy priority. Under the current conditions - and this is historically the lowest level of unemployment, growth rates close to potential - monetary policy alone cannot lead to asustainable acceleration of economic growth. There should be no illusions about this. Moreover, the measures to stimulate growth that the Government proposes will be effective, including the growth of long-term, primarily private, investments, and willwork to the fullest extent only with consistently low inflation. There can be no long-term investments, as well as available long-term loans in national currency, with high inflation. And this means that in the current phase of the economic cycle,the goal of our monetary policy remains unchanged - inflation is close to 4% constantly. As you know, inflation has been near 4% or below the target for only about a year and a half. Lending is growing, rates, especially long-term rates, are gradually decreasingbehind inflation and inflation expectations. For ten months of this year, lending to enterprises grew by 5.9%, more than twice as high as in the 10 months of last year. High growth rates of lending to individuals remain ( 18.7% against 9.8% in January-October 2017). Mortgage for 10 months increased by 17.4% (let me remind you, for the same period last year - by less than 10%). In recent months, rates have risen slightly, including reacting to the increase in the key rate. At the same time, the growth of lending continues, that is, rates on average remain at a comfortable level for borrowers. And the increase in deposit rates that occurred made them attractive again for the population, after the decline in August and September, deposits began to grow again - in octoberthey increased by 0.6 percentage points. We can say that now the situation is quite balanced relatively, on the one hand, the interests of borrowers, on the other hand, depositors of banks. It is no coincidence that I drew your attention to the dynamics of lending, because we still often hear the call to lower the rate, concerns about how our policy will affect lending, whether it is too tight. Both the current dynamics and our experience during the four years that we have been living in the mode of inflationarytargeting, or inflation targeting, show that rates are steadily decreasing precisely after the decline in inflation. And exactly the same is shown by the experience of others. these are far from isolated examples. By the way, countries that use inflation targeting account for more than two-thirds of global GDP. These countries are successfully achieving a steady decline in inflation. Moreover, real interest rates in these countries are declining after the introduction of inflation targeting. We believe that the policyof keeping inflation low for the long term is also the policy of ensuring the availability of credit, and we can also see this in comparison with other countries. Monetary policy cannot compensate for internal structural constraints, but a clear and predictable monetary policy that ensures low inflation, and at the same time the availability of tools that ensure the maintenance of financial stability, help reduce the sensitivity of the economy to external shocks. And for us, this is about It's important. And today it is even more important than in previous years. We need to carry out transformations, move to a new growth model under unfavorable external conditions, with high uncertainty. What external risks we are dealing with now and how should wetake these external risks into account in our policies? First. Risks associated with oil. Our economy is still dependent on the price of oil. The most important tool for stabilization here, of course, is a floating exchange rate. A floating exchange rate allows the financial system and the economy to adapt and function normally at different levels of oil prices. However, we know from experience that risks are created not only by changes in prices themselves, but also by the fact that when this happens abruptly, itcauses volatility in financial markets as a whole. This requires us to be on the alert and be conservative in our predictions, which we consider justified. Until recently, some called our baseline scenario too conservative. But the high price levels that we saw in the middle of this year have really only lasted a few months. And in recent weeks, the price of oil has fallen sharply, at some point approaching the lows of 2018. At the same time, I want to note that although oil is still a significant risk factor that we are closely monitoring, but still - and our calculations show this - now the Russian economy has become much less sensitive to fluctuations in oil. Conditions. And above all, thanks to the budget rulesof the u. Second. What are the external risks? These are the risks associated with the so-called normalization of US monetary policy and its impact on the situation in emerging markets. The massive inflows of capital that have occurred in the past years in the world, whendeveloped countries have pursued unprecedentedly soft policies, may be replaced by a period of equally significant and prolonged capital outflows. And, as history shows, it is the emerging market countries that can suffer from them first. An important newsource of problems this year has been the escalation of foreign trade tensions between the United States and China and a number of other countries. The introduction of mutual protectionist barriers by the largest economies negatively affects global trade and poses threats to sustainableglobal growth. At the same time, serious bursts of market volatility, a fall in stock markets, with especially unfavorable development - the transition from trade to currency wars are not excluded. This year, we've already seen a number of examples where a combination ofexternal and domestic economic and political factors has led to a major spike in problems in individual countries that has spread to emerging markets as a whole. And by the way, it's worth noting that one of the key causes of instability in these countries in these cases was doubting that the central banks of these countries are capable of independently pursuing prudent monetary policy and standing guard over. persistently low inflation. Countries with large accumulated debts, current-account deficits, and inconsistent monetary and fiscal policies are more vulnerable. Therefore, when looking at other people's experiences, we must pursue responsible policies in terms of both fiscal spending, fiscal policy, and monetary conditions. The third is the risks associatedwith sanctions. Sanctions themselves, as we have seen in previous years, cause negative but time-limited effects. Ultimately, they are also affected by sanctions. Sanctions themselves, as we have seen in previous years, have negative but time-limited effects. Ultimately, they are also affected by them. the financial system and the economy are adapting. In the context of uncertainty about the future sanctions regime, we must have the entire set of tools that allow us to maintain financial stability and, depending on the situation, be ready for a real increase in sanctions pressure and for market nervousness in case of bad expectations. So, let me remind you, in September westopped buying foreign currency within the framework of the budget rule precisely in response to a sharp jump in the volatility of Russian financial markets. With this decision, the stabilization of both the OFZ market and the foreign exchange market confirmed the justification of our step. Taking into account external factors and such internal factors as the increase in VAT, the balance of risks for the economy and inflation is now shifted towards proinflationary risks. This means that monetary policy should remain somewhat tighter than ifthese risks did not exist. At the same time, the choice of specific steps in the field of monetary policy will be carried out taking into account the actual implementation of certain risks and their impact. on inflation expectations. Now directly about the forecast scenariosof the Fundamental Directions of Monetary Policy Policy. We consider three scenarios: - Basic - which implies a decrease in the price of oil to 55 per barrel. in 2020. - The scenario with unchanged oil prices is on average at the level of 75 per barrel. Here I would like to note thatin the Main Directions it was called a scenario with constant prices, but in connection with the latest dynamics it can be called a scenario with high prices. - And a risky scenario. In the baseline scenario , the Bank of Russia expects annual inflation to accelerate to 5-5.5% in 2019 and return to our target near 4% in 2020. The reasons for the acceleration of inflation are the accumulated weakening of the ruble and the increase in VAT. Our estimate of the contribution of the VAT increase to annual inflation is 1 percentage point, but we understand that the range of estimates is very wide and will depend on the specific situation; we estimate it from 0.6 to 1.5%. Gdp growth, according to our estimates, next year may slow down to 1.2-1.7% as a result of the imposition of effects from both lower oil prices and the increase in VAT. But the latter, we believe, will have a short-term restraining effect and in the second half of the year will be compensated by an increase in investment demand from the public sector. In the future, GDP growth will accelerate, youwill be able to see our forecast figures. In the scenario with oil prices at the level of 75 / barp. - this scenario differs slightly from the baseline scenario in terms of inflation forecasts and GDP growth, which is primarily explained by the budget rule, which smoothes outthe impact on the economy of the situation on the oil market. And here the inflation trajectory is close to the baseline scenario, although GDP growth rates will be slightly higher in 2019, at oil prices of 75/barrel. will be 1.5-2.0%. In the processof preparing the Main Directions, the Bank of Russia also calculated the risk scenario. It includes a significant outflow of capital in 2019 due to a possible strengthening. sanctions and/or capital outflows from emerging markets. Also, we calculated this risk scenario when the price of oil falls to 35 per barrel. This does not mean that we consider this scenario likely, but we must understand how the situation will develop in a negative case, how we should react to this situation. And, according to our assessment, in this scenario a recession is likely in 2019, but already in 2020. according to our estimates, the economy will again move to growth, and in 2021 the growth rate will already be comparable to the level of the baseline scenario. There may be a short-term surge in inflation to double-digit levels, the need to tighten monetary policy, but this will also be a short-term effect, and we have the tools to cope with this. And a few words about the important. Usually at meetings you always ask a question about the regional aspect of our work and ourmonetary policy. We are paying special attention to this issue now both when preparing the forecast, so that it reflects the processes that are taking place in the regions, and when adopting monetary policy. We want to look not only at the average values in the economy as a whole , but also to understand more deeply the processes in the regions. Now our regional divisions on the ground are increasing analytical competencies. The heads of our main departments in the federal districts always come to Moscow on a week of meetings of the Council of Directorson the rate, report on the situation in the regions. No less, or maybe, and a more important area of regional work is advising the regions on monetary policy issues. Our specialists actively interact with the authorities: they participate in working groups under regional administrations, in many regions there are agreements on information exchange with the Central Bank. After each meeting on the rate, central bank employees hold round tables, seminars with business in the regions. In 2018, such meetings were already held in 25 cities, they were attended by more than six thousand participants from the real, from the financial sector, local authorities, the expert community, universities. We want to be partners for the regions in the development of their economyon the basis of persistently low inflation. And in conclusion, I would like to say that sometimes it may seem that the Central Bank is such a major pessimist in the country. We talk so much about threats, we talk about risks, we talk about uncertainty. We always insist on conservative estimates in forecasts. In fact, of course, we are not pessimists. And of course, we not only believe that our country, our economy is capable of more, but we are also doing everything to make it happen. And part of our work in this, in that the country's economy grew at a high, steady pace and real incomes of the population increased. The well-being of the population , a necessary condition, not sufficient, but absolutely necessary - is financial stability, macroeconomic stability in the countryis not. To give people more confidence in the future, we ourselves always have to remember about the risks. And to have at our disposal all the necessary set of tools in order to maintain financial stability, to return inflation to the goal, to stop the risks of financial stability. Thank you very much for your attention!

Title: Governor of the Bank of Russia spoke at the Congress of the Association of Russian Banks
text: Governor of the Bank of Russia Elvira Nabiullina spoke at the congress Association of Russian Banks April 7, 2016 Performance Video recording of the speech on the official channel of the Bank of Russia in IoiLiYe Dear colleagues! First of all, let me congratulate you on the fact that this year marks the 25th anniversary of the Association of Russian Banks. The Association has done a great job of protecting interests of the banking system and its development. I sincerely congratulate you on this. Thank you for the opportunity to speak at your convention. In my speech, I would like to dwell in more detail on the prospects for the development of the banking system, our approaches to regulation and supervision, but I want to start by assessing the general economic situation and our monetary policy. Because both the prospects of the banking industry and the real sector are largely determined by how the economy is adapts to itsconditions, what external and internal factors affect key economic indicators. The situation in the Russian economy remains difficult, although the worst fears have not been realized. The recession is not over yet, but the economy is already close to the point of stablesilization. And the Bank of Russia expects a slight decline this year, about 1.3-1.5% of GDP, with an oil price of 30 per barrel. If, of course, the price is higher, as it is now, then the decline may be smaller. At the same time, I think it is very importantto emphasize that we should look not only at the rate of economic growth or recession, but at what structural changes are taking place in the economy. Because this is probably the most important thing now - how the economy adapts to new conditions. And we see that here certain positive signals, expected changes in the structure of the Russian economy have begun: there is a shift from the so-called non-tradable sectors to the tradable, especially export-oriented and partly import substitution (agriculture, food industry, chemical industry). This includes the question of what lending priorities for the banking sector may be. That is, all sectors that can take advantage of the new conditions, including a lower ruble exchange rate , associated with the development of exports, non-primary exports, with import substitution. Of course, the pace of structural shifts is still low, which is hampered by low investment activity and insufficient mobility in the labor market. Financial Markets In the financialmarkets, the situation is now much more stable than in 2014-2015 and in January of this year. Volatility has decreased, the prices of financial assets have increased. In addition to global factors, this was facilitated by the policy of a floating exchange rate, adjustingthe balance of payments to low oil prices. Under these conditions, the conditions of structural changes in the Russian economy, the monetary policy of the Central Bank is aimed primarily at reducing inflation, which rose sharply last year due to the large-scalefall in oil prices and the objectively subsequent depreciation of the ruble. Of course, we took measures to reduce inflation, taking into account their impact on economic growth and on financial stability. Some progress has been made here. Inflationfell from almost 17% in March last year to 7.3% in March of this year in annual terms, that is, more than 2 times. Therefore, I consider it absolutely inappropriate now to talk about the fact that we allegedly have stagflation. But of course, this does not guarantee us a furtherdecline in inflation. This is due to the fact that in the decline in inflation in recent years, the role of one-time favorable factors, such as lower world food prices, a good harvest of vegetables and potatoes in Russia last year, as well as the strengtheningof the ruble, has been significant. Since inflation risks remain, at the last meeting of the Board of Directors, we kept the key rate at 11%. Among the inflation risks, I would pay special attention to those related to the budget. I think Anton Germanovich will talk about this in more detail. I want to say that if the balance of payments has practically adapted to low oil prices, then the budget policy, the budget system has not yet fully adapted to the fall in oil and gas revenues. The reserve backgroundallows us to finance the increased budget deficit, however, in our opinion, it is urgently needed to develop a program that would balance the budget system in the medium term. Without this, the budget will be a source of risks for both the economy and monetary policy. The Bank of Russia believes that achieving the 4 percent inflation target in 2017 is not only absolutely real, but also simply necessary. In addition to the social effect (let me remind you that inflation is primarily a "tax on the poor" , on those who receive low incomes), low inflation at the level of 4% will reduce investment risks for business, contribute to greater stability of the exchange rate, reduce risks and risk premiums. Why? As a rule, along with a decrease in inflation, lower There are risks to financial stability, since in conditions of low inflation the exchange rate is more stable, it is not subject to large fluctuations following inflation. Therefore, risk premiums are reduced, and it is easier to calculate business projects and build long-term plans for business development. I want to say that keeping the key rate unchanged for a long time, although there have been many questions about this, brings a positive result (and not only in reducing inflation), which we are now seeing. Market participants' confidence that inflation will decline in the future is gradually growing. And we see this in the data on the behavior of interest rates. We see that rates on long-term loans are now falling faster than on short-term loans, even ifour key rate is unchanged. Because economic entities are laying down on the fact that inflation will gradually decline. And if this happens, there will be a steady decline in inflation (we proceed from this) and a decrease in inflation expectations. TheRussian Bank will be able to more actively reduce the key rate in the future without creating risks to financial stability. Separately, as far as our monetary policy is concerned, this is the last topic in this part that I wanted to touch upon. I would like to saythat this year there is a high probability that in our relations with banks we will move into a new system, from the so-called structural liquidity deficit to a structural liquidity surplus. I'll start by saying that we need to understand the terms "deficit" and "surplus" very correctly. A structural liquidity deficit does not mean that there is a lack of liquidity in the market, just as a structural surplus does not mean that we have excess liquidity, its surpluses. Liquidity by the central bank's method of regulation will be as long as it takes for short-term money market rates to be close to the key rate. "Deficit/surplus" means only changes in the relations between banks and the Central Bank. So far, for several years, the Central Bank has been lending, and it hasbeen lending to banks, and the situation may be that if budget reserve funds are spent quickly enough, we will start borrowing from banks. In any case, I would like to say that no matter how much our relations with banks change, the Central Bank hasall the tools to regulate interest rates in the economy. Yet why is this transition significant, why am I talking about it? The fact is that in the transition from a structural deficit to a surplus, there may be changes in the so-called transmission mechanism of monetary policy (i.e. in how the signals of our monetary policy are transmitted through the financial market to the economy). Structural surplus reduces some risks associated, for example, with a lack of collateral, with a shortage of This form of security. But it can create new risks, it can provoke excessive interest of banks in risky lending, in buying risky assets. And the Central Bank will monitor this. But I want to say right away that in the conditions of a structural surplus, it is normal that banks will keep funds on deposits with the Central Bank or invest in bonds of the Bank of Russia. It should also be noted that the very transition from a structural liquidity deficit to a structural liquidity surplus is accompanied by a decrease in money market rates within our interest rate corridor and may be accompanied by a certain reduction in other interest rates in the economy with the key rate unchanged. That is, even if we do not change the key rate, in the economy as a whole, interest rates may automatically ease monetary conditions. And we, of course, take this into account in our policy. Now about the current situation in the banking sector. Garegin Ashotovich painted such a somewhat gloomy picture, but if you look at the statistics as a whole, at the average situation in general, the situation in different banks is different. Despite the negative continuing background, there is a positive trend in the banking sector. And the banking system in very difficult years interms of the stability of financial markets, external shocks passed quite decently, maintained stability and stability and continued to lend to the economy. There is some fresh data for this year, for the first quarter of 2016. We see that the assets of banks continue to grow gradually, reaching 81.2 trillion rubles, growing by 0.3% in three months - this is already taking into account the cleaning from the exchange rate. Let me remind you that in the first quarter of last year, assets fell by more than 5% (5.3%). Crediting. Creditto the economy is still growing very weakly. In the first quarter, loans to enterprises practically did not change, but let me remind you that in the first quarter of last year there was a decrease in lending to enterprises by 1%. I want to say separately that we are concerned about what ishappening with lending to small businesses. Although the situation by the end of last year - the beginning of this year began to improve somewhat, lending to small and medium-sized businesses is decreasing. I understand that banks assess the risks accordingly. We see that by the end of 2015 the decline in lending to small and medium-sized businesses was at the level of 5%. And in these conditions, of course, we need additional incentives for banks to lend to small businesses. We have taken and are taking a number of measures, including increasing, despitethe liquidity surplus, the limit on our special instrument to support loans to small and medium-sized businesses by 25 billion rubles. We have reduced the risk ratio for high-quality loans to small businesses to 75% in order to give you the opportunity topay more attention to small and medium-sized businesses. And we have a special group, we are working on additional measures together with the SME Corporation and business associations and banks that will allow lending to small and medium-sized businesses. In general, I believe that lending tosmall and medium-sized businesses is a priority area that can have an effect in the next few years, given that our economy is being restructured, and small and medium-sized businesses, of course, should be of greater importance in economicdevelopment. As for lending to individuals, it continues to decline after the boom of previous years. But I want to say that basically the most risky segment of retail lending, unsecured consumer lending, continues to decline. At the same time, mortgages are growing at a slow pace. As of March 1, 2016, the portfolio grew at an annualized rate of 13.3% (this is excluding the impact of the exchange rate). At the same time, the quality of mortgage loans, which we monitor, because there is no need for any bubbles here, remains quite good. In general, the quality of the loan portfolio, which is probably natural in the context of such economic dynamics, a weak economy, is deteriorating, and the share of overdue debt is growing. As of April 1, it was 7% in banks as a whole. And I want to say that, of course, two factors play a role here. The first is that in the conditions of a downturn in the economy, the asset quality, not always good, that you had on your balance sheets and has been preserved since the 2008 crisis is revealed. 2009. On the other hand, of course, the quality of new assets is deteriorating. Nevertheless, we see that the growth rate of overdue debt has decreased sharply compared to last year. In the first quarter of last year, it was 16.6%, this year - 3.6%. It is important that the inflow of household deposits into banks continues. This is very important for the banking sector to have the resources to lend to the economy. And we see that the public's confidence in banks remains. Under these conditions, your dependence on the resources of the Central Bank has decreased, now the share in the liabilities of banks is 5.1% (two times lower than it was in the first quarter of last year). Two words about the financial result. Indeed, as Garegin Ashotovich said, profitability has decreased. But, of course, it cannot be compared with the profitability of those years when our economy grew at a very high pace. Nevertheless, despite the fact that at the beginning of last year there were losses in the banking system, by the end of the year the banking system made a profit, and profitability remains this year, for thefirst quarter banks received 107 billion rubles. It is clear that the situation is different in different banks: there are profitable banks, there are unprofitable banks. But in general, the banking system has a profit, it is certainly less and this is natural. The economy will grow,profitability will increase, and profits will increase. But nevertheless, both profits and capital, which is very important, are enough to increase credit to the economy. Our estimate is that there is now a significant reserve of total capital - 1.8 trillionrubles , which allows you to increase lending to the economy. Now to the supervision, to the topic that is of concern, probably, the most. Our first priority and the priority of internally restructuring our supervision and working with you is to prevent and identifyproblems early in banks. We are absolutely convinced that we need to move towards our early identification of problems and early adoption of measures. And we are aimed at ensuring that supervision takes a proactive stance. For this, among other things, the Central Bank is taking an internal We are creating a Bank risk analysis service that will specialize in banking risk analysis. This function will be centralized, and it will be aimed at ensuring that there is an operational and at the same time scrupulous, up toand including practical transactions, analysis of the risks of banking operations. And so that there is no situation when the same loans to the same legal entities are evaluated by different banks in completely different ways, we will also strive for a certain harmonization here. Of course, we proceed from the fact that supervisory measures should be commensurate with the shortcomings and problems in the work of the credit institution. We are ready to work with the ARB precisely to ensure that supervisory measures correspond to the severity of the violation, let's say, and this is our principle, it should beimplemented. The second important priority of supervision is openness, dialogue with the banking community. We constantly hold meetings, send letters to show the bank what shortcomings are found in its activities. If the managers and owners of bankstake a constructive attitude, we see that this exchange of information is very useful and, as a rule, leads to positive problem solving. That is, even if there are violations, the owners and managers correct them, and there is no need to take action. However, I must say that, unfortunately, not in all cases this information is used for good. We see in a number of cases when we subsequently revoked licenses that the information provided was used by unscrupulous banks to camouflage problems, toeven change assets, in order to hide risks, and this leads to the creation of risks and threats for creditors and depositors. Therefore, when providing information in a dialogue with you, we must take this into account. But - also - more Once - with bona fide banks, with thosewho correct the situation, we are ready for an open dialogue, for partnerships. At the same time, society makes great demands on us and on you, including on the publicity of information about the financial condition of banks. And about the publicity of the measures that apply to credit institutions. Now, with the exception of one case related to an insured event, in principle, we do not publish information about the supervisory actions that apply to the bank. Naturally, there are fears that such information can provoke an outflow of deposits, distrust of depositors. Nevertheless, taking into account the study of international experience, we carefully looked, we believe it would be appropriate to start disclosing the most serious supervisory measures. It is important to ensure greater publicity of the measures applied to credit institutions, starting with the disclosure of information on the introduction of the most serious measures against credit institutions. That is, for example, to disclose information about bans on banking operations. Because otherwise, customers who keep money in the bank say that we do not understand the state of the bank, the supervisory authority does not disclose this information. We will discuss this with the banking community, act carefully so as not to create any new risks. But nevertheless, we believe that such information should be disclosed, especially given that that, unfortunately, there are cases of information leakage and information wars, which we should simply prevent with our policy of opening upthe toast and transparency of the measures taken. At the same time, we believe that it is necessary to increase the amount of information that the bank itself discloses. Not only about supervisory measures, but about the situation inside the bank for consumers of banking services. Because often even for creditors the bank For large banks, the situation in the bank is opaque. And society demands greater transparency from credit institutions. The Bank of Russia supports this position, and we are ready to develop approaches to risk disclosure that can be useful for credit actors, for users of banking services. We are developing standards for disclosing such information on the Bank of Russia's information resources. And we are ready to discuss this entire format with the banking community. Now about financial recovery. The policy of the Central Bank is that we give the opportunity to correct the situation to those banks that have difficulties, but the owners and management, on the one hand, have a desire to take measures to improve the bank, on the other hand, they have such resources to heal the bank. And we are now discussing, among other things, the possibility of amending the legislation so that the owners of banks, whose capital adequacy ratio has fallen below 2% (and I remind you that this is the case when we are obliged to takemeasures for revocation or reorganization), so that the owners or managers of banks in this case can retain the opportunity to participate in financial recovery: they did not abandon the bank in this case, did not try to withdraw assets, but understood that they also have no one Second prospects. Of course, we are talking only about those owners whose constructive intentions and capabilities are beyond doubt. It seems to me that we should also discuss these amendments to the legislation. Our task is also to increase thetransparency of the selection of sanatoriums and the requirements for sanatoriums, so that we select truly effective sanatoriums who can restore the solvency of the bank. Now a few words about priorities in banking regulation. Last year, the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision for the first time assessed regulation in Russia for compliance with the Basel standards. There was a lot of discussion about the implementation of the Basel standards in our country. I must emphasize that, in our opinion, compliance withBasel is an important factor for maintaining the integration of the Russian banking sector into the international financial system. Our banks remain internationally active and borrow from those capital markets. Which are now available, and for this purpose thisco-development is also very important. The results of the assessment were published in March, according to which the current regulation in Russia is recognized as consistent with international standards. In the course of work to bring our regulation into line with theZelsky standards, we worked to change our regulatory framework. And I must say that this work was in two directions: not only in the direction of tightening, which the Basel standards demanded, but also in the direction of some softening. You know that the capital adequacy requirements and risk ratios for loans to small businesses and the best mortgages have been relaxed. We will certainly continue to implement the Basel standards, given our state of the banking system., Nevertheless, we see that the situation in the banking sector can be corrected not only by the introduction of international standards, but needs special regulatory measures. What are the priorities here in regulating our own? First, we see the need to reduce the systemic risks associated with the fact that banks take on too large currency risks through regulation. We have a share of loans to enterprises in foreign currency of more than 40%. We have heard dollarization of deposits, where it is more or less stable, a little more than 30%, nevertheless, this is a high figure. but the dollarization of credit is even greater. And this creates systemic risks and significant movements of the exchange rate. Therefore, in our opinion, we should gradually reduce these risks. This is the reason for the introduction of changes, which will come intoforce in less than a month, from May 1, on increased risk ratios for foreign currency loans and at the same time we are increasing deductions to the FOR on foreign currency deposits. Another important area in regulation is to counteract the artificial divisionof the capital of credit institutions through various kinds of schemes. Unfortunately, we see that these schemes have a significant distribution. We will make changes to our regulation, which details the signs of indirect investments of a credit institution in its capital and the procedure for supervisory actions when they are detected. The problem of the entire banking sector and, perhaps, of the entire financial system remains the prevalence of lending to persons associated with the bank. Therefore, when problems arise, we immediately see theown business, the bank very quickly "lies down", because a large proportion of loans related to its personal business, the business of owners, managers. And therefore, from January 1, 2017, after a two-year delay, we will introduce a new limited standard. Risk analysis for persons related to the bank (H25). Now for the reserves. In general, this issue constantly arises in our discussions, it was discussed at the meetings that Garegin Ashotovich spoke about, and is now being discussed, and indeed a separate working group has been created, but I want to say that we do not have excess reserves in the banking system. Our reserves have been created at a historically normal, let's say, level. And no more and no less. do not deviate much from the historically normal level. They say, in difficult circumstances, let's reduce reserves, reduce the provision for bad loans, because it's hard for banks. I think this is unacceptable because banks work, I remind you again, with other people's money. You explain to your depositors and the lenderthat their resources that they carry to the banks should be less protected. I think they won't understand you. And creating sufficient reserves is your insurance for your obligations. it's your future resilience, your financial institution. Therefore,we will continue to work on the creation of a sufficient level of reserves. Yes, there are certain costs, Garegin Ashotovich said why the bank should check the borrower, whether he conducts real activities or not. But this is your borrower, if youdon't want to check, you create a 100% reserve for it. If you want to check and make sure that he is doing real business, well, prove that he is conducting real activities. Otherwise, it turns out that we are risking the money of lenders and depositors excessively. This banking systemshould not allow.
