Nevertheless, there are problems in applying approaches to reservation. I agree with this. Garegin Ashotovich and I talked about this. We need to streamline the issues on deadlines, and there is something you gave an example on apartments. We are certainly ready to work with you on such things, and this working group is aimed at eliminating such shortcomings, imperfections in the reservation policy, so that the supervisory practice of reservations itself is in dialogue with the bank. We could listen to your arguments and give bona fide banks enough time to form these necessary reserves. Of course, changes in our supervisory and regulatory practices by the Central Bankare not enough to improve the effectiveness of supervision and regulation, so legislative initiatives are also needed. I will focus on just two of them, and I will conclude with that. The first concerns auditing. We see that there are unreliablebank audit practices. In cases with revoked licenses and so on, we see that in more than 50% of cases there are positive conclusions without any reservations from the point of view of the audit. And, in our opinion, here we need an immediate solution to theseproblems at the level of legislation. We believe that the first thing is to define the procedures for interaction and exchange of information between audit organizations and the Bank of Russia, as it is in many countries, the exchange of information between us. And the second thing is to give theBank of Russia the authority to maintain a register of audit organizations that are allowed to conduct a mandatory audit of the financial institutions' financial institutions, as well as the right to impose increased requirements on them. And we consider this important to protect the interestsof depositors and creditors so that auditors here have increased responsibility. The second direction is related to banking and financial holdings. Indeed, we have some progress in the area of consolidated supervision. But so far, the Bank of Russia does not have the authority to regulate and supervise bank holdings, which include several banks and other financial companies that have the same owners. The fact that the same owners have the opportunityto own different financial assets that are not combined into a single financial holding leads to numerous abuses, Undermining the financial stability of banks and other financial companies, and in some cases can create risks of financial stabilityand. I'm talking about cases when, at the expense of generally not very complex schemes, banks create fictitious capital, paid in the end at the expense of loans from the same bank. Or when the funds of pension funds, insurance reserves through the purchase of bonds of banks ultimately, they go to finance the projects of fund owners and insurance companies. Or when, through lending to leasing companies, banks have the opportunity, in fact, to avoid the need to comply with regulations and accrue adequate reserves. It's not uncommon toabuse repo operations, and we see this, and sometimes we encounter outright fraud, where the same asset can migrate when checking from the balance sheets of one organization to the balance sheets of another organization. Therefore, in our opinion, there should be adequate opportunities to curb such unfair practices. To do this, it is necessary to establish the powers of the Bank of Russia to supervise bank holdings. And to extend to bank holdings the norms relating to the rulesfor the calculation of the amount of capital, mandatory standards, standards of supervisory reporting. Secondly, we consider it appropriate to think about obliging the owners of banks and other financial companies, if they are part of a financial holding, to createan intermediate company - a resident of the Russian Federation (I emphasize - a resident of the Russian Federation) to manage a bank holding or to give the Bank of Russia the authority to create such a company. It is desirable to do this in order to separate the banking and financial activities of the holding from other activities (industry, construction, trade). And we often have such an intersection of risks. Another significant issue is the business reputation of bankers. I think that the entire banking community is interested in being trusted and that the reputation of bankers, the banking system is high and causes positive emotions in society. Therefore, of course, we must do everything to ensure that people who have already stained themselves with offenses and fraud leave the banking environment, from banking organizations. Therefore, a database is being kept on unscrupulous managers and owners of banks. Now there isinformation about more than 5 thousand persons, and we do not give these persons the opportunity to acquire more than 10% of the bank's shares and participate in management bodies. but, in our opinion, stricter requirements are needed here. We believe that the ban on holding a management positionand acquiring large blocks of shares in a bank should reach 10 years with a one-time limit, with a recurrence there should be a lifetime ban, and this should also apply to auditors who sign knowingly false audit reports. At the same time, I would liketo note that often the problems that arise are not only and not so much related to fraud, deliberate violation of the law. Unfortunately, our external situation is changing rapidly, and our regulation is changing quite quickly, there is not enoughprofessionalism and competence. We have also thought about this and want to offer you and, perhaps, talk to the ARB in order to organize special advanced training programs in such areas where there are questions. This includes financial literacy, risk management, bankruptcy prevention, cybercrime, which now poses some of the big risks. In a number of such areas, we need to make joint training programs in order to improve the skills of both your respective hundredmines and bank managers, so that those who want to conduct banking activities in good faith can do so at the most professional level. I specifically focused on But at the same time, I would not like you to get the impression that we really have the same shortcomings here, so I would like to remind you of the beginning of my speech, which was discussed, including the analysis on figures, that in general thesituation in the banking sector is normal. it is adequate to the situation in our economy, and in general, banks are quite successfully fulfilling their mission to maintain economic growth and finance economic growth. And in conclusion, I want to say that we are making every effort to ensure that the Russian banking sector is sustainable, so that it meets the needs of the economy, we are improving regulation and supervision, we maintain a dialogue with the bankingcommunity. We hear the voices of bankers who ask us to be softer, but, unfortunately, especially given the difficult economic situation, we are obliged to protect the rights of depositors and creditors of banks to act in such a way as to protect the rights of depositors and creditors of banks. how we act. And I am sure that in theend we will have less unpleasant work on revoking licenses, both business and the population will be able to be confident in their banks. I wish you success in your difficult work, thank you for your attention. ???1

Title: Speech at the V Financial Stability Forum
text: First Deputy Governor of the Bank of Russia Ksenia Yudaeva spoke at the V Financial Stability Forum April 8, 2016 Performance Our forum is devoted to issues of financial stability, so in my report I will mainly talk about possible risks. Risks should not be feared or avoided. You need to be prepared for risks, that is, to have tools to manage risks, prevent them and mitigate the negative consequences of their implementation. Therefore, in my speech, I will briefly present our vision of some of the main risks, as well as focus on individual policy measures aimed at reducing the impact of risks on the Russianfinancial system. I would like to dwell on three main points: 1) possible risks associated with the situation on global markets; 2) measures of the Bank of Russia to reduce currency risks in the financial system and in the economy as a whole; 3) the relationship between monetary policy and financial stability in the current Russian macroeconomic conditions. I will start with the situation on global markets. After the surge in volatility in January, the situation has stabilized somewhat in recent weeks, but fundamentallyon remains unstable. The main problem is low economic growth and low productivity growth. The experience of developed economies over the past 7-8 years has shown that attempts to influence the situation only with monetary policy measures without monetary policy measures carrying out adequate structural reforms are not able to move the situation in the economy from the dead point. We see time and time again evidence of this development. Economic growth in the main economic centers of the world remains low, despite unprecedentedsteps to ease monetary policy. On the other hand, the price for ultra-soft monetary policy is volatility in the markets and the risks of bubbles. Negative interest rates have a negative impact on the situation inthe banking and financial sectors, which creates additional risks. As for the situation in the oil sector, there are still many uncertainties. The excess of supply over demand remains. At the same time, the decline in oil prices contrary to expectations did not lead to an acceleration in economic growth in the global economy. The expected acceleration of growth in consumer countries, which should have compensated for its slowdown in the producing countries, has not yetoccurred. Perhaps this is due to structural shifts in the global economy. Chief among them is the transition of the Chinese economy from growth based on exports and investment to growth based on consumer demand. Last year, concernsabout China became a source of volatility in global markets. The situation has stabilized somewhat. Positive results have begun to emerge from fiscal stimulus measures adopted in the second half of 2015. ThePeople's Bank of China has also accepted risk mitigation measures. Therefore, the current risks associated with the Chinese situation have decreased significantly, but they cannot be completely discounted. In terms of emerging markets in general, many of themare experiencing slower economic growth and high volatility in currencies and markets. One of the reasons for the vulnerability of these countries is the high level of economic growth. corporate sector debt. Since 2008, the nature of this debt has changed: companies have borrowed less from banks and often borrow directly from global markets through bond issuance. Rising rates in the United States are leading to higher debt prices and difficulties in its refinancing, which contributes to the additionalvolatility of the exchange rates of the respective countries. Russia also faced such a problem. A lot has already been said about payments on foreign debts, I will not dwell on this. But no less important is the problem of the widespread use of domestic foreign exchange lending. Now the share of corporate lending in foreign currency is about 40%. This creates a number of risks, both at the micro and macro levels. I will start with the risks for the banking sector. Banks' capital instruments are mostlymined in rubles. As a result, the weakening of the ruble automatically causes an increase in risk-weighted assets, and thus leads to a decrease in the capital adequacy ratios of banks. And this, in turn, negatively affects their stability and limitsthe potential of lending. Therefore, the dynamics of lending becomes procyclical. In addition, such a high level of development of foreign currency lending suggests that banks do not quite correctly assess its risks. Neither banks nor borrowers seem to have a clear understanding that the difference in interest rates between ruble and foreign currency borrowing reflects currency risk. That is, by borrowing in foreign currency at lower rates, the borrower assumes the risk of servicing the increased debt in the event of a weakening of the exchange rate. And the difference in rates roughly covers these costs, taking into account the likelihood of their occurrence. Only the lack of a clear understanding of currency risks can explain the fact that That even after the 2008 crisis, there continued to be active foreign currency lending to borrowers without appropriate foreign exchange earnings, primarily from the construction and real estate sectors. Such undercounting of borrowers' currency risks also has macroeconomic implications, exacerbating fluctuations in the rate of economicgrowth (or decline) in the face of fluctuations in oil prices, as well as increasing exchange rate volatility. The mechanism here is simple: more currency is needed to service foreign currency debts during the period of exchange rate fluctuations, so its purchases increase, which further increases the volatility of the exchange rate. At the same time, the growth of foreign currency borrowings during the period of appreciation of the exchange rate leads to an additional inflow of capital, which also increases volatility. The measures proposed by the Bank of Russiato establish increased risk ratios for loans and other claims in foreign currency are aimed at limiting such risks. Currently, it is planned to exclude domestic exporters from the scope of increased requirements. It should be understood that this approach has its pros and cons. Indeed, exporters have a certain level of so-called natural hedging, and their currency risks are less. On the other hand, the share of foreign exchange lending is already quite high and perhaps even exceeds the level of natural hedging. Finally, the conclusion that the widespread use of foreign exchange lending increases the volatility of the national currency exchange rate in the face of external shocks is true both in relation to lending to non-trade. Moreover, if we talk about the development of the market for currency hedging instruments, it is important that its participants are not only importers, but also exporters. Their currency risks are usuallythe opposite, so in the end the sellers of insurance against currency risks of importers are exporters and vice versa. And foreign currency loans to exporters reduce their need for hedging instruments. Dollarization, or rather, currencyization isa complex problem associated not only with foreign currency loans, but also with a high share of foreign currency in the liabilities of banks. A significant level of dollarization (or currencyization) of deposits increases the risks of a shortage of foreign exchange liquidity, reduces the effectiveness of the central bank's implementation of monetary policy. Therefore, the measures of the Bank of Russia are aimed at discouraging the attraction of liabilities in foreign currency: from April 1, 2016 At thesame time, it is obvious that demonetization is a rather slow process, the balance of foreign currency assets and liabilities is important, so the Bank of Russia plans to introduce measures gradually. The key condition for successful demonetization measures is the implementation of the inflation targeting policy, which increases confidence in the national currency and generally reduces the risks of financial instability. Moderately tight monetary policy, including keeping the key rate unchanged for a long time, is bearing fruit. Inflation has fallen by more than half compared to peak values. Market participants' confidence in the Bank of Russia's policy is gradually growing. As a result, interest rate curves are becoming inverted by reducing long stakes. A steady decline in inflation and inflation expectations will allow the Bank of Russia to more actively reduce the key rate in the future without creating risks to financial stability. Of particular note is the expected shift this year to a structural liquidity surplus from the structural deficit we've been living with in recent years. Structural surpluses reduce some risks, but can create new ones. The volume of refinancing in the Bank of Russia is decreasing, as a result of which the dependence of the banking system onthe Bank of Russia's financing is decreasing. The structural problem of lack of market collateral is receding into the background. It is becoming easier for systemically important banks to meet the short-term liquidity ratio. But foreign experience suggests that the structural surplusof the liquidity face does not automatically contribute to improving the situation with market liquidity. On the contrary, against the background of structural surpluses in a wide range of countries of the world, there has recently been a slight deterioration in the liquidity situation in global markets. The depth of individual markets has decreased, and the size of transactions that can be carried out without affecting the price has decreased. The so-called TIAZn sgazN has become more frequent. With regard to Russia, it should be understood that in the conditions of a liquidity surplus , the effective operation of the money market, which redistributes liquidity, becomes especially important. From this point of view, new money market instruments, including repo with CSU, which will be discussed later in our session, are useful. At the expense of deposit operations and the issue of bonds, the Bank of Russia will withdraw all excess liquidity from circulation, as a result of which in the conditions of structural surplus in the banking sector there will be as much liquidity as it would be in conditions of structural deficit. That is, as much as is needed to meet the demand for money at the level of the key interest rate set by the Bank of Russia. Nevertheless, in the conditions of a liquidity surplus, it is impossible to completely exclude the risk of bubbles in individual markets (as itdid, for example, in the period up to 2011, when the liquidity surplus and low interest rates contributed to the boom in the market of unsecured consumer lending). monitor and, if necessary, applycroprudential policy measures. A few words about the situation in the Russian economy. It is improving but remains challenging, which, as elsewhere in the world, is a factor of vulnerability to the financial market. Separately, in this regard, I would like to dwell on the situation with theBudget. The Russian budget system has not yet fully adapted to low oil prices and falling oil and gas revenues. The Reserve Fund allows financing the increased budget deficit, but it is necessary to develop a program that would balance the budget system in the medium term. Perhaps it is time to think about a new budget rule. Without this, the budget will be a source of risks and for the economy, and for financial stability. Finally, a few words about why meeting the inflation target of 4% will reduce the risks to financial stability. As a rule, lower inflation is less volatile and more predictable. The exchange rate is more stable, because it depends on monetary inflation, and if it is more stable, then the rate is more stable. Risk premiums in conditions of low inflation are reduced, and with them the risks to financial stability. Therefore, the policy of the Bank of Russia to reduce inflation and maintain it on a low level will help reduce the risks of financial stabilityand reduce the vulnerability of the Russian economy to financial risks.

Title: Governor of the Bank of Russia presented at the plenary session of the State Duma The main directions of the unified state monetary policy for 2016 and the period 2017 and 2018
text: Governor of the Bank of Russia Elvira Nabiullina presented at the plenary session of the State Duma The main directions of the unified state monetary policy for 2016 and the period 2017 and 2018 November 13, 2015 Performance Speech 3. Nabiullina at the plenary session State Duma Good afternoon, Sergei Yevgenyevich, dear deputies of the State Duma! At the outset, I would like to thank the deputies for their very deep, very detailed participation in the work on the Main Directions of Monetary Policy. As a result of the discussions of both the working group and the committees, we clarified and supplemented thedocument. On Tuesday, the updated document was approved by the Board of Directors of the Bank of Russia. I will start with a general description of the current situation and the main risks that this situation presents to us. These are prerequisites for the implementation of our monetary policy. After that, I will briefly dwell on the forecast and our main monetary policy instruments. Current situation The situation in the Russian economy continues to be strongly influenced by the continuing uncertainty in world markets. From the point of view of external risks, the decline in oil prices, the slowdown in the growth rate of the Chinese economy and the normalization of the monetary policy of the US Federal Reserve are in the foreground. The transition of the oil market to a new equilibrium with a lower price level has had and will continue to havea negative impact on the Russian economy. The fall in oil prices, combined with the effect of restricting the access of Russian banks and companies to external borrowings, leads to a reduction in foreign exchange earnings, according to our estimates, by about 200 billion, in annualterms. In China, a sharp change in the situation is not expected, but certain risks are associated not only with a slowdown in growth rates, but also with a change in the structure of economic growth in China. In industry, the growth rate of which affects the demand for raw materials, the decline is faster than in the chinese economy as a whole, where the service sector is becoming increasingly important. With respect to Fed policy, the focus shifts from a specific rate hike date to a longer-term policy horizon, that is, the rate at which rates will rise. The divergence between market expectations and the Fed's actual policy of raising rates could create risks of capital flight from emerging markets (which include Russia) and increased volatility not only in this, but at least next year. These are the risks we we take into account in our policy. Under the influence of external negative factors, unfortunately, the high volatility of the ruble exchange rate remains. Nevertheless, it has declined since the beginning of the year and no longer poses serious risks to financial stability. Moreover, its impact on inflation and inflation expectations and, accordingly, on the behavior of economic agents is decreasing. External conditions remain unfavorable, but our economy is gradually adapting to them. Inflation is decreasing. The jump in inflation at the end of last year and the beginning of this year was caused by powerful, but one-time factors - the decline in the price of oil and the subsequent depreciation of the ruble. The effect of these events has already materialized. Inflation is slowing down, we expect it to fall to 12-13% by the end of this year. According to our forecast, inflation will continue to decline quite rapidly next year. By theend of 2016, according to our forecasts, inflation will be 5.5-6.5%. In the Main Directions of Monetary Policy, we lay down three forecast scenarios, and in all three scenarios - basic, optimistic and pessimistic - we achieve the target for information. 4% by the end of 2017. I note that when making decisions on monetary policy, we always mean the balance of risks for inflation and for the economy, the achievement of the inflation target will not occur at the expense of economic growth. We expect a return to positivegrowth rates by the second half of 2016, and by the end of 2015, according to our estimates, the decline will be from 3.9 to 4.4%. Capital outflow this year will be approximately 70 billion - here we lowered the forecast (previously we expected 85 billion). but a significant factor that has accelerated the adjustment of the balance of payments and the change in the structure of the economy in response to external shocks. As for the balance of payments, we are seeing both an increase in the current account balance and a decrease in capital outflows for reasons unrelated to debt repayments. Along with the adaptation of the balance of payments, we are also already seeing signals of a change in the structures of the balance of payments. The first signs that in the export and import-substituting sectors the situation is beginning to look a little more stable. A few words about the situation in the banking sector. I will start with the situation on the deposit market. This year we managed to reverse the situation last year, when during the year there was a decrease in the volume of ruble deposits. For 10 months of this year, deposits increased by 14.2% (excluding currency revaluation by 10.2%). Now as for lending. At the beginning of the year, lending reallyslowed down, and in some areas, for example, small businesses, continued to decline. However, in recent months, credit growth has resumed. For 10 months, banks increased lending to enterprises by 7.1% (excluding currency revaluation of 2.2%). I would like to note that lending growth is taking place despite the fact that the quality of banks' loan portfolio has deteriorated. True, in this area we see some positive changes. Overdue debt is growing, but this trend is "fading". Thus, in October of this year, the share of overdue debt on loans to non-financial organizations increased by 0.1%, to 5.9%, on retail loans - from 8.0 to 8.1%. Nevertheless, the growth rate of lending can be limited not only by high interest rates, but also by the accumulated rather high debt burden of the non-financial sector as a whole. The total level of debt burden of enterprises, which includes both external loans and bond loans, is now about 80% of GDP. This is lower than in developed countries. x countries, but higher than in many countries with emerging markets. There are sectors and companies with the potential to increase lending, and there are those that are contraindicated by further debt growth - there is already a debt burden that can pose a threat todevelopment. There are big risks in construction, some companies in the manufacturing sectors, among commodity companies, risks remain in the coal industry. And the issue of financing growth in the real sector is to a much greater extent a matter of restoring payments. the ability of companies and raising capital, than the issue of increasing loans. We see from the experience of other countries that excessive expansion of lending can create great risks for development in the future. I will now turn to our forecast. We have alreadypresented our forecast earlier, so I will go through it quite briefly. So, we distinguish three forecast scenarios depending on oil prices. In the baseline scenario , the average annual price will be 50 per barrel, the optimistic scenario is the growth of oilprices to 70-80, per barrel, the risk scenario - the average annual oil price is below 40 per barrel. In all scenarios, we assume that the regime of financial sanctions and trade restrictions will continue in the next three years. In the baseline scenario, we expectthat the annual growth rate of the Russian economy will move to the positive area in 2017, and in 2018 growth of about 2.0-3.0% is expected. In the baseline scenario, as inflation declines and inflation expectations stabilize, we see an opportunity to continue lowering the key rate. In the optimistic scenario, the recovery of economic growth (in annual terms) will occur already in 2016. Inflation will gradually decline, as in the baseline scenario. The potential for lowering the key rate will be somewhatgreater, as well as the potential for replenishing gold and foreign exchange reserves. In the face of heightened uncertainty about the prospects not only for the oil market, but for the global economy as a whole, it is important to be prepared for the most adverse developments. To do this , we have considered a risk scenario. In the event of an increase in risks, we will be ready to use the full arsenal of tools and measures available to us, including increasing the volume of foreign exchange refinancing and the implementation of foreign currency sales to maintain financialstability. We have such tools and are ready to be used if necessary. Now about refinancing tools. I would like to remind you that in addition to standard instruments, we have introduced specialised instruments aimed atsupporting lending in priority sectors and where there are market failures. First, about the development of standard tools. In the second half of last year and the beginning of this year, we focused on the problems of collateral deficit due to the growing demand for ruble liquidityfrom the Central Bank and the problems of access to foreign exchange liquidity. To solve the problem of collateral, we expanded the lombard list, the list of the Bank of Russia, increased the correction coefficients for assessing the value of assets in collateral. We have also createda tool for providing foreign exchange liquidity on a borrowed basis. But already in the first half of the year, the situation with both ruble and foreign exchange liquidity improved significantly. The growth of deposits in banks began. The volume of debt on repo operations in rubles decreased from 2.8 trillion rubles. at the beginning of the year to 789 billion rubles. on today's date; the debt on secured loans of the Bank of Russia for this period decreased from 4.4 trillion rubles. in twotimes, to 2.2 trillion rubles. The foreign exchange repo instruments and loans in foreign currency introduced last year made it possible to improve the situation with foreign exchange liquidity, smooth out the passage of the peak of payments on external debts and thus contributed to the stabilizationof the foreign exchange market. Since the second quarter, the situation with foreign exchange liquidity has been improving, and the demand for our operations is falling. As a result, the volume of funds issued for all instruments in foreign currency, decreased from a maximum level of 36 billion, to about 26.5 billion The limit on these operations is set by the Bank of Russia in the amount of 50 billion. It should be noted that the tools for providing foreign currency liquidity are not limited to 2015: repo operations were introduced for the period up to the end of 2016, and forredit in foreign currency - until the end of 2017. The Bank of Russia monitors the adequacy of foreign exchange liquidity from non-financial companies and banks to make payments on external debts. The assessment for 2016 showed that payments on external debt in c this year will be uniform. Moreover, we conduct special surveys of our largest companies, and, according to surveys of the thirty largest companies, payments on external debt (I emphasize, taking into account intra-group financing, whichis available) in the first quarter of 2016 will amount to 6 billion. IN THE FOURTH QUARTER OF THIS YEAR - 8 billion. US dollars (again - taking into account intra-group payments). The volume of corporate payments on external debt in 2016 will be about 2 times less than in 2015. In general, the Russian external debt has decreased dramatically since 2014, it has decreased by almost 30%. At the beginning of 2014, the entire external debt amounted to 729 billion US dollars, currently it is 522 billion US dollars. Now about specialized tools. We have four of them aimed at supporting lending: small and medium-sized businesses (the rate there is 6.5%, a period of 3 years), non-primary exports, project financing (for these two). The rate is now 9%) and support for military mortgages. As of today, 43.7 billion rubles from the limit of 100 billion rubles were used under the program to support investment projects, 32.8 billion rubles were used for lending to small and medium-sized businessesfrom the limit of 50 billion rubles, 17.2 billion rubles were used for lending to non-primary exports. from the limit of 50 billion rubles. And at the moment, a little less than 20 billion rubles have been used. We are often approached with a requestto increase the limits on these specialized instruments. I do not dispute that in some cases, when the existing limits are chosen, this is makes sense to do. So, this year we have increased the limit on refinancing military mortgages (as I have already said), on projectfinancing - from 50 to 100 billion rubles. about the state and get credit within the framework of a specialized instrument. It is therefore important for us to pursue policies that will ultimately lead to lower interest rates on all loans, rather than simply expanding financing at preferential rates for a select few, thereby slowing or reducing the scope for lowering interest rates on all loans. In conclusion, I would like to say that, as you can see, we are quite flexible in responding to the situation, adjusting our tools, introducing additional support measures where they are needed. We strive to respond very quickly to any changes in external conditions. As the results of the first nine months of this year showed, the measures taken work. But at the same time, we also do not allow the distortion of monetary mechanisms. - credit policy, excessive relaxations for the banking sector, which would allow instead to solve problems, mask them. Our task is not to mask the problems in the economy, but to give banks and the real sector time to learn how to do business in the new conditions. In the era of high global volatility (it is likely to be a considerable time), the main task of the central bank is to ensure price stability, financial stability and, in general, economic stability. In the event of severe shocks, not all of these goals are easy to achieve at the same time. Last year, when we decided to move to a floating exchange rate under difficult conditions, we had to allow inflation to jump in order to reduce the risks to the economy. But we managed toquickly control this inflation, and we are now continuing a policy that will lead to lower inflation. In parallel, we have taken measures to maintain overall financial stability. The next task is to The period is to prevent inflation,which intensified earlier this year, from becoming a threat to economic growth in the future. At the same time, long-term market interest rates for economic entities are of particular importance. They will decrease only if inflation and inflation expectations decrease. It is important for us to consolidate this trend, namely the tendency to reduce long-term interest rates. When deciding on interest rates now, we must take into account both current and future risks to economic growth and inflation. By lowering rates too quicklynow, we could create risks that rates will start to rise in the future. We shouldn't allow that. At the same time, when making decisions in the field of monetary policy, we proceeded and will proceed from the fact that financingdepends on the confidence of market participants in each other, on their faith in the ability, including the Central Bank, to ensure price and financial stability, their confidence in the future is much greater than on the cost of short-term funding from the Central Bank. Thank you very much for your attention.

Title: Governor of the Bank of Russia at the XXVIII International Financial Congress
text: Governor of the Bank of Russia Elvira Nabiullina performed at XXVIII International Financial Congress 4 July 2019 Year Good morning, dear colleagues! I am pleased to welcome you to the next International Financial Congress. Traditionally, the congress brings together representatives of all sectors of the Russian financial market, and for us this is an opportunity to discuss the challenges facing the financial system and the regulator. In past years, the main challenge was related to how the Russian economy and financial sphere should adapt to the new world - with low oil prices and a sharply increased level of uncertainty, wheregeopolitical factors have become "jokers" that can dramatically change the balance of power in the game. Achieving macroeconomic stability in the new conditions required great efforts. Now there is a solid basis for development: low inflation and the tools tostabilize it near the target level, primarily the inflation targeting policy, disciplined responsible budget policy pursued by the Government. On the part of the Central Bank, we have also worked to clean up the financial system, to strengthen supervision and regulation, to develop tools to maintain financial stability, and this also contributes to the fact that today our country is more protected from external risks and prepared for new possible surges offreedom. But, I think, none of those present has any illusions that this is enough, that everything is now in order. Perhaps, on the contrary, we are now facing an even more formidable challenge - the economic growth rate is very low, business does not yet seethe situation, the incomes of the population are practically not growing, and citizens have little sense that the stability achieved has given them a better quality of life. What hinders growth? Of course, there's always a temptation to blame everything on external factors, but I don't think it's allabout them. Yes, the global economy is slowing down. Trade wars and geopolitical escalations are only making things worse. We have no reason to believe that in any foreseeable future the external situation will fundamentally change. Yes, there will be upward and downward fluctuations, both with new actions and agreements of countries in the trade war, and with attempts by central banks to stop the most negative effects or vice versa - with new outbreaks of populism in politics, with geopolitical aggravations. That is, the external environment will remain difficult. We must understand this. But, on the other hand, it is not so bad. In any case, we're clearly not living in a risky scenario right now. Oil prices are slightly above expectations, our country continues to be interspring for global capital markets. The main limitations for development, in my opinion, are internal. And therefore, in my speech today, I would like to dwell on what role the financial sector and the policy of the Central Bank could play in this situationand what is needed from the point of view of economic policy as a whole for the situation to change. The answer to this question is known: structural restrictions need to be lifted. The central bank is responsible for maintaining price and financial stability. And this is not our fault, it is a consequence of the fact that the tools that the Central Bank has at its disposal ultimately affect price and financial stability. In themselves, low inflation and the absence of risks to financial stability are favorable forgreater rates and quality of economic growth by expanding planning horizons, increasing transparency and reducing macroeconomic risks. That is why in recent years we have focused on the task of reducing inflation to the target of 4% and maintainingit at this level, as well as ensuring financial stability both at the level of the system as a whole and at the level of individual institutions. The most important bearing element of macro stability is also the Government's adherence to the budget rule. It has made itpossible to isolate the economy from fluctuations in oil prices to a significant extent and to accumulate a safety cushion in case of risks. But macro stability is not growth. And the growth now is about 1.5-2%, and in the first quarter it was only 0.5%. And that's withvery low unemployment. And that's the result that we're going to have without structural change, because policies to maintain macroeconomic stability can only stabilize the economy near its current potential. If we try to shift the potential growth rates with central bank instruments, we will eventually get either inflation or bubbles in financial markets, and most likely both. And to increase the potential, to use all the opportunities that the economy has to increase the rate of economic growth and ultimately increase the well-being of people, is only through structural transformations that will contribute to the redistribution of resources, both labor and financial, into areaswith greater returns, with greater productivity, creating more added value. The main thing that needs to be done in order for the economy to begin to grow is a radical improvement in the investment climate. Here it is impossible to engage in a shift in the focus of economic policy, a distraction of attention to non-primordial factors. This year, the Governmenthas launched national projects that are designed to remove structural constraints. These projects, which involve investment in education, healthcare, and infrastructure, should work if effectively managed. But there are twoserious problems that, in my opinion, cannot be hushed up if we really want sustainable economic growth. First. It is necessary to create incentives for entrepreneurial initiative. Economic growth is created by business, not the state. Publicinvestment cannot replace private investment. And even with the successful implementation of national projects in their state part, there is no guarantee that they will create a commensurate multiplicative effect through the expansion of private investment. And it is important to emphasizethat private investment is not loans obtained at low interest rates in banks under state guarantees. Private investment is, first of all, additional share capital, own funds of both large businesses and small entrepreneurs, which they are willing to risk in the expectation of future growth of their business and profits. And the willingness to take on this risk directly depends on the notorious investment climate. If an efficient business is not ready to invest andonly companies in a weak financial position that need them for survival and not for development are in demand for the treatment of financial resources, then it should not be surprising that the financial sector is reluctant to lend to companies. The second problem is that structural changes take time. We - first because of high oil prices, then because of the need to concentrate on strengthening macroeconomic stability - postponed the implementation many overdue structural reforms, and now we want a quick result. As a result, we againfind ourselves in the trap of finding simple solutions, when we are looking not where we lost, but where it is light, and for some reason, usually the search for a solution with this approach leads to the Central Bank. If during the crisis phenomena of 2014-2015 as simple solutions it was proposedto impose restrictions on the movement of capital, a sharp reduction in the key rate or the large-scale distribution of money to "the country's needed" enterprises, now new ideas have emerged. For example, the fight against consumer lending in the hope that if banksare allowed to issue loans to individuals, they will begin to actively lend to the corporate sector and this in itself will start the flywheel of the investment boom. I must once again state that there are no simple solutions. This is well understood by those who have ever faced the solution of optimization problems. If one factor is really limiting - in our case, this is primarily the investment climate - then no matter how we change other factors, we will not get an improvement in the situation. Moreover, if we try to mask structural problems by handing out cheap money, our country will lose even more time: first, we will lose the hard-won macroeconomic stability, and then we will re-solve the problem of its restoration, undermining faith in the future among the population and business. Improving the investment climate, alas, is not limited to reducing administrative barriers. We need the protection of private property, independent courts, and it is the judicial settlement of corporate conflicts, the better quality of corporate governance, the development of human potential. These words we say almost unchanged for many years. At first they seemed correct, then a common place, then the appeal to the topic of the investment climatebecomes empty words of officials, and now sometimes it seems like a cry of despair. But we still need a better quality business environment, and that's a lot of work. What can and should the financial system do in this situation to promote economicgrowth? The financial system should also become part of structural changes through the formation of a long-term investment resource, the development of the stock market and the attitude to lending to effective projects. If we talk about lendingand the real sector, then, of course, the Bank of Russia is very interested in its development. And within the framework of approaches to the so-called stimulating regulation, we will strive to make corporate lending more attractive for banks,without prejudice to risk management with a thorough analysis of borrowers by banks. As I have already said, simply lending to everyone in a row or "necessary" companies is completely wrong and will only harm economic growth or allocate resources to inefficientsectors. Healthy corporate lending is, first of all, lending to operating companies engaged in the development of production. In the meantime, we see that banks are very happy to lend to mergers and acquisitions. That is, they lend to thedistribution of property, and not the expansion of activities, while more and more often experiencing problems with the repayment of previously issued loans. A year ago, we said that we were concerned about this trend, but banks asked us to postpone the introduction of regulatorymeasures aimed at limiting lending to mergers and acquisitions. And we went to meet the wishes of market participants, gave time to prepare. But, of course, we see that without a direct change in regulation, regulatory pressure from our country,this trend will not change. Therefore, we do not intend to postpone the introduction of these measures further. By the end of the year, the increase in reserves for possible losses on loans under such transactions will be accepted and will come into force. We will attribute such loans to the III category ofquality, with an estimated reserve of 21%, if there is collateral, it can be reduced to 10%. The transfer of loans to the II quality category will be possible if the borrower shows a good financial result, but the reserve will still not be lower than 5%. We will not havea long series of exceptions that soften this rule: investments in the authorized capital of enterprises within the framework of federal targeted programs, in strategic enterprises, below the reserve in the presence of state guarantees. From the point of view of the development of long-term investments in the realsector, our pension funds are a key participant in the financial system. Our policy is aimed at increasing the role of non-state pension funds as a source of long-term money. We have already changed the regulation in such a way as to stimulatelong-term personal investments of NPFs in the real sector: we allowed not to revalue assets due to short-term market fluctuations, expanded opportunities for investing in concession bonds, introduced restrictions on the volume of investments in the financial sector. We see that NPF investments in the financial sector are declining, and in the real sector against this background they are growing, but the potential for further growth still exists. The priority for us here is to monitor the stability of pension funds, and this is the basis for confidence in pension savings as a wholeand for the development of the accumulative element in the pension system. Financing small and medium-sized businesses continues to be one of our priorities. We believe in banks with a basic license as an institution for supporting small and medium-sized businesses. Whilethe new licenses have existed de facto for only six months, it is too early to assess how it works, we will closely monitor the development of this type of banking business. At the congress, a separate discussion will be devoted to the business models of banks with a basic license. It includes anew topic - the development of green financing. Socially responsible environmentally friendly business should receive better conditions in the financial market. These are the companies that think about the future. Now we are working with the Ministry of EconomicDevelopment on the principles of disclosure of non-financial information by companies, including on environmental and social responsibility. The first issues of green bonds have already passed, coupons for them are subsidized by the Ministry of Industry. And yet, we still perceive d0eep Tipapseas exotic, but in developed markets it has already become a real factor in investment policy, which affects the access of companies to capital. And I think it is important to develop it in Russia, and the Central Bank will pay special attention to this. Now about the challenges that are facing the financial sector and us as a regulator. The main challenges are now really related to digitalization. This is the main driver of changes in the financial sphere, in the transformation of business models. The Russian financial sector has quite successfully ridden the digital wave, according to estimates , we are in third place in the world in terms of penetration of financial technologies, but at the same time new challenges arise. The first one, which we understand well andare already working with: digitalization requires large investments, a ticket to the digital world is expensive and not affordable for small participants. But the road is the infrastructure, and on its basis even small participants will be able to offer innovative, competitive products. That is why we have launched our infrastructure projects: biometrics, Marketplace, Fast Payment System. Today they will also be devoted to a separate session of the congress: how they work, what results they bring. But the most pressing issue is that theseprojects themselves become a factor in the transformation of the market, and the market is sometimes happy about it, and sometimes not at all. An obvious example is the Fast Payment System. When it came only to transfers between individuals, almost all market participants rejoiced that I would be ableto bite off a piece of the pie from the business of the largest banks, compete with them in payment services. And the largest players then raised the question of which is unfair when a regulator stepped in to the competition, destroying the model that allowed maximumm to benefit from a combination of monopoly position and innovation. We insisted and continue to insist that the priority for the regulator is the development of competition for the sake of better conditions for obtaining financial products and services by consumers. In the end, we create infrastructurenot only and not so much for the financial market, but for the economy and for consumers. And now, when the second stage of the development of the Fast Payment System is approaching - the launch of payments in favor of legal entities, the same banks that ardently supported the SBP initially began to worry about what will happen to their card business, a high-margin business, the price conditions of which cause fierce disputes with retail trade. And we still have one answer: we will promote the development of technology and competitionin the financial market in order to achieve the best price and high quality of services for the consumer and the opportunity to be sustainable and profitable for all market participants. Trying to slow down progress, fearing for the stability of existing business models, is to deprive yourself of the future. We must look ahead and, of course, develop modern technologies, making them cheaper, making convenient services for the consumer. The second call flows directly from the first - this is the possession and management of data. Large financial and non-financial institutions that own a volume of data that is not comparable to smaller players will become new monopolies. And this begs the question of how we will control their market power. And also how we will ensure the security, the protection of data, especially when it comes to entering the national markets of supranational players. We consider it important to create conditions for non-discriminatory access to data, To this end, we are also implementing a digital profile project together with the Government. We are thinking about the development of regtech solutions, for example, individual ratings of a citizen or scoring of small and medium-sized businesses that could develop credit bureaus or specialized companies and offer to small participants. Third- and the most ambitious challenge - is associated with the development of platform solutions, when one seller can offer different types of financial products, and the challenge is also the entry of non-financial players into the financial market. including the largest technologicallytheir VidTesN aggregators. This situation also creates a great challenge for us, for the Central Bank. What regulations should be applied to non-financial companies providing financial services? How to regulate players who simultaneously sell products of different types- banking, insurance, investment, some even medical services, non-financial services? Who should have access to the central bank's money? Only banks, like now? Or also fintech companies, other companies that provide financialservices? For example, we can look at international experience: in Switzerland there are special licenses of fintech companies, in Hong Kong - licenses of virtual banks, the Bank of England also began to work with new players according to the rules of the financial market. We are alsostarting a mother about opening up fintech direct access to transactions with the Central Bank. And today, in connection with these challenges, I would like to start discussing with you two major innovations that will require digitalization, a detailed discussion with you. First. Moving towards regulation by type of activity, not by requirements to a legal entity. Now the regulation of the financial market involves a different approach to participants offering different financial products and services. For example, the regulation of banks,companies, microfinance organizations is based mainly on the regulation of requirements for a legal entity, while the regulation of professional participants in the securities market, collective investment institutions, trade organizers and so on is based on the requirements for their activities, that is, we have such a mixed system. The market trends that I have mentioned are pushing us to shift our regulatory focus from legalentity requirements to requirements for the activities to be carried out. If a company starts providing financial services, it will have to obtain a license from us for the relevant type of activity. In fact, this is a big regulatory shift that requires a comprehensive discussion with the market, and we plan to start such a discussion. Second. How can behavioral surveillance be ensured in the new environment? As you know, the Central Bank is a mega-regulator and is also responsible for protecting consumer rights in the financial market. And we see that the development of platform solutions is already leading to the fact that the main sales channel for various financial products is becoming banking, due to the fact that our banks are much more developed than many other typesof financial activity. Banks sell investment life insurance policies, other investment products. At the same time, the products offered are becoming more complex and require real expertise in the field of risk from the consumer. Our not very big practice so far isthat the spontaneous, uncontrolled offer of such a variety of tools to the population can lead to disappointment of customers (as, in fact, happened with the rapid growth of the investment life insurance market). And such a development of the market, which is fullof ignorance and inability of the consumer to assess the risks, undermines confidence in the financial market as a whole. Therefore, we need sales standards, standards for disclosing information to customers. Now we have behavioral supervision tools for non-credit financialorganizations, sales standards and self-regulatory organizations that monitor their implementation play a key role here. But in the banking sector, and we see that the banking channel is becoming the main one, we do not have self-regulation. The model of bankassociations that we have developed does not imply that associations can influence the behavior of their members and even more so punish them for unscrupulous practices. And it is possible to close this control loop only if all the agents sellingthe rodukts adhere to the standards. That is, the question arises of self-regulating organizations in the banking sector. There is a fork in the road here that we also want to discuss with the market and that we must, in our opinion, go through. We can think about the fact thatthe associations begin to partially perform the function of self-regulatory organizations - to develop standards. But the Central Bank will control the standards. Or we should create a full-fledged institution of self-regulation in the banking sector, when self-regulatoryorganizations will have both the functions of setting standards and the functions of monitoring their implementation. In any case, we come to the need to change the legislation, which will allow, through the mechanism of self-regulation, to control the integrity of the productsof both banking and non-banking products by banks. Optimization of the regulatory load We understand that in the conditions of low rates of economic growth for financial institutions and at the same time the rapid development of fintech competition, cost reduction is becoming an importantfactor in the sustainability of business models. And we, as a regulator, understand that a number of actions need to be taken here. We understand that the administrative costs associated with interaction with us as a regulator are also an optimization zone. Financial institutionsjustifiably complain about this all the time, and here, of course, we need actions that will lead to a real reduction in costs associated with our regulatory activities. And here we also see that the main potential for cost reduction is the same digitalianization, so we will implement the PedTesN and BirTesN approaches. The government has launched the "regulatory guillotine" project, and I can't say it's fully applicable to the financial sector, because yet our regulation has evolved under more modernconditions. There aren't many outdated regulations, and besides, our reform to centralize supervision is largely designed to solve the problem of uniformity of supervision. And yet there are a lot of non-workings in our regulation. outdated, redundant norms. We planto have a constant dialogue with the market to optimize the regulatory burden. We decided to create a working group that will accept proposals from market participants on adjustments to regulation. We will look at our norms in terms of assessing their actualimpact - not only the regulatory impact, when it is assessed what effects we expect from future regulation. Here we have regulation, And we have to assess how it's impacted and how the goals that this regulation was originally introduced have been met, and our main focus is on outdated norms that overlap in regulation, duplicate each other, and often create arbitration between different rules. But we think that we're going to start with older norms, because for those norms that are, let's say, about three years old, it's still hard to assess their actual impact, and it's unlikely that the conditions have changed much, so we're going to start with the old norms. In addition, we have a task with you (we've been discussing it for a long time), which is to reduce the amountof reporting. We've promised to optimize it many times, and in order to take faster steps than we're doing now, we want to audit the reporting and data provided by the supervised organizations, there's a big optimization resource here, and I think you'll agree with that. In addition, we are already seeing which regulations we can abolish as superfluous. Thus, in banking regulation, it is possible to abolish the N10.1 standard, which limits the total amount of credit risk of the bank in relation to all insiders. Ethat standard, in our opinion, became redundant after the entry into force of H25. There is also the prospect of simplifying the supervisory assessment of the economic situation of banks - the number of parameters there can also be reduced, there are a lot of them. We are counting on working in a dialogue mode with market participants. As for the future of regulation, there is also a question that market participants ask all the time - this is the time to implement the changes. You remember that as a general rule, the period between the adoptionof normative acts and their entry into force is 10 days by default. Of course, we often take measures with a deferred decision, discuss all approaches with financial market participants before the adoption of a regulatory act, but nevertheless, by default, this date remains, and we understand that this is too short a period and we will be ready to increase these terms. And the main thing I would like to say is that we really want to develop all these changes in dialogue with you, so we urge you to be bolder in formulating problematic issues. We are really interested in identifying problem areas and in solving them, so we can only do this in a dialogue with you. And finally. We understand that it is difficult to work in the financial sector. Both the economic situation and the long-term trends so farsuggest that every year the competition will be tougher, the margins will be lower, traditional business models will quickly become a thing of the past, I hope new business models will come. But I believe that our financial system has formed a sufficient margin of safety, and we have been working on this for a long time. And if we do not shy away from solving problems, If the tasks of extracting benefits here and now do not prevail over the goal of long-term sustainability, we will be able to cope with thisand the challenges and make a significant contribution to the development of the Russian economy and improving the well-being of our citizens. I wish you fruitful work at the congress and hope that the discussions will be interesting and useful for you! Thank you!

Title: Speech at the plenary session of the State Duma of the Russian Federation
text: Speech by the Governor of the Bank Russia Elvira Nabiullina in plenary session State Duma of the Russian Federation November 20 , 2019 Performance Good afternoon, Vyacheslav Viktorovich! Good afternoon, dear deputies! The Bank of Russia annually presents at the plenary session of the State Duma the Main Directions of the Unified State Monetary Policy. AsVyacheslav Viktorovich said, we discussed the Main Directions in great detail at the working group, in the State Duma committees, and with the factions. I would like to thank the deputies for their hard work in this area. Your comments allow usto improve both our approaches to politics and the format of presenting our main documents. Traditionally, the consideration of the Main Directions in the Duma goes beyond monetary policy alone. Indeed, monetary policy creates the conditions fordevelopment. And I think it is right to talk about how we have achieved our goal in the past period and how we will achieve it in the future. And perhaps even more importantly, what fruits low inflation brings to the economy, how it affects the developmentof the financial system. I'll start with the economic situation. Economic growth this year has been more modest than expected. But now the economy is accelerating, in the third quarter it grew by 1.7% compared to the same period last year. Growth is supported by a good harvest, trade, and accelerated budget spending. Let me remind you that the delay in fiscal spending has had a restraining effect both on growth in the first half of the year and on a more rapid decline in inflation. Now, according to our estimates, the fiscal policy, according to our estimates, will go from restraining growthto supporting it. For its part, in order to create conditions for economic growth, the Central Bank ensures price and financial stability. This sets the conditions for doing business not only today, but also tomorrow. A company's business plans are not for a quarter or a year, but for several years ahead, and low inflation is one of the key conditions for business planning. Our monetary policy, as you know very well, is aimed at keeping inflation close to the target of 4%, and we managethe key rate depending on what we see the forecast, its factors and risks. A year ago, when I spoke to you with the Guidelines, we were going through a phase of dealing with the increased risks of accelerating inflation. During the year, gasolineprices rose, external financial markets were uneasy, we also expected price increases following the change in VAT at the beginning of 2019. Then we raised the rate twice to ensure a quick return of inflation to the target. In total, we raised the rate by 0.5 percentage points. Butsince then, as inflationary pressures have decreased, we have already reduced the rate by 1.25 percentage points. As a result of preventive actions, the surge in inflation was relatively small, to 5.3%. Then inflation gradually approached our targetof 4% and by the end of the year will be at the level of 3.2-3.7%. The faster decline in inflation was largely due to a delay in budget expenditures - we included these costs in our forecast, this influenced our decisions on the rate. And if we had understoodthe spending schedule, then perhaps we could have started lowering the key rate earlier. Now we see a catch-up increase in spending. And if the rigidity of the budget policy is determined through the non-oil and gas deficit, then in the federal budget it fellsignificantly - from 6.4% of GDP in October 2018 to 5.1% of GDP in August of this year. And only by the end of the year, we see it reaching the planned level of 5.9-6%. Since about a quarter of aggregate demand is implemented through the budget, the uniformity of budgetexpenditures is important for monetary policy to more effectively achieve its goals. This year was really a transition period - a period of adjustment to the increase in VAT and to the deployment of national projects. Our forecast for the next three years shows that inflation will be on target for the entire forecast period, and the growth rate of the economy will gradually increase. Now our rate is 6.5%. This is the lowest value since mid-2014. It is important that the rate was reduced not by accelerating inflation, but on the basis of its reduction, followed by interest rates on loans. Now the interest rates on loans are lower than they were in 2013, when the key rate was 5.5%. In the world as a whole, investment growth has slowed down significantly. And mind you, thisis happening at record low interest rates in many countries. Investment is falling not because credit is not available, but because the uncertainty of the outlook for development, global demand against the backdrop of trade contradictions has increased. We periodically hear proposals to make rates lower, even negative, as in Europe, so that lending grows and economic growth accelerates. But on the fact that that rates will turn negative, the reasons that interfere with investment will not disappear. And in most countries that have resorted to negative rates, lending has not grown, and in some cases even slowed down. But how resilient our economy is to changing external conditions, how healthy our financial system is, this, of course, directlyaffects investments and economic ones. growth. Financial and price stability are the first (if you will, "zero") conditions for economic growth. We are aware that external circumstances are unlikely to become more favorable: the world economy is slowing down, this can(and already leads) to lower prices and demand for our export goods, trade wars are not subsiding. But our goal is not to let these circumstances interfere with the development of our country. What are we doing to ensure financial stability? First of all, financial organizations, banks, first of all, must be stable and must have a margin of safety. This is what our policy of improving and cleaning up the banking sector is aimed at. The second is the accumulation of reserves and changes in their structure. As you remember, during the crisis period of 2014, accumulated reserves helped us cope with shocks: thanks to them, we were able, among other things, to launch foreign exchange refinancing to help our companies calmly pay off external debts, when foreign markets closed for many of them. This year, international reserves increased by an additional 72 billion. At the same time, since the beginning of 2018, we have changed the structure of our reserves quite a lot. reducing the share of the dollar. This gives us more protection, more confidence in any economicand geopolitical circumstances. The third is protection against changes in oil prices and other external factors. It was provided to us by a combination of a floating exchange rate and a budget rule. The liquid part of the NWF will exceed 7% of GDP, andthe Government is discussing how to dispose of this money. We expect that the option will be chosen when the stabilizing, crucial effect of the budget rule remains. The fourth is the de-dollarization of the banking system. We've all seen how large foreign currency liabilitiescan become a problem when external circumstances change. In recent years, we have consistently pursued a policy of demonetization through regulation. The currencyization of loans to enterprises has decreased from almost 40% in 2015 to 24.5% now. At the same time, the share of settlements in national currencies with major trading partners is growing, which also protects us from the risks associated with the dollar. To sum up the monetary policy part of my remarks, we estimate that we are in a bettershape than ever in terms of price and financial stability, and the Government has accumulated enough resources to implement a development agenda, and that's the basis for a much-needed acceleration in economic growth. Now about other areas of our work, which also create the prerequisites for economic growth. Development of lending. Lending to enterprises is growing moderately - for three quarters the growth is 3.6%, but at the same time the growth of ruble loans is steadily kept atthe level of 1 0-12%. Investment activity is constrained not so much by rates as by the quality of the business climate and general economic uncertainty. Of course, the low growth rate of the economythis year is a cause for concern. This is partly due to temporary phenomena, including the already mentioned delay in budget spending, but in many respects to structural factors, this is the main factor. And overcoming structural constraints isan important task for our economy. For our part, in order to stimulate lending to the real sector, we are changing approaches to regulation, including for project financing. We decided to extend it not only to VEB, toequity construction, but also to large investment projects in general. Consumer lending is growing at a faster pace than corporate lending. To cool it down, we have introduced an indicator of the borrower's debt burden in October in order to prevent excessive debt loadsof citizens. This measure is more preventive. Our analysis shows that there are no risks of financial stability here now. And at the same time - and this is very much the case. Positively, the share of mortgages in retail lending has increased. In September, the annual growth rate of mortgagewas 18.3%; this is slightly lower than last year, but it is still good. pace. Mortgages support housing construction, and the construction industry can be a source of growth in other industries. But you and I are well aware that you can't putthe development of construction on the shoulders of citizens without offering them protection in return. And this is exactly what happened before in shared construction. Many deputies were approached by voters with this problem: it is impossible to hold developers accountable, to get compensation. Unfortunately, attempts to apply other schemes for the protection of citizens, including the use of insurance, did not give the desired result. The construction of the law allowed insurance companies in many cases to legally refuse citizens to pay. Now legislation has been adopted (and we also actively supported and promoted it), according to which both the responsibility and the insurance premium are transferred to the fund for the protection of the rights of equity holders. According to the legislation, companies must transfer about 8.3 billion rubles. Today, nine insurance companies fully fulfilled their duty and transferred 1.4 billion rubles, two have so far transferred 0.8 billion out of 2.4 billion rubles. But respect and NASCO, from which we revoked their licenses, must transfer about 4.5 billion rubles. The situation with Respect was the subject of consideration at one of the plenary sessions of the State Duma. I would like to note that the Arbitration Court of Appeal confirmed our correctness and the legality of the orders to revoke licenses. The Bank of Russia sent materials relatedto the company's activities to law enforcement agencies. And what is very important now: within the framework of the working group of the State Duma, additional systemic measures are being developed to prevent such situations, primarily to counteract the withdrawalof willow acts. Further. Since July, our construction industry has been switching to escrow accounts. In this mechanism, the construction is credited by the bank and the citizen does not risk his money. The next topic I would like to touch upon is the development of non-cash payments. Why is this important? It makes theeconomy more transparent, it supports e-commerce, where the seller and the buyer can be thousands of miles apart. It's more secure payments, it's lower collection costs, and so on. But it alsoimproves the efficiency of our monetary policy. Non-cash payments are increasingly in demand by consumers, and we must provide convenient and safe tools: both for transfers between individuals and for payment for goods and services. Five years ago, non-cash payments accounted for only 30% of transactions, and no one believed that the trend would change, but now we already have 65% of non-cash transactions and 35% are cash payments. Since 2015, we have a national payment instrument - tothe Art "Mir", and all intra-country transactions, including international payment cards, are carried out through the national payment card system. The Mir map is beginning to explore the space of the Eurasian Economic Union and the CIS, they are already accepted both in Turkeyand in Vietnam. This year we launched the Fast Payment System (SBP). Now it provides citizens with cheap transfers between 25 banks participating in the system. 10 of the 11 largest [banks have already entered this system. This saves citizens from the bankingmonopoly, when transfers within the ecosystem of one bank are cheap, and to transfer money to another bank and even to another region, you need to pay a high commission, often - interest from the payment. And now we are already testing the payment for goods and services usinga mobile phone using an OR code. Tariffs in the SBP are 2-3 times lower than acquiring tariffs, and equipment for accepting payments is quite affordable. This reduces costs, preserves the attractiveness of non-cash payments (let me remind you: businessesoften complained about high acquiring commissions). And the last topic I would like to touch on today is consumer protection and financial inclusion. Ultimately, the effectiveness of our work can be assessed precisely by customer satisfaction. The problems ofthe past time have been related to insurance - OSAGO. We have been working here for several years to increase the availability of policies in certain regions, the transparency of tariff formation. And the second problematic topic is investment life insurance. Here we encountered unscrupulous practices when people were sold a product whose real income was noticeably lower than the seller promised. On OSAGO this year, complaints fell by 40%. This means that such measures as a single agent for OSAGO, an electronic policy, a naturalrefund, a tariff corridor have worked. And I want to thank the deputies for supporting many initiatives, they were all discussed in detail, in detail, hotly. Tariffs for OSAGO in the country decreased by 3.7%, in some regions - by more than 10%. Asa result of the restrictions, the market has shrunk by 32% as a result of the restrictions, but it was our conscious decision, it was necessary. The experience with the ILI shows that we need to quickly adopt legislation on the categorization of investors in order to protectpeople from imposing risky products and services on them. Financial inclusion. Since last year, we have launched special projects to increase financial inclusion in the Far East, the North Caucasus and the South of Russia. It is there that a significant part of the populationlives in small and hard-to-reach settlements and for a long time experienced a shortage of financial services. Now there are projects of both banks and Rostelecom with our participation using mobile offices, with cash withdrawal through the cash desks of magazinov, expanding access to the Internet and mobile financial services. And as a result, the share of settlements with an unsatisfactory level of financial inclusion in the Far East alone decreased from 17 to 13.5%, and the share of settlements with goodfinancial inclusion increased from 58 to 84%. And we will continue such projects. In our opinion, this is a very important element in increasing the availability of financial services. And in conclusion, I would like to say that we are really seeing progress towards the goals that are important for our society, for our economy. Stable inflation and a stable financial system, a more flexible and responsive financial market. We would not have been able to go even half of this way if we had not received a budget for the economy. the support of legislators. I would like to thank you for your constant, interested, very close cooperation, for the discussions that we are holding to support the initiatives key to the development of the financial system.
