Title: Speech at the meeting of the State Duma of the Federal Assembly of the Russian Federation "On the Annual Report of the Bank of Russia for 2012"
text: Speech by the Governor of the Bank of Russia S. M. Ignatiev at a meeting of the State Duma of the Federal Assembly of the Russian Federation Federation "On the Annual Report of the Bank of Russia for 2012" June 19, 2013 Performance Dear deputies! We bring to your attention the annual report of the Bank of Russia for 2012. 2012 turned out to be quite successful for the Russian economy. The volume of GDP increased by 3.4%. However, it should be noted that during the year the annual GDP growth rate decreased - from 4.8% in the first quarter to 2.1% in the fourth quarter. Retail trade turnover increased by 6.3%. Investments in fixed assets increased by 6.6%. Theunemployment rate was 5.5% of the economically active population, the lowest value of this indicator over the past 20 years. The federal budget was executed with almost zero deficit. True, this was achieved largely due to the preservation of high worldoil prices. Russia's balance of payments remained strong in 2012, although its current account surplus fell from 97 billion in 2011 to 75 billion in 2012. The growth of both exports and imports of goods slowed down. Exports of goods in dollar terms increased by 2.7%, imports of goods - by 5.4%. Net private capital outflows have declined slightly (from 81 billion in 2011 to 54 billion in 2012), but it still remains abnormally high. Included in the capital outflow is the 38 billion "Questionable Operations" position, and since MPs had a lot of questions about this issue, I'll talk more about this later. Inflation rose from 6.1% in 2011 to 6.6% in 2012. Let me remind you that the target intervalfor 2012 was 5-6%. The main reason for the growth in inflation is the poor harvest of 2012, which led to a rapid increase in prices for grain and other food products. In the field of interest rate policy, perhaps the most significant was the decision of the Bank of Russia to increase the refinancing rate and other interest rates of the Bank of Russia by 0.25 percentage points from September 14, 2012. This decision was made in order to limit the growth of inflation expectations against the background of higher food prices. In 2012, the money supply continued to slow down. This is a necessary condition for lower inflation. The monetary aggregate M2 grew by 12% in 2012, while in 2011 it increased by 22%. In its exchange rate policy, the Bank of Russia continued to use the floating currency corridor mechanism for the value of the bi-currency basket. In 2012, we expanded the corridor to 7 rubles, increased the mobility of the corridor. The banking sector grew at a moderate pace in 2012. The portfolio of bank loans to non-financial organizations and the population as a whole increased by 19%. At the same time, loans to non-financial organizations increased by 12.7%. Loans to the population increased by 39.4%, including unsecured consumer loans - by more than 50%. In our opinion, banksunderestimate the risks of unsecured consumer lending, so in 2012 we made decisions aimed at limiting its growth. Thus, at the beginning of 2013, the requirements for the formation of reserves for possible losses on unsecured loans were increased. From July 1, 2013, the risk ratios for such loans will increase to calculate capital adequacy. During 2012, there was a tendency to increase interest rates on bank loans. For example, the weighted average percentagerate on loans in rubles to non-financial organizations for a period of up to 1 year increased from 9.3% in December 2011 to 9.4% in December 2012, for mortgage housing loans for the same period it increased from 11.6 to 12.7%. Now about the so-called dubiousoperations. To dubious operations, the Bank of Russia includes payments of Russian organizations, the stated goals of which obviously do not correspond to the actual ones. At the same time, tax legislation is clearly violated. The real purposes of such operations may bethe evasion of taxes and customs duties, embezzlement of budget funds, kickbacks and bribes to officials, money laundering, financing of terrorism and drug transactions, etc. A significant part of the dubious operations is aimed at withdrawing funds from Russia. In 2012, the total volume of these operations, according to the Bank of Russia, amounted to 52 billion. At the same time, we attributed more than 13 billion to the current account. This may be, for example, payment for gray imports (this figure is not available in the balance of payments). The rest We included 38 billion in the financial account and in the outflow of capital. This is an increase in foreign financial and other assets of Russian residents accumulated as a result of shadowy, illegal activities. In May of this year, we received an official request from the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Russia regarding a number of organizations that were used to conduct illegal financial transactions by the defendants in one criminal case that had already been initiated. The Bank of Russia investigated the direct and indirect payment links of these organizations. Two days ago, we sent a response to the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Russia, which has more than 230 pages. It turned out that the organizations indicated in the request of the Ministry of Internal Affairs are only a small part of an extensive network consistingas a mini-mumm of 1173 one-day firms, through which at least 760 billion rubles were withdrawn from the country with a clear violation of tax and currency legislation and, in addition, at least another 21 billion rubles were cashed out with a clear violation of tax legislation. I gave the numbers without re-counting - net sums of dirty money, so to speak. I used the words "at least" because we investigated only short indirect payment links. Among the participants of the network, we included only organizations associated with the companies specified in the request of the Ministry of Internal Affairs, chains consisting of no more than three payment transactions. Operations were carried out mainly between 2010 and 2012, although some of them date back to 2009 and even 2008. It seems that this entire network of fly-by-night firms is controlled by one group of individuals. It is very important that this criminal case be investigated as fully as possible and the organizers and operators of this network of fly-by-night firms, as well as their clients , the real beneficiaries in whoseinterests illegal financial transactions are carried out, are identified. There is a lot of work to be done. It will be necessary to send hundreds, and maybe thousands of requests to commercial banks, to interview hundreds of founders, directors of fly-by-night firms, to interview persons who openedbank accounts for these financial companies, who received keys for remote account management. But the scale of the problem deserves it. Obviously, one investigator will not be able to cope with this work. It is necessary to create an operational-investigative group of several dozen people, and maybe more. Thank you.

Title: Information on the results of the briefing by the Chairman of the Bank of Russia E.S. Nabiullina, First Deputy Chairman K.V. Yudaeva, First Deputy Chairman and Head of the Bank of Russia Financial Markets Service S.A. Shvetsov
text: Information on the Chairman's briefing Bank of Russia E.S. Nabiullina, first Deputy Chairman K. V. Yudaeva, First Vice-Chairman - Head of the Bank of Russia Service on Financial Markets by S. A. Shvetsov September 13, 2013 September 13, 2013 Performance E.S. NABIULLINA Good afternoon, colleagues. I want to talk about the decisions that were made at today's meeting of the Board of Directors. First of all, we considered one of the key documents that the Central Bank is adopting - "The main directions of the unified state monetary policy for 2014 and for the period 2015 and 2016". This document, after approval by the Board of Directors, and such a decision has taken place, is sent to the Government and the President. It is assumed that it will also be heard at a government meeting on September 19 and then will be submitted to the State Duma. This document is based on the principles of policy continuity, but it is slightly different in format: it is slightly shorter, the structure has been updated. We proceeded from the fact that this structure is more convenient for the perception of the document. We have given our own forecast estimates of the developmentof the economy and have redefined the main goal of our policy to reduce inflation. As for forecast estimates, of course, we proceeded from what is happening in the global economy. According to our estimates, the growth rate remains low. The recoveryof economics in the leading countries - both in the United States and in the European Union - will occur, but not at a very high pace. Recently, many analysts have been lowering their forecasts, mainly for countries with emerging markets. For our economy, this means that the contribution to GDP growthof exports will be negative. Investment activity remains rather weak. Therefore, we forecast GDP growth of 1.8-2% for this year. Inflation, if there are no additional shocks and if the trends that have developed now, first of all, on food prices, at administered prices and tariffs, will continue, will fit into our target corridor of 5-6%. For the next 3 years, we made our assessments of the development of the economy, calculated 3 options. The baseline is based on estimates for oil prices of 101 for 2014 and 100 for the next two years. This coincides with the Government's estimates. As I have already said, we took into account the decision on housing and communal services, although from the point of view of the impact ofinflation, we will see a rather uneven dynamics, if we take into account that in 2013, according to our estimates, housing and communal services prices will grow by 12%, that is, about 2 times more inflation, then there will be zero, that is, freezing, below inflation, and then - in moderation in flutters. Therefore, when determining the inflation target, we had to provide for the preservation of the same target parameter as for 2014 at 4.5% for 2015. Nevertheless, 4-4.5% for Russia are normal and desirable indicators for inflation. In theMonetary Policy Guidelines, we envisage a gradual liberalization of exchange rates to create all the conditions for completing the transition to inflation targeting. This goal is maintained by 2015. From the point of view of creatingconditions for the transition to inflation targeting, a number of additional decisions were made today at a meeting of the Board of Directors, primarily on the structure of rates and on the instruments of the Central Bank's interest rate policy. We have unified the rates for the provision and absorption ofliquidity on weekly instruments, we are introducing a key rate. This will be the main rate that economic entities will be able to focus on. To date, it is 5.5%. In addition, we introduce an interest rate corridor, the width of which is 2 percentage points, and the lower and upper boundaries are formed by fixed interest rates on one-day instruments. In this regard, we reduced the rates on overnight loans to 6.5%, that is, to the level of the upper limit of the corridor. An important decisionis the fate of the refinancing rate. You know that the refinancing rate is practically not provided with liquidity by the Central Bank, but this rate is used in many laws, and in many regulatory documents, contractual relations of the bankoc. The current refinancing rate, although widely used, weakly reflects the monetary policy of the Central Bank. We decided to equalize the refinancing rate from January 1, 2016 with the key rate that I spoke about. Why is this pause given? Just to change the regulatory legal acts, if there is such a need, understanding that the refinancing rate will be formed differently, and so that banks and other economic entities, who use the refinancing rate in their contractual relationships have been able to adapt their policies. In addition, we have introduced a new instrument for the regular provision of liquidity, these are 3-month floating rate auctions, which are needed in order to free up market collateral for money market operations for banks and thus increase the efficiency of the transmission mechanism. This decision was made taking into account the structure of collateral in the form of non-market assets for terms that banks have. In addition, today decisions were made on the level of rates. When making a decision on the level of rates, we proceeded from the following considerations. First, inflation remains above the target corridor, although we expect inflation to return to the target corridor by the end of the year. Second, inflation expectations are stable and not increasing, but remain at a high level. Our task is to reduce inflation expectations. This is required to achieve inflation targets that are serious enough for the next year. And the third consideration from which we proceeded - the task of reducing inflation from 6% to 4.5% in 2014 - is quite serious, even though it was decided to freeze tariffs for housing and communal services. Even taking into account this decision, we have a fairly serious movement - by 1.5 percentage points. Another consideration concerns the dynamics of economic growth. We estimate the potential growth rate in the range of 2-2.5%. Now there is a small negative output gap, somewhere within 0.5%. There are other indicators, such as unemployment. It, despite the monthly fluctuations (then growing, then falling), remains at a fairly low level, at a historically low level for Russia. All this points to the structural nature of the slowdown in economic growth. To accelerate it, we need growth. To accelerate it, we need growth. Productivity. And monetary stimulus here is unlikely to be effective enough. Firstly, there is not a very large output gap, and secondly, rather large inflation expectations - this all became the basis for keeping interest rates on major operations at the same level. The Ministry of Finance is reducing spending, in real terms there is a decline, that is, our budget makes a negative contribution to economic growth and will make a negative contribution to economic growth and will make the whole of 2014, as in fact in the first half of this year. That is, pressure on the Central Bank will grow. The question is this: in this situation, you will continue to insist on structural reforms and so tell Vladimir Vladimirovich his questions: carry out reforms, Mr President. K.V. YUDAEVA Today we announced our estimates of the rateof release and the output gap. To be honest, I was very surprised when I went to the Central Bank that it was making such estimates, because, in my opinion, estimates of potential output and the output gap in Russia no longer makes anyone. And all the reasoning on how effective or not effective the Central Bank can be in terms of maintaining economic growth. they are "on the subcortex" associated with estimates of the output gap. If we believed that we had an output gapof, say, 1.5%, then in our conditions we would believe that the Central Bank can really and should even use monetary policy measures to maintain economic growth. But our analysis shows that the recent slowdown in economic growth has largely occurred not under the influence of some cyclical factors that the Central Bank can influence, but because of changes in structural factors that the Central Bank cannot influence. And therefore, despite the fact that the rate of economic growth has really slowed down significantly, use monetary policy effectively to ensure that the central bank has not been able to influence the economy. it is impossible to accelerate this pace. That is, there will be no serious effect from such a policy. That's what our internalestimates show, and so we're continuing this line. You're probably saying that there will be a lot of other factors affecting output that could cause the output gap to persist or widen in subsequent years. If the output gap goes away, the demand pressure for inflation will decrease, then naturally. we will change monetary policy, including using it as a tool to support demand without affecting inflation. Thank you!

Title: Speech at parliamentary hearings in the Federation Council
text: Speech by Bank of Russia Governor E. S. Nabiullina at parliamentary hearings in the Federation Council on October 8, 2013 October 8th, 2013 Performance Dear Valentina Ivanovna, dear colleagues! Thank you for the invitation to the parliamentary hearings. At the same time that the Government submits the forecast and the draft budget for consideration in the Parliament,the Central Bank introduces the main directions of the single monetary policy. And I would like to devote my speech to substantiating the main tasks of monetary policy for 2014-2016, first of all, the tasks of completing the transition to inflation targeting next yearwith a consistent decrease in inflation in 2014-2016. Why do we set ourselves these goals? In our opinion, they are the best response of the Central Bank to the economic challenges of today. Let me explain why wethink so. The economic growth rate is really very low. At the same time, there are many indicators, economic indicators, which show that this slowdown is not due to cyclical reasons, but to structural reasons, that is, not to the current situation, to the deterioration of the conjuncture, but to the structure of the economy, to its low productivity, to low competitiveness. This is indicated by for example, indicators of unemployment, which remains quite low, and, therefore, the acceleration of the premain can be based not so much on an increase in employment, but on labor productivity, on the growth of labor productivity. Let me remind you how we see the stages of economic development. The engine of post-crisis development in 2009-2010 was the improvement of the foreign economic situation. After the fall during the crisis, demand and prices for our export goods recovered, and this was the engine for economic growth. Over the past year, growth in both physical volume and price indicatorshas actually stabilized, not even stabilized, is decreasing. If you look at this year's data for January-August, we have a 1.6 percent decline in exports. Another indicator that worries us is the current account balance. For three quartersof this year, the current account balance was 29.5 billion, two times less than last year. For the third quarter - 1.1 billion. Last year for the third quarter it was 5.8 billion. This means that exports in the coming years are unlikely to be the engine of economic growth that they were before the crisis (when exports grew by almost double digits) and immediately after the crisis. At the second stage of post-crisis development, in 2011-2012, the driver of economic growth was domestic consumerdemand, which was based on the growth of household incomes and on the growth of consumer lending. In my opinion, it has also exhausted its role as a catalyst for growth. Attempts to stimulate consumer demand lead to an increase in imports and to the "inflating of bubbles" in the consumer lending market, in fact, to fuel inflation. The main factor in the economic growth of the new stage, of course, should be investment. We need this precisely to increase competitiveness and labor productivity. Moreover, unlike in the pre-crisis period, when the rapid growth of consumer demand provided a quick return, now the country needs investments with relatively long payback periods, investments associated with increasing labor productivity. So far, I must say, these investments are very low. It is not easy to achieve such investments, it is necessary to change both the expectations and behavior of economic entities. And to change these expectations, it is necessary to increase the level of predictability of the situation. And for this, it is necessary to reduce a whole range of risks and costs, including the risks of property rights, administrative, corruption, infrastructure costs, costs associated with the tariffs of natural monopolies, and, unconditionally(as for the Central Bank), to give the real sector the opportunity to receive loans for long periods at acceptable rates. A necessary but insufficient condition for the long-term predictability that is needed for investment projects is persistently low inflation. Long-term investment projects are certainly attractive to investors when inflation is low, when there is confidence in the Central Bank's policy of maintaining inflation. This is certainly necessary for citizens, once again, for business. and in the investment-oriented model of economic growth. This is what our policy is set up for in the coming years. We base our monetary policy on the analysis of scenarios for the development of the economy. The Central Bank also makes its forecast estimates. Of course, we look at the Government's forecast estimates, but we also make our own forecast estimates, and we will increase this competence, because, as Valentina Ivanovna said, a reliable forecast is a very important quality for the validity of any politicaldecisions and any management decisions. Our main scenario, I must say, is still slightly more pessimistic for the next three years than the Government's forecast. Proceeding from the fact that growth should be investment-driven, and taking into account the parameters setby me in terms of oil prices, and I would like to remind you that the scenarios for both the Government and ours are expected to reduce oil prices by about 6 per barrel compared to this year, under these conditions, in order to have growth at the level of 3 percent, We needa major increase in investment, which is based on structural changes. And we certainly have doubts that we will get this effect so quickly. It will be spread over time and will most likely appear as early as 2015-2016. Nevertheless, withthe decision on monetary policy, we will base it on a thorough analysis of emerging trends as economic growth. and employment, inflation and other indicators that characterize the situation. Next year is a key year for us, 2014. And I would like to emphasize that this is not just a policy that declares a decrease in inflation (we have always declared a decrease in inflation in recent years), but this is a certain institutional mechanism that, in our opinion, will increase the confidence of the population and enterprises in the policy of the Central Bank, reduce inflation expectations (they are still quite high and form this inflation background) and thereby to make the downward trend of inflationmore stable. In making this decision, or rather, confirming it, because it was adopted back in 2011, we also analyzed the consequences of possible alternative policies, in particular, the proposals that were made to actively stimulate economicgrowth, monetary policy measures, easing monetary policy, let's say, ahead of monetary policy easing. In our opinion, if we go this way, then there will be practically no real effect on growth. And thereis a serious risk of a surge in inflation, because, despite the fact that the economy is slowing down, it is not so easy to restore falling demand for the products of the main industries. Where do we see a serious decline in demand now? First of all, among exporters, from the same ferrous, non-ferrousmetallurgy, in the coal industry. Obviously, stimulating domestic demand, primarily current consumer demand, which can be achieved by monetary stimulus measures is unlikely to help in such a situation, it will not immediately give anything for the growth of demand in the relevant sectors, which means that all our monetary stimulus can simply go into price increases and inflation, will provoke a new round of growth in tariffs of natural monopolies and tariffs for housing and communal services. By the way, sociological surveys have been showing for several years, That it is utility tariffs and inflation that are the main problems for our population, so lowering these parameters allows us not only to create conditions for sustainable and balanced growth, but also to maintain social stability. Lowering the inflation ratewill also reduce interest rates on loans in the economy on a long-term basis. By the way, I would like to briefly dwell on what the real level of interest rates the Central Bank keeps on its instruments. Many people believe that this level is still limited tothe refinancing rate, which is 8.25 percent. This is not the case. Moreover, we recently decided to stop any operations on this refinancing rate altogether. Now it is playing. a purely reference role. The main operationsare conducted at the key rate, which is 5.5 percent, that is, below annual inflation, and we decided that in 2016 we will equate the reference refinancing rate with the key rate. We can't do it quickly. Why? Because the refinancing rate includes fines, subsidies, and many other payments in the economy. And we want to give the Government and other economic agents the opportunity to adapt to this new policy of the Central Bank, and therefore we will equalize the rates not now, but in twoyears, so that these decisions are made. Nevertheless, I ask you to pay attention, basically, on the key rate. And one more thing. Central bank rates are just one of many factors that affect the final cost of credit forborrowers in the economy. Central Bank rates and final rates differ at least twice. In my opinion, there are three main factors here. The first is that the final rates include the so-called risk premium that banks put into interest rates, and it's caused by the low level of protection of creditors' rights, the lack of transparency of borrowers, administrative costs. And reducing these risks, which are higher than in many other countries, requires serious legislative work. And we have already initiated consideration of a number of issues, including, for example, on issues such as liens. We are also engaged in an inventory of our regulatory documents in order to reduce the excessive administrative burden on banks. And, of course, banks, as well as allsubjects of economic activity, enterprises, need to reduce their own costs. The second factor that affects the level of rates is the insufficient level of competition in various segments of banking services. And the third is the unbalanced structure of loan portfolios, the enthusiasm of banks in recent years for the segment of consumer lending, especially unsecured lending, which gives a fairly high level of return, profitability. And I must say that the growth rate of consumertrade was three times higher than lending to enterprises. This skewed loan portfolio, of course, also affects interest rates. We are now taking measures to ensure that to gradually cool this market. Next, I would like todwell more timidly on what consequences inflation targeting has for the policy of the Central Bank, the economy, as well as on some key parameters of our policy. As an indicator of inflation, we propose to take the consumer price index. Other central banks sometimes use an indicator of core inflation, which is cleared of volatile components - such as food prices, administratively regulated tariffs for the services of natural monopolies. And, of course, theCentral Bank has less influence on the consumer price index as a whole, but we believe that this indicator, the core inflation index, it is not very clear to both the population and economic entities, so we propose to use the consumer price index. As specific targets , we propose the following: 5 percent for 2014, 4.5 percent for 2015 and 4 percent for 2016. These are quite ambitious, but, in our opinion, achievable goals. When calculating these benchmarks, we use well-known information, including the Government's plans to index the tariffs of natural monopolies, food price forecasts. But it is clear, that life is richer than forecasts, and therefore the real significance of these factors may in practice differ from what we expected when settingsuch parameters. In this regard, we made a decision: setting a target for inflation, set an interval of permissible inflation values plus or minus 1.5 percentage points. If inflation, under the influence of unforeseen factors, deviates from thistarget, but falls within this interval, then we will not change our monetary policy. If it goes beyond these limits, then, accordingly, it is possible to change monetary policy. In our view, this will allow us to avoid excessivetightening of monetary policy in response to strong but temporary factors, such as we have seen in past years, for example, related to drought, to poor harvests. In order not to specifically tighten monetary policy, responding to a surge in certain prices, we propose to establish such an interval. The next important point is the exchange rate policy. Already, the exchange rate in Russia is floating. We use interventions only to smooth out fluctuations, we plan to start open market interventions to replenish the Reserve Fund and the NWF by the decision of the Ministry of Finance, but when switching to inflation targeting, we plan to abandon interventions precisely in order to maintain the exchange rate. The fact is that in monetary and foreign exchange policy, as well as, probably, in life, it is impossible to achieve several goals with one tool alone, to chase two birds with one stone. And in the face of the high volatility of external factors, life here presents us with various surprises. Now it's, for example, problems with the approval of the budget, the debt ceiling in the United States. Everyone was waiting for the US to withdraw from non-standard monetary policy. In these conditions, it is impossible to simultaneously restrain the volatility of both interest rates and exchange rates. And some of thesefactors should take the brunt of the acceptance of external volatility. For many years, we had experience in targeting the exchange rate. And we know what consequences this often led to - to shock changes in our financial policy. And, when we were holding the exchange rate, how volatile interest rates were, interest rates were soaring very high then. Now, in our opinion, it is very important from the point of view of monetarypolicy to ensure the stability of interest rates, because the stability of interest rates is what is important for all economic entities. I'll be quick to say that we're streamlining our interest rate policy instrumentsin order to achieve the effect of our decisions on final rates. I've already said that there's a whole transfer mechanism between what decisions we make on our rates and the rates at which loans are issued in the economy. . And we need to make it more effective. To this end, we decided to simplify our tools, to make them more understandable for the market. And the main tool for providing liquidity to banks is our weekly repo operations on an auction basis. In addition to the fact that we are improving such instruments for providing liquidity, studying the practice of other central banks that create instruments that stimulate the growth of certain types of lending, discussing the possibility of creating our own kind andtools. And here for us the priority is loans to small and medium-sized businesses, and here with the Government we have made progress in discussing this mechanism, and we could refinance. in fact, tools based on loans to small andregular businesses. And the second such tool that we are currently working on is refinancing for investment projects, so to speak, refinancing for investment. The work is still only at the initial stage, but we believe that wecould launch and develop such an instrument. We predict that if the main scenario of our forecast is implemented, lending growth will be about 15 percent per year. I must say that this growth rate is ahead of gdp growth and, if compared with many other countries, is higher than the growth rate of lending in European countries. and in the United States. Now the main thing for us is to create long-term conditions, long-term macroeconomic stability in order to ensure the transitionof our economy to an investment-grade growth model. Thank you very much for your attention.

Title: Speech by the Chairman of the Bank of Russia at the meeting of the State Duma of the Federal Assembly of the Russian Federation with the presentation of the "Main directions of the unified state monetary policy for 2014 and the period 2015 and 2016"
text: Speech by The Chairman of the Bank of Russia E. S. Nabiullina at the meeting of the State Duma of the Federal Assembly of the Russian Federation with the presentation of the "Main Directions of the Unified State Monetary Policy" for 2014 and the period 2015 and 2016" 20 November 2013 November 20, 2013 Performance Dear Sergey Evgenyevich, dear colleagues! The maindirections of the unified state monetary policy are developed in accordance with Article 45 of the Law on the Central Bank. This year we have prepared a document in an updated format. It's shorter. The focus of the document is on monetary policy issues, and not on all areas of the Central Bank's activities (let me remind you that we have planned a separate document on the main directions of financial market development). On the recommendation of the State Duma deputies, we added a glossary, a table onmonetary policy in other countries, but the main thing, as it seems to us, is to strengthen the strategic nature of the document. The main challenge for all of us, and monetary policy must also respond to, is the transition to a new qualityof economic growth. The old model of development, based not just on high, but on constantly rising commodity prices, has obviously exhausted itself. For six quarters in a row, unfortunately, growth rates are declining. Instead of 5-6% growth, the new norm is 1.5-2%. And, unfortunately, according to the Central Bank's estimates, this is not a short-term cyclical slowdown caused by the worsening of the crisis in global markets. The slowdown is structural in nature. And it is associated with the exhaustion of opportunities for recovery growth - with the reloading of production capacities, the expansion of employment and, especially recently, the growth of wages and consumer lending. For example, in the area of consumer lending, we estimate that there are already elements of overheating: an excessively highlevel of debt growth relative to the income of a wide group of borrowers. And as a result, consumer lending can become not so much an engine of growth as a threat to financial stability. Then the question is, what should theeconomy do? I am convinced that it is due to investment. But we are interested not just in terms of volume indicators of investment, but their conjugation: first, with the growth of labor productivity, with technological modernization, and, secondly, with the diversification of the structure of the economy. The entire economy should become "friendly" to projects with a long payback. Investors need to have confidence in the success and sustainability of their businesses for years to come. Broadening investors' planning horizon certainly requires notable progress in many areas. The best contribution of monetary policy to improving the investment climate, which is important for economic growth, will beprice stability and reduced macroeconomic uncertainty. In recent years, some progress has been made here and moving forward. we should never risk these conquests. Inflation is very easy to disperse, but it is immeasurably more difficult to curb it. And we must not forget that it, and not, for example, the exchange rate, most of all "hits" the well-being of ordinary people, the purchasing power of wages and pensions. Therefore, the principle of our policy for the next three years is to achieve the goal. The task of the Central Bank is to find in its solutions the right balance between economic growth and price growth. Stability. Monetary policy will not be so tight as to suppress economicgrowth, but it will not be so soft as to accelerate inflation. To achieve this, it is necessary to complete the transition to a new way of conducting policy - inflation targeting, which began in 2011. The Central Bank not only declares the needto reduce inflation, but also, together with the Government, sets inflation targets, publicly assumes these obligations and then also publicly reports on their achievement, or on the reasons for deviations. In this regard, of course, the importance of interaction between the Central Bank and the Government increases, both in the formation of realistic forecasts and in determining policy in the field of regulated tariffs. The role of non-monetary factors in inflation is obvious to everyone. And therefore I want to emphasize that the containment of tariffs, which isthe same in the housing and utilities sector, is a key element in the success of the entire policy to reduce inflation. We propose to move to setting targeted inflation targets, rather than interval ones, as we do now. This will increase the rigidity of obligations and give a clearer benchmark to economic entities . The consumer price index will be used as a target indicator, and not core inflation, since it is much more understandable, familiar to both the population and business. But since the consumer price index contains many components thatwill be affected by factors of a non-monetary nature, primarily temporary, seasonal action, we propose to establish a corridor of possible deviations of 1.5%. It may seem that we are giving ourselves relief. I want to say that this is not the case. We are doing this so that , in the conditions of a large weight of non-monetary factors, we do not pursue an excessively rigid or excessively soft policy. But the threat of deviation from the target the indicator on the medium-term horizon will be a signal of policy change. The specific targetsproposed in the document before you are 5% for 2014, 4.5% for 2015 and 4% inflation for 2016. These are challenging but achievable targets. The next direction is monetary policy. Today, the Central Bank does not seek to maintain anyfixed level of the exchange rate and conducts interventions only to smooth out fluctuations or replenish the Reserve Fund and the NWF. We have to remove the contradictions between our main policy tool, operations to provide liquidity to banks, and operations in the foreign exchange market. We need to eliminate the situation, and we will do this, when we simultaneously increase the provision of liquidity through repo operations and withdraw liquidity through regular interventions. However, this does not mean a complete reckoning. Aza from foreign exchange transactions. We will continue the operations that we conduct for the Ministry of Finance. In addition, we are now studying the experience of other countries in carrying out foreign exchange transactions in a floating exchange rate, but in order to maintain financial stability. Another area of our work is to streamline liquidity instruments to increase the impact of our decisions on inflation and on final interest rates in the economy. We decided to simplify this system of instruments. Now we have more than 20 instruments with different urgency, collateral, interest rates. Not all of them are in demand. So we are introducing a simpler system. which is based on the key rate. Now it is 5.5%. I would like to draw your attention to the fact that this islower than inflation. In addition, we have introduced a regular three-month auction loan secured by non-market assets at a floating rate. Of course, all our decisions on rates will be based on forecasts of economic development, inflation indicators , growth rates, unemployment, and capacity utilization. This year we present 4 scenarios in our paper. Two of them, as usual, are stressful - with low and high oil prices. One scenario is our baseline scenario, whichseems the most realistic to us. It assumes that the economy will grow at a rate of 2-2.5% per year, and by the end of the 3-year period - 3%. The main growth factor at this stage will remain private consumption, and investment growth will be 3-3.8%. In this scene, we achieve our inflation targets while gradually reducing the current small negative gap between the potential and actual production. The growth rate of lending will be 15%, which will be about twice thegrowth rate of nominal GDP. In other words, the growth rate of lending will be a supporting, not a deterrent, to economic growth. We also expect a gradual reduction in nominal lending rates for final borrowers. This will be twoyears - this is lowering inflation and taking measures that legislators are now preparing, in particular, to reduce the risks associated, first of all, with the opacity of borrowers. And here we are very much counting on joint work with State Duma deputies in the development ofsuch legislative initiatives. By the way, we are now actively working with banks, the Government, and colleagues in the State Duma on measures that will stimulate lending to small and medium-sized businesses, as well as the development of mortgage lending. Another scenario presented in the document is the Government's scenario. It assumes a high rate of implementation of structural reforms and their impact on GDP growth rates. This scenario is very desirable, but we believe that it is a little less likely than the baseline scenario on which we are orienting our policy. If it is implemented, it will not require fundamental changes in monetary policy, since as a result of structural reforms, potentialGDP growth will accelerate. With this, I would like to finish a brief description of the Main Directions due to the allocated time, thank the deputies of the State Duma for their joint work in the committees and I am ready to answer your questions and comments. Thank you.

Title: Speech by the Governor of the Bank of Russia at the conference "Actual issues of implementing state policy in the field of combating the legalization (laundering) of proceeds from crime and the financing of terrorism"
text: Speech by Bank of Russia Governor E. S. Nabiullina at the conference "Actual issues of implementation state policy in the field of combating the legalization (laundering) of proceeds from crime, and the Financing of Terrorism" on 18 December 2013 December 18, 2013 Performance Good afternoon, colleagues. I want to say a few words about the banking system. In general , in 2013, the banking sector showed growth in all major indicators - in terms of assets, loans, deposits. So, as of December 1 of this year, if we take annual figures, the growth rate of assets was 18 percent, the growth of loans to non-financial organizations of theeconomy was equal to 14.3 percent. The growth of deposits of the population amounted to 21 percent, that is, according to the main indicators, the banking system grew in double digits. Capital adequacy in the banking system is at an adequate level. The quality of risk management is also gradually improving. The banking system is ready for implementation basel III international approaches. According to the assessment of resistance to various risks, the banking system even slightly improved its performance compared to the previous year. The Bank of Russia is pursuing a policy to further strengthen the banking sector. We proceed from the premise that the structure of the banking sector should be diversified both in terms of forms of ownership (public and private), as well as in size, in termsof regional representation of banks, and in terms of business structure. The main thing is that banks are transparent, financially stable, law-abiding and reliable for citizens. Concerns about the sustainability of the banking system are completely unfounded. You know, recently the so-called black lists have been circulating, information is spreading about the alleged problems in individual banks. I am ready to say again that this is a lie. Yes, we revoke licenses, but this is not a forced, but a necessary part of the regulator's work in any countrynot in the world. The decision to revoke the license as a last resort of supervisory response is made exclusively in accordance with the law in each individual case. And this contributes to strengthening market discipline and, in general, increasing the stability of the banking sector. The assets of banks whose licenses were revoked in the outgoing year accounted for less than 1 percent of the total assets of the banking sector. Pursuing this policy, we proceed from the priority of the stability of the banking system, make balanced decisions in supervisoryactivity. Of course, the main topic of today's conference is the implementation of state policy in the field of combating the legalization of proceeds from crime and the financing of terrorism. It's an extremelyimportant topic. It's not just us and not just our country , the whole world is facing this problem. Flows of "dirty" money are formed in the shadow economy and seek to penetrate almost all types of organizations involved in the circulation of funds and theirbenefits. The banking system, by virtue of its ability to move funds quickly and to any extent almost anywhere in the world, is very attractive to criminal structures and, as a result, is particularly vulnerable. In order to progressively develop the economy and the financial sector, it is necessary to change the situation when a significant part of financial resources is diverted into illegitimate financial transactions. Unfortunately, 2013 confirms the persistence of problems in this area. The first problem is the withdrawal of capital forthe first time on dubious grounds. According to the Bank of Russia, in 2012 the volume of such withdrawal amounted to 39 billion US dollars, for 9 months of 2013 - about 22 billion US dollars. We have to admit that recently for these purposes unscrupulous economic entities have been actively using the opportunities associated with facilitated procedures for the movement of goods and control within the Customs Union. According to our estimates, In 2012-2013, about 47 billion US dollars were withdrawn from the Russian Federation through the countries of the Customs Union. The second problem is cashing out. According to our assessments and the assessments of international experts, the use of cash in large volumes - in greater than is necessary to serve the reasonable,economically and justified needs of the legal economy - is a serious risk factor for the legalization of proceeds from crime, evasion of taxes and customs payments, receipt of the proceeds of corruption and the financing of terrorism. Annual cashing volumes in Russia are estimated at hundreds of billions of rubles. Under the current circumstances, the Bank of Russia, as a supervisory authority, cannot but respond to these challenges and threats. Every year, credit institutions send several million messages to Rosfinmonitoring containing information about operations that meet certain criteria, as established by law. Analysis shows that approximately two-thirds of such messages relate to operations that the banks themselves qualify as suspicious. And here, of course, the question arises: if credit institutions qualify certain operations as suspicious, then should they comply with customer orders to conduct such operations, should they continue to serve customers conducting such operations? According to the Bank of Russia, the system that existed until recently - before the adoption of amendments to the legislation this summer - was rather a system of subsequent response to negative events. Obviously, that the system should be focusedprimarily on preventive response - preventing and preventing the penetration of criminal proceeds both into the financial sector and into the economy of the country as a whole. This opportunity for preventive response was provided by lawmakers this summer. This is an extremely important legislative innovation. To date, banks have fairly broad powers: - 1) not to open bank accounts for a wide range of situations that cause them concern that such an account (deposit) couldbe used for the purpose of legalization (laundering) of proceeds from crime; - 2) refuse to execute the client's order to perform the operation, except for operations for crediting funds received on the account of an individual or legalentity; - 3) have the right to terminate the bank account agreement with the client in case of two or more decisions to refuse to execute it within a calendar year orders to perform a transaction. That is, in fact, the whole setof measures that are taken out of the "know your customer" principle. The issue of the implementation by credit institutions of new powers, the rights obtained is one of the priorities for the Bank of Russia. Our actions are aimed at ensuring that banks widely use the rights granted to them, including the adoption of internal control rules in order to counter the laundering of proceeds from crime. In order to promptly prevent the occurrence of situations that threaten not only the interests of creditors andbusiness owners of credit institutions, but also the banking system as a whole, active work is being carried out within the framework of the Letter of the Bank of Russia dated September 4, 2013 No. 172-T "On Priority Measures for the Implementation of Banking Supervision". Work with all banks is carried outin a planned mode, and decisions on the application of various supervisory response measures are made by the Bank of Russia on the basis of the entire array of information that characterizes the activities of credit institutions. It should be emphasized that the applied approaches applyto all credit organizations without exception and no preferences are established for large, small, medium-sized banks. Our work is aimed at prevention, not at harsh repressive measures. And I would like to draw your attention to the datathat, in my opinion, quite clearly illustrate the direction of the policy being pursued. Thus, on the grounds of exclusive violation of the law on combating money laundering, 8 licenses were revoked in 2013. Solely on this basis, if there were noinnovations related to negative capital, while the number of banks that stopped conducting dubious operations, according to the results of our monitoring, amounted to 54. That is, banks adequately respond to the measures taken. This suggests that already at thistime credit institutions are using additional opportunities provided by the legislation. I would also like to draw your attention to the fact that the Bank of Russia provides credit institutions with the opportunity to further analysethe activities of a particular client and convince the regulator and the supervisory authority that operations that formally have signs of doubt are nevertheless carried out by customers in accordance with the principles of good faith and reasonableness, are economically justified and legal. And such examples, I assure you, are enough. The tasks of the Bank of Russia for the near future are as follows. The first is comprehensive assistance to credit institutions to introduce into their activities the mechanisms provided for by the updated legislation. Taking into account the novelty of the functions assigned by this legislation to credit institutions, we will place special emphasis on providing banks with methodological assistance on the implementation of legislation. The practice of holding joint events (conferences, seminars, round tables, meetings) will continue, allowing, within the framework of dialogue with banks, to find mutually acceptable solutions on the most pressing issues in the field of combating money laundering and financing. Terrorism. The second task is the subsequentrelease of the banking sector from customers conducting dubious operations and operations related to money laundering. Suppressing the activities of such clients is our common task, not only of the regulator, but also of all banks. Andhere banks will be provided with assistance and control over how the right not to work with dubious customers is exercised. The third task in the context of the topic we are discussing is to improve the banking system by stopping the activities of those participants who actively, in significant volumes conduct illegal financial transactions, money laundering operations, serve the shadow sector of the economy and do not want to change their behavior, that is, those whose business model is based on such dubious operations. The fourth is the introduction of a risk-oriented approach to the activities of credit institutions on the basis of new international standards, primarily the FATF recommendations, which will strengthen the business reputationof the participants of the bank's and financial markets and positively affect the assessment of our country by international organizations. Another priority is the introduction of anti-legalization mechanisms in the activities of non-banking financial organizations,which have been regulated and monitored since September of this year by the Bank of Russia. We are talking about microfinance organizations, credit consumer cooperatives and others. We must do everything to prevent the flow of dubious operations from the bank. In the non-banking segment of the financial market. A few more words about the work of the Bank of Russia aimed at optimizing the regime for bringing credit institutions to justice for violating the requirements in the field of combating the legalization of criminalcodes and the financing of terrorism. As you know, in 2011 the Bank of Russia was obliged to bring credit institutions to administrative responsibility for violations of the requirements in the field of combating money laundering. Almost three yearsof experience in the implementation of the relevant powers by the Bank of Russia have shown that the procedures of the Code of Administrative Offenses have not been very effective. The Bank of Russia is obliged to fine banks even for minor, including technical, violations, while the effectiveness of these measures is not very high. Therefore, together with banks, we came up with an initiative to adjust approaches to attracting credit institutions for violations with an emphasis on the application of the norms provided directly for by banking legislation. There are such measures, you know, and they are, in our opinion, more effective. Currently, the relevant bill is in the State Duma. We hope that the legislators will consider it favorably. I would like to express the hope that the measures taken by the Bank of Russia and the Russian banking community to combat money laundering and the financing of terrorism will help increase confidence both within the banking system and in the banking system itself and on the part of the state, and, most importantly, fromthe side of customers. Customer confidence in the banking system, in the fact that the banking system is transparent, Reliable, these are our main priorities and assets. This will help to ensure that the domestic banking sector meets the level that is determined by the requirementsof economic development, social development of our country and international best practices. In conclusion, I would like to thank the Association of Russian Banks for organizing the conference. It was our joint initiative to look at how thelegislation adopted in the summer is being studied, the experience is not very large, just a few months, but the topic is extremely important. I think it is very important to regularly review the results of the implementation of the legislation, the problems that arise during its implementation, and in this matter constantly maintain a regime of bilateral communication with banks. We hope that through the joint efforts of both the state and the banking community, we will be able to solve the problem of effective counteraction to dubious operations. Thank you for your attention. Thank you.

Title: Speech by The Governor of the Bank of Russia at the XXV Congress of the Association of Russian Banks
text: Speech by the Governor of the Bank E.S. Nabiullina of Russia at the XXV Congress of the Association of Russian Banks on April 2, 2014 April 2, 2014 Performance Good afternoon, dear friends. Allow me to touch on two topics in my statement. The first is the situation in the economy and our monetary policy. And the second topic is the development of the banking sector, banking regulation, banking supervision. The situation in the economy creates numerous challenges for the banking system. The trends that emerged last year continue to operate, but new risks have also appeared, including those associated with a high level of uncertainty in the current geopolitical situationand. The Bank of Russia is seriously concerned about the dynamics of inflation. I would like to remind you that this is a priority for us - reducing inflation, on which social well-being depends, and in many respects this is important for the prospects for economic growth. At the moment, it has accelerated to the level of 6.64 percentage points in annual terms, which is higher not only than our target at the end of this year, but also our range (let me remind you, this is a target of plus or minus 1.5 percentage points). Nevertheless, we expect inflation to stabilize by the second half of the year. But the risks that inflation will be above the target of 5% for the current year are still high. The most important reason for the growth in inflation was the weakening of the ruble by 7% against the bi-currency basket since the beginning of the year, as well as the resulting strengthening of inflation expectations. The reasons for this exchange rate dynamics are varied. The first is global economic factors: the curtailment of stimulus measures by the US Federal Reserve, investors' concerns about the stabilityof the financial sector in China. The second is domestic economic factors, such as a slowdown in economic growth, the deterioration of the current account of the balance of payments throughout the past year, the balance of which, however, unlike many developing countries, continues to be positive and even increased at the beginning of this year compared to the beginning of 2013. And of course, the third reason is that geopolitical factors have recently played a significant role, a nervous reaction to them both from investorsand from bank customers. In early March, the dynamics of the exchange rate began to create risks not only for the acceleration of inflation, but also for financial stability. To prevent these risks, the Central Bank changed the parameters of monetary policy. Thereare still a few words about capital outflows. Capital outflow estimates for the first quarter are coming soon, but it's already clear that they're well above our initial baseline forecast for this year. That forecast was 20 billion, but it's important to understand the nature of that outflow. Part of it is the withdrawal of money outside the country by foreign investors and Russian legal entities and individuals. The other part is a consequence of the transfer by citizens and companies of their own fromtheir countries to foreign currency, which they keep, including in Russian banks. That is, the money of residents often remains within the country, they are simply converted from rubles to foreign currency. At the same time, according to the items of the balance of payments, we see an increase in capital outflow as a result of the growth of foreign assets of banks. which are increasing accordingly due to the growth of foreign currency deposits. In turn, the growth in demand for foreign currency leads to an increase in interventions by the Bank of Russia, and such processes, in our opinion, should be taken into account when interpreting the nature of capital outflow. By the way, despite the understandable conversion of ruble deposits into foreign currency deposits, the share of foreign currency deposits in banks remains at an acceptable level. As of mid-March, it was 21%. Inflation is taking place against the backdrop of still low rates of economic growth, and the greatest concern, of course, is the investment downturn. And obviously, in conditions of high uncertainty, it will be very difficult to restore investment growth. But this is our main task, ours together with the Government. The situation with consumer demand looks somewhat more stable now, which even accelerated in February. If we talk, returning to the exchange rate, about the effect of the weakening of the ruble on growth, it is so far, it is ambiguous. Many producers note the presence of a positive effect, but it is partially compensated by the rise in price of borrowing denominated in foreign currency, as well as an increase in the prices of imported components and investment goods. The Bank of Russiaregularly updates the main parameters of its forecasts, and we currently believe that the implementation of our forecast, the main forecast for economic growth in The year 2014 we represented last year is unlikely. We assumed that growth would be 1.5-1.8%. Now, in our opinion, it is more likely that the growth rate will slow down to below 1%. I would like to note that the unemployment rate remains relatively stable despite the slowdown in economic growth. This may be partly due to the actionof internal factors, but in general it indicates a high proportion of structural factors in the economic slowdown. Of course, it is necessary to analyze not only the general unemployment rate, but also other indicators that characterize the situation on the labor market - incompleteness, forced vacations. And here we are observing a slight decrease in the intensity of labor use. Nevertheless, in general, the situation on the labor market does not yet cause concern. And in such circumstances, the Bank of Russia, when forming the monetary policy,primarily acts on the basis of considerations of price and financial stability. In this regard, on March 3, at the Board of Directors, we changed the parameters of monetary policy. The key interest rate was raised to 7%. And at the next Council of Directors, on March 14, a signal was given that it would not decline over the coming months. at least until the June meeting of the Board of Directors. Raising rates allows you to limit inflation risks and reduces the possibility of speculation in the foreign exchange market. Inaddition, we have increased the size of accumulated interventions, which lead to a shift in the boundary of the currency corridor, which made it possible to stabilize the ruble exchange rate. The Russian currency returned to the values of mid-February at a lower level than in February.At the same time, the amount of liquidity in the system remained at a level sufficient to keep interest rates within our interest rate corridor, - 6-8%. Meanwhile, in the last days of March, there was a slight excess of the upper limit. Throughout the year, when formulating monetary policy, we will continue to proceed from the considerations of maintaining price and financial stability, but, of course, we will take into account the situation in the economy when making decisions- with economic growth, with unemployment and other factors. When implementing the exchange rate policy, we still plan a gradual transition to the inflation targeting regime, but we reserve the opportunity to useinterventions to ensure financial stability after the transition is completed. Due to the high uncertainty at the moment, we maintain the parameters of the exchange rate policy at the values that are necessary to prevent excessive fluctuations in the exchange rate, but after stabilizing We will continue the gradual transition to a floating exchange rate. In addition, realizing what impact our decision to raise the key rate may have, we are starting to introduce a special tool that will allow banks torefinance for a long time secured by investment loans - this, along with expanding the experiment and expanding refinancing for loans to small and medium-sized businesses. We hope that the law on securitization will also work here, which will allow the Bank of Russia to work in the region. refinance banks that are engaged in lending to small and medium-sized businesses. Nevertheless, this is a special tool that will support banks engaged in investment lending. We believe that the availability of long-term resources for banks will create opportunities for further expansion of financing of investment projects. Now let me turn to the development of the banking sector as a whole, banking regulation and supervision. Despite the difficult macroeconomic background, which I spoke about at the beginning, this year the dynamics of the development of the Russian banking sector remains high, which is based on the growth of lending. The growth of assets, loans to the economy, and the capital of banks is stillsignificantly ahead of GDP growth. And now we have every reason to believe that the targets that were defined in the Strategy for the Development of the Banking Sector for the Period up to 2015, will be achieved. The annual growth of corporate loans in 2012-2013 was 12.7%. This year we saw an increase of up to 17%. However, we should not be fooled by this growth, because to a large extent this is due to the revaluation of foreign currency loans. According to our estimates, in order to maintain sustainableeconomic growth, lending growth should be at the level of 12-15% per year. The dynamics of consumer lending is normalized - it is becoming more Balanced. This is also due to the regulatory measures taken last year and thanks to a more prudent policy of the banks themselves. Now the growth rate of consumer loans is at the level of 27.4 percentage points. The structure of lending to the population is improving. Against the background of a decrease in the growth rate of the unsecured segment,the expansion of the mortgage segment continues. Lending. Its growth rate is 33%. The growth of car loans is 22%. And we assess this dynamics as fairly normal, we expect a gradual decline in unsecured consumer lending. Of course, the main taskof the bank's system is not only to maintain its indicators sustainable, but above all to provide financing for the development of the economy. The needs of the economy imply further expansion of access to credit and lower interest rates. Over the pastyear, the weighted average interest rates on corporate loans decreased from 12.2 to 10.6%, and on loans to individuals by 3 percentage points. This trend, in our opinion, should continue - bearing in mind the growing trend to reduce inflation, and thework of the banking sector to reduce costs and increase its own internal efficiency. Is the banking system ready to ensure the implementation of tasks to finance economic growth? Resource base. High rates of deposit growth remain. Although this year they have decreased, they remain very high: as of March 1- 17.5% year-on-year. The inflow of deposits of legal entities increased to 24.3%, that is, resources enter the banking system. A significant source of expanding the resource base of bankslast year was the funds of the Central Bank of the Russian Federation. Their volume for the year increased by 1.7 times, and by the beginning of this year the share of bank funds in the liabilities of banks was 7.7 percentage points. By the way, Last year, when switching to new instruments for the redesign of liquidity, we made a serious decision to change this system and introduced the main tool - a weekly repo, which was also mentioned by Garegin Ashotovich. In our opinion, the banking system has adapted quite successfully to these instruments. Such a set of tools allows and gives banks a greater incentive to actively manage their liquidity. Nevertheless, we still have one-day repos. We have We have already held 11 such one-day auctions, and we are conducting them based on an analysis of the liquidity needs of the banking sector. Therefore, it seems to me that all the main instruments for providing liquidity are set. Of course, we are concerned about the lack of market collateral. It must be developed. And at the same time we are expanding the application ofRegulation No. 312. I must say, over several years the expansion has occurred several times. We are constantly expanding the set of non-market loans, which we take, and, accordingly, provide you with liquidity. The total profit of credit institutions over the past year amounted to 994 billion rubles, which is 1.8% lower than the result of 2012. The main reason for the decline, in our opinion, is a more conservative assessment by banks of their risks and the creation of additional reserves. Due to the steady growth of assets ofbanks and a slight decrease in the amount of profit the indicator of return on assets slightly decreased - from 2.3 to 1.9%, but, in our opinion, these are absolutely acceptable indicators. By the way, in the two months of this year, the banking system has already received a profit of17,0 billion rubles, which is 12% more than in the same period last year. The capital of banks last year continued to grow - grew by 15.6%. And the capital adequacy ratio is 13.5%. At the same time, even in the context of the transition to Basel III, the indicator of the sufficiency of the capitalhas changed slightly. And, thus, it can be stated that the banking system is ready to implement Basel III, to basel III standards. And this implementation is quite soft. What risks do we see in the banking sector? One of the risks is credit risk, although the quality of the loan portfolio of banks is quite stable. The share of overdue debt was 3.5%, the share of problem and bad loans was 6.2%. But in the conditions of a slowdown in economic growth, a deterioration in the qualityof corporate loan portfolios cannot be ruled out. Therefore, banks should be ready for this. We also pay increased attention, and you should do this first, analysis of the financial situation of the largest borrowers, concentration of risks in certain sectors inorder to manage these risks. At the same time, we expect an increase in the quality of retail loan portfolios due to the regulatory measures that are being taken and changes in the policy of the banks themselves. As I have already said, the liquidity situation, in our opinion, remains generally stable. Banks have successfully adapted to the new model of liquidity management, and this is evidenced by the dynamics of banks' operations with the Bank of Russia, as well as the results of regular stress tests conducted by the Bank of Russia. We conduct suchress tests. And according to the results of the latest stress test with extremely conservative assumptions in negative scenarios, While some banks may face liquidity shortages, the share of these banks in the total assets of the banking sector and their impacton the systemic stability of the banking sector is assessed as limited. The rest of the banks have sufficient liquidity to cover possible outflows. At the same time, geopolitical risks are significant, especially if our banks and companiesare struggling with restrictions on the possibility of refinancing in Western markets. The revision and change in the rating forecast may have a negative impact on financial stability. We are now looking at how we can respond to this, including from the pointof view of providing the necessary liquidity, if there is a need for this. Next, about banking regulation, banking supervision, and the preparation of legislative proposals. I would like to dwell on the issues of our supervisory policy. Firstly, we pay the closest supervisory attention to banks that may have an increased concentration of risks, including on the business of owners, on the industry, on the region, the concentration of investments in non-core assets. And I have a request to banks to respond to this. Secondly, these are banks that have mistakes in business policy, unjustifiably aggressive policies, overly optimistic assessments of the creditworthiness of borrowers, which can lead to an excessive accumulation of risks. And of course, the third category of risks is the deliberate actions of owners, management, leading to a deterioration in the quality of assets, to the withdrawal of assets, as well as to involvement in servicing the shadow economy. The supervisory policy will be balanced, but consistent. This year, the Bank of Russia will focus on banks whose activities are of systemic importance for the country, for the regions, including systemically important banks, banks experiencing financial difficulties, and banks engaged in large-scale dubious operations. We have a whole arsenal of tools, primarily preventive action. And we are focused on preventive activities. But we need to improve some of the tools, and I have said this many times. I would like to say again that it is very important for us, of course, to fight false reporting, because all our supervisory activities are based primarily on reporting, and unreliable reporting is one of the problems. We therefore support the introduction of criminalliability for the provision of unreliable reporting, hiding signs of bankruptcy. In order to expand supervisory capabilities, we will continue to exercise the powers already granted by the legislation, including those related to professionaljudgment in identifying the concentration of risks on the owner's business. We will expand the range of banks to which our authorized representatives can be appointed. Now they are appointed to 58 banks, and before the end of the year we will appoint an additional 100 banks to oops. We will apply those measures, those norms that give us the opportunity to supervise the activities of banking groups, including the right to apply supervisory response measures to members of the banking group, and other measures. I would like to informyou that the Bank of Russia has set up a Working Group on Reporting Optimisation. This topic is always relevant. Unfortunately, not much has been done here so far. A number of decisions have been made that reduce the burden on credit institutions, but I would like to note that this WorkingGroup has much more tasks than it has already solved. I appeal to you to provide us with proposals on cost optimization. related to excessive reporting, duplicate reporting, reporting forms. One of the topics that has been actively discussed recently is the topic related to the allocation of systemically important credit institutions. This is one of the key areas of financial sector reform, which is being implemented at the international level and has been approved within the framework of the Group of 20. Last year, we created a special department in the Bank of Russia - the Department for Supervision of Systemically Important Credit Institutions. Appropriate units are also being created in our territorial institutions. And this year wewill discuss with the banking community additional prudential requirements for systemically important credit institutions, including additional capital adequacy requirements, although concerns have already been voiced about this. We assume that systemically important credit institutions should have such additional requirements. In addition, we can talk about the presentation of requirements for drawing up plans for the restoration of financial stability (Anton Germanovich also spoke about this, we expect a billon this matter), as well as the application of increased, including in terms of implementation, requirements for their liquidity. I want to note once again that systemically important credit institutions are not pampered by fate, which are granted absolution of sins and the right to eternal life, but large organizations, from which, accordingly, more should be asked. At the same time, we are developing our functions as a mega-regulator. I think that although representatives of the banking community have gathered here, the topic of regulation and supervision of the financial sector as a whole certainly concerns you. For us, the main goal for the coming years will be the introduction of uniform regulatory requirements for the financial market, of course, taking into account its peculiarities, but unified, in order to exclude thepossibility of regulatory arbitrage. This will require bringing the quality of regulation and supervision of non-bank financial institutions to a level that already exists in the banking sector. And we have to honestly admit that now the level of regulation and supervisionand there is lagging behind in a number of parameters. At the same time, we will pay special attention to the protection of the rights of consumers of financial services. This is a very, very important area for our work. It is also necessary to introduce risk-based approaches in supervision, which are aimed at preventing violations of regulatory requirements, and it is also planned to establish the institution of supervision of the largest organizations of the non-banking sector. Among the priorities of the mega-regulator are building work on consolidated supervision, introducing the institution of self-regulation and, of course, improving regulation and supervision in this segment of the financial market. This is not an end in itself. The goal is to give impetus to the development of the financial market, to increase confidence in it. So far, the financial market in the country is very poorlydeveloped. And closer to completion, I would like to say a few words about the work to counter illegal financial transactions. Two main problems are relevant here - this is the withdrawal of capital abroad on dubious grounds and cashing out. Asa result of the adoption of legislation, credit organizations have a wide range of tools derived from the "know your customer" principle. And banks now have the opportunity to apply preventive measures. The banking system - this is shown by our monitoring as a whole -has adopted new institutions and began to actively apply them in practice. Of course, there are issues related to the costs of using this institution. and we are discussing at the meetings and, I think, will continue to discuss so that it is the least burdensome, including in resolving the issue of access to databases that will allow banks to identify their customers at the lowest cost. For its part, the Bank of Russia is also implementing supervisory response measures. In 2013, supervisorymeasures were applied to 115 credit institutions in the form of a restriction or ban on the implementation of certain banking operations on the grounds of countering illegal transactions. When revoking licenses for 2013-2014, 16 credit institutions had their licenses revoked precisely for violating the provisions of Federal Law No. 115. The figures show that there is a certain positive trend, and we see a decrease in the volume of dubious transactions in the second half of 2013 compared to the second half of 2012. The volume that we record related to the withdrawal of funds abroad has more than halved, and the volume of cash transactions, respectively, by more than a third. Of the total number of credit institutions with signsof high involvement in conducting dubious operations, which was recorded by mid-2013, 75% by the end of the year did not carry out these operations, that is, the preventive component worked.
