The banks themselves get rid of customers, do not conduct operationsthat are questionable. 75% of banks, I repeat, according to our data, stopped conducting such operations. And I emphasize again, that we always give banks the opportunity and time to take action and stop such operations. But despite thedynamics, the volume of suspicious transactions is still significant. We assume that there is also a diversion of these dubious operations into forms that are not recorded by our monitoring, to non-banking institutions. Therefore, one of the key tasks for us is a unified method of approach to working with non-bank financial organizations. Attention is drawn to the risks of unscrupulous market participants using large banks for the purpose of conducting dubious operations, so the heads of these banks should also strengthen their "anti-legalization" procedures. And, of course, one of the key tasks is to close all channels, reveal all the schemes of such operations, identify the ultimate beneficiaries so that sucha shameful, negative phenomenon in our economy disappears. A few words about the payment system. Recent events have shown an obvious need to develop our own payment system, primarily in order to ensure the reliability and continuityof internal accounts. Let me remind you that the share of internal transactions in the entire turnover, in all transactions that occur using payment cards, is 90%. And the Bank of Russia has now created a Working Group that is working on the platform of the nationaland latent system. Of course, we will prepare our own proposals for the development of legislation, especially since the draft law has already been introduced. But for us, there are key questions about how to organize it, how much we can use the developments that already exist among different players. This system, of course, should be attractive to all participants, not burdensome for the client, non-monopolized and quite effective. Therefore, such work is carried out. All specific tasks are not all, but part of the tasks that I have missed. In his speech, on the development of the banking sector and the financial sector as a whole, they are aimed at making the banking system more stable, more transparent, more reliable for the client, client-oriented, more attractive for investment. It should not accumulate excessive risks. It should be capitalized in order to solve the problems of financing, economic growth, and above all at this stage - the growth of investment lending, Because future economic growth, sustainable growth is impossible without investment growth, and the banking system must respond to this need of the economy and switch more to the development of investment lending. I have already said that we, for our part, will find such tools. I urge banks to work more actively to improve the quality of assets, build effective risk management, reduce costs, increase internal efficiency and intensify work with those borrowers whose activities form the basis of economic growth. Investment loans, small and medium-sized businesses, mortgage lending - the banking system must respond to the challenges facing the economy as a whole. In conclusion, I would like to say that the Bank of Russia has developed a long-termtradition of fruitful cooperation with the banking community and the development of this cooperation is a priority for us. We are preparing and discussing all the decisions that we are preparing and discussing with you. We will continue to discuss it in order to hear your opinion, your criticism, to express to you our reasons why we are preparing certain decisions, in any case. to conduct a constant dialogue. And such an open dialogue, in my opinion, is a condition for the banking system to develop sustainably and provide quality services to the population and business.

Title: Speech by The Governor of the Bank of Russia at the forum "Russia Calling
text: Speech by the Governor of the Bank Russia E.S. Nabiullina at the forum "Russia Calling!" October 2, 2014 October 2, 2014 Performance Indeed , the diagnosis of an economic slowdown is very important for making a decision on monetary policy. Simply put, if the decline in economic growth is mainly structural, then the measures should be, first of all, structural,and monetary policy in this case, monetary incentives can have a positive effect only as additional measures and in combination with structural measures. Otherwise, monetary stimulation will lead to growth. Inflation, capital flight, and devaluation pressures. If the slowdown is cyclical, then that's the basis for looser monetary policy. Of course, the current situation is a consequence of a combination of the three factors you mentioned, but, according to the Central Bank, the dominant factor is still astructural factor. The rationale for this is well known, they are discussed. If we look at the state of the labor market and not only the indicators of general unemployment, the latest data is 4.8%, with the seasonality removed - 5.1%. These are very low indicators of unemployment. otitsa. But other indicators of the state of the labor market, such as the number of hours worked, the number of people on forced vacations, show that the labor resource is in a state, if not full, then close to full employment. Of course, we havesignificant problems in the field of labor, which, by the way, Alexei Valentinovich (Ulyukayev - Ed.) spoke about. This is low labor productivity. And even with high employment, people can both work time and receive wages, but at the same time produce moreproducts - such a hidden type of unemployment. Our economy often adapts to the harsh conditions of falling economic growth in this way. In our opinion, the situation on the labor market cannot be improved by measures of monetary stimulation, structural measures are needed related to the possibility of a flow of labor resources to more efficient sectors, to more efficient production, and to increase Productivity. The second known factor that indicates that the slowdown is structuralin nature is the use of production capacity. Yes, it is not a very reliable indicator, it is measured in different ways, but if we compare the load of production capacity with the pre-crisis level of 2008, we have almost reached it, and competitiveproduction capacities are largely occupied. There are sectoral differences, but if we talk generally, then it's like that. The third factor is the decline in external demand. For the Russian economy, it is largely under the influence of stagnation in the Eurozone, a slowdown in the Eurozone, a slowdown in economic growth in China. And it is difficult to qualify this factor, whether it is structuralor cyclical, because there are structural changes in the global economy, new technologies are being introduced. I think it would be naefve to expect that the demand for our export goods will return to that level. to the structure as it was before the crisis of2008. Part of the decline in external demand can probably be compensated for Stimulating domestic demand, but it is unlikely that our economy is ready to absorb such a volume of raw materials, metals and oil in the current state of the processing sectors. This requires investment in recycling, and this again requires the delimitation of infrastructure bottlenecks. Therefore, in our opinion, structural changes are key: improving the investment climate, reducing administrative costs in the economy - whatAlexei Valentinovich was also talking about, I fully support it, fair competition for That there should be a selection of the most effective projects, investments in infrastructure, but also with a clear priority that these are the infrastructureinvestments that create bottlenecks and give a multiplier on the economy, and the labor market that I spoke about. Cyclic factor. It really is. Some output gap, which is also difficult to measure. But in our opinion, it is quite small, and thereforethe application of monetary stimulus measures can only lead to an increase in inflation expectations. Force majeure factor. I think we also have to take it into account and evaluate it very correctly, because one of the mistakes that can be in ourlithium, and that we have to avoid, is if we're going to act like we're dealing with a short cyclical slowdown. I think it's very important to understand that we have challenges, first of all, Structural and long-term, sothe consistency of policy, which is where Alexei Valentinovich started again, is a very important factor. Consistency with flexibility, and based on this, the Central Bank is trying to build its policy. On what principles do we build our policy? The first is that thereare no restrictions on the movement of capital. We think this is an important achievement of the economic policy of the previous period. And the rejection of this achievement can really set us back many years. At the same time, we understand the concerns of our businessthat access to foreign markets has declined, and there are external debts that need to be paid. So our banks, our companies are in a difficult situation. But, understanding this concern, nevertheless, the fundamental factors that allow us to dealwith this burden, they are also obvious. Still, the total debt is corporate, public external debt in relation to GDP - we have at a fairly acceptable, low level. After the crisis of 2008, many banks and companies worked from their currency position. It's more or less balanced, the debt structure, both in terms of urgency and in terms of holders -basically, debt holders are exporters who have foreign exchange earnings -much better than the situation in 2008 and than even now in many countrieswith emerging markets. Plus, of course, the Central Bank and the Government have reserves for that. to maintain financial stability as well. You need flexibility in tools. We recently decided to introduce short currency swaps. I must say, by the way, the day before yesterday, after the appearance of rumors about the possible introduction of restrictions on the movement of capital, absolutely groundless rumors, this one-day currency swap worked, yesterday the currency returned. In addition, we planto introduce currency repo in a few weeks for a period of 7 and 28 days. We believe that this will help our enterprises, our banks to cope with the problems that exist in connection with the closure of foreign markets. The second principle. We talk a lot about inflation, about itscharacteristics. For us now, a very important focus of our policy is inflation expectations. It is high inflation expectations that are the key factor in the growth of medium- and long-term interest rates. It is very important for us to anchor inflation expectations at a stablelevel and maintain them at this level. This is a much more difficult task than achieving a low inflation rate in a particular year. We understand this very well. We are asked: why are you completing the multi-year transition to inflation targeting, andnow that we have a surge in inflation, when there are such external challenges? Do we need to do this? We believe that this should be done, first of all, because of what I was talking about. Our diagnosis: the economic slowdown is, first of all, structural in nature,and this requires an investment-oriented type of economic growth. This requires long money at acceptable rates. In order to have long- Money at normal rates, you need to create incentives for savings, and there should be a low premium for urgency, which directly depends on inflation expectations. Therefore, the transition to an inflation targeting regime, which is not just aimed at reducing inflation, but at reducing and anchoring inflation expectations, we consider fundamentally important. Very often The question is also asked: how is the task of reducing inflation expectations combined with the transition to a floating exchange rate, namely, with the risk of rising inflation expectations following the growth of expectations for a change in the exchange rate? We understand that there is such a dependence, we are prepared for this in advance. We are not going to completely withdraw from the foreign exchange market, we will carry out currency interventions or use alternative instruments, such as the currency swaps that I mentioned, to address financial stability issues. Andmost importantly, we will intervene more often than countries with long experience of inflation targeting do, as they did in the initial periods. when they switched to inflation targeting. And the key factor for us in completing the long transitionto this type of policy is flexibility: flexibility. in instruments - we use non-standard instruments, while maintaining the direction of monetary policy, and in matters of refinancing - we provide Refinancing for non-tradableactivity. Therefore, it is very important for us not to lose strategic goals, to be consistent in policy and to show the appropriate flexibility that time and new challenges require of us. Thank you very much for your attention!

Title: Speech at the Federation Council meeting
text: Speech by the Governor of the Bank Russia E.S. Nabiullina at the meeting Of the Federation Council on November 26, 2014 November 26, 2014 Performance Dear Valentina Ivanovna! Dear Senators, I will begin my speech with issues that are now widely discussed, of concern to the public - in particular, the situation in the foreign exchange market, high inflation and the availability of loans to the economy - andthen I will go directly to the stated topic of regulation and supervision in the financial market. Now there is a difficult situation in the economy. On the one hand, the growth rate of the economy has slowed down significantly under the influence of both internal structural and external negative factors, on the other hand, inflation has significantly accelerated. In these conditions, the Bank of Russia intends to show flexibility, to approach comprehensively, responding to the challenges that are facing the faces. Russian economy, while not forgetting about the strategic goalsof x. The Central Bank takes measures to ensure price and financial stability, stability of the banking sector and the financial market. We use specialized mechanisms to debottle bottlenecks, where market failures also manifest themselves, we take into accountthe peculiarities of our economy and the specifics of the situation. We understand that investments are needed to overcome the economic slowdown and for import substitution. Only on the basis of investments in modernization, in the replacement of worn-out fixed assets, is it possibleto increase the productivity of labor. But in order to increase private investment, of course, bank loans are needed. The state, for its part, also participates in investment projects, but this is the first There are projects related to the development of infrastructure, with investments in the development ofeducation and healthcare. As for private investment, it is necessary to create favorable conditions for investors. For example, we see how many companies now, in conditions of increased uncertainty, prefer to pay increased dividends instead of investing profits. Therefore, a set of measures is needed to improve the investment climate, reduce administrative restrictions, ensure predictability of the tax burden. And of course, along with this, we need to reduce interest rates on loans. What is the central bank doing to do this? First of all, we intend to ensure that inflation is reduced. Low inflation is an integral part of a favorable investment business environment. Many people believe that the trigger for the growth of credit rates was the increase in thecentral bank's interest rate, but in fact, the basis for raising rates was the growth of inflation. If you look closely at how the rate is formed for the final borrower, for enterprises, we will see: the main resource of banks is the deposits of the state. n and organizations (the share of funds of the Central Bank, although it has grown recently, is 9.2%). People and businesses will not carry their savings to banks if deposit rates are lower than inflation. If deposit rates in banks are lower than inflation, liudi prefer to spend (on durable goods, etc.), but not to save. Therefore, the rate on deposits, and hence on loans, cannot be lower than inflation. And even if the Central Bank kept the rate now at 5.5%, as it was at the beginningof the year, with inflation at 8.6% per annum, banks would not reduce interest rates on loans, and the resources received from the Central Bank would rather be used in the foreign exchange market. Therefore, if we want to reduce interest rates on loans, we need to reduce inflation. That's whythe Central Bank talks so much about lower inflation. Therefore, inflation is essentially a tax on the poor. According to polls, the rapid rise in prices remains a key problem for the population. And when the proposals are made: "Let's stimulate economic growth at the expenseof inflation," we must understand that this proposal is to finance not the most effective projects at the expense of the incomes of not very well-off people. Our task is to help ensure that the process of selecting effective, high-performance projectsin production and import substitution works. Therefore, the Central Bank, along with the general policy of reducing inflation (and the necessary increase for this). Key rate) and, given the lack of long-term money in the economy, introduced special, preferential mechanisms for refinancing. This year, a refinancing program for investment projects was announced. Loans from the Central Bank will be issued for three years at a fixed rate of 1.5 percentage points below the key rate. Initially, it was planned that the benefit would be 1%, but with the last increase in the rate, when we raised it quite significantly, we increased it to 1.5%. We have a program for small and medium-sized businesses. Our rate on this product is only 5.5% per annum, but even with this rate, the program, unfortunately, is poorly implemented, and we plan to change it with representatives of small and medium-sized businesses. There is a program to support non-primary exports. Now we are working on a support program for supporting agricultural lending. But, despite the fact that we implementsuch programs (this is not a standard mechanism for the Central Bank), they may be limited in nature, so as not to lead to a change in the direction of monetary policy and an increase in inflation. The main measures to support industries should beimplemented within the framework of state programs that the Government implements. Strategically, we must reduce inflation in order to lower rates. Low inflation is the predictability of financial conditions, which is necessary for the implementation of investment projects. However, we will not reduce inflation to the detriment of the economy, and therefore we always strictly monitor the balance of these two aspects (inflation and economic growth). The Bank of Russia is acting gradually, focusing on a gradual slowdown in inflation to 4% over the next three years. Often there are doubts about the feasibility, feasibility of this task - reducing inflation to 4%. But we consider it quite real, albeit difficult. This level of 4% is adequate to the state of the economy, it is higher than in developed countries, butthe situation there is significantly different from ours. We expect that, taking into account the measures taken by us, inflation will begin to decline from the second quarter. 2015. By then, too, the temporary factors that led to its growththis year will have largely been exhausted. If the Bank of Russia kept the key rate unchanged or even lowered it, it would have had very little effect on economic growth, but we would now have a weaker ruble and significantly higher inflation, which would create risksfor financial stability. In the future, as a steady downward trend in inflation and inflation expectations is formed. we will be ready to ease monetary policy. According to our estimates, this will be possible in the second half of 2015, yes. Now about the situation in the foreign exchange market. There were objective factors for the depreciation of the ruble, first of all, external ones: restricting the access of our companies and banks to external financial markets, lowering the price of oil, the Policy of the Federal Reserve Systemto strengthen the dollar. Against this objective background, speculative pressure on the ruble increased. We have taken a whole range of measures aimed at solving two problems: first, to meet the objective need of companies and banks in foreign currency , including for the payment of external debts, and the second to suppress speculative activity. At the same time, as planned earlier, we abandoned regular currency interventions and switched to a floating ruble exchange rate. The floating exchange rate mitigates the impact on the economy from negative external factors. Now the weakening of the ruble helps the economy to adapt to objectively changed conditions, supports export growth, creates conditions for intensifying import substitution. It is important that we do not miss theseopportunities. A floating exchange rate will also gradually lead to the fact that inflation will react less to fluctuations in the exchange rate. In recent years, we have already observed that the degree of reaction of prices in the country to exchange rate fluctuations is decreasing. The acceleration of inflation now isgreater than if a similar weakening of the ruble had occurred a few years ago. According to our estimates, for example, in the few years preceding the 2008 crisis, the effect of the transfer of the exchange rate to prices would have been twice as great. Butin order for all the lucas of the floating exchange rate to manifest themselves in full, it takes some time to adapt the economy and participants of the foreign exchange market. The Bank of Russia is not withdrawing from the foreign exchange market, we continue to closely monitor the situation and are ready to respond promptly, includinglarge-scale currency interventions, if there are risks to financial stability. I will move on to the situation in the banking sector. This year, banks have faced, on the one hand, the restriction of traditional borrowing in Western markets, and on the other hand, the increased demand for resources within Russia. And in these difficult conditions, lending to the economy this year has grown by 5.5 trillion rubles, or 13% since the beginning of the year. At the same time, the reporting of banks shows that the quality of the loan portfolio is declining. Butinsofar as the Central Bank demanded from commercial banks a balanced reliable assessment of the quality of loans and the formation of sufficient reserves for them, and imposed more stringent requirements on capital, asset quality, we believe that banks can cope with this situation. As banks increase lending to the economy, they need resources. For of most banks, one of the most important sources is the deposits of the population. We see that the pace of attracting citizens' funds to deposits has slowed down. Nevertheless, the deposit growth rate has reached 10% in annual terms - this is taking into account currency revaluation. Without taking into account currency revaluation, the figure is less - this level, of course, is lower than last year, and, apparently, additional measures are needed in order to attract deposits to the Banksystem. In order for banks to maintain the current lending rates, many may need additional capitalization. This is the task of bank owners. the solution of which will show their responsible attitude to business, to creditors, depositors of banks. Now a number of banksare already working on recapitalization - for ten months of 2014, the capital of the banking sector increased by 700 billion rubles, or 9.6%. One of its most important tasks the Bank of Russia sees in the prevention of "diseases", that is, in the detection and preventionof various problems in the banking system at an early stage. And only as a last resort, if the situation in the bank does not improve, we resort to at least the revocation of the license. The Bank of Russia consistently pursues a policy of strengthening supervision for the improvement of health improvement and strengthening the banking sector. The essence of this policy is to cleanse the market of chronically unstable or involved in the commission of dubious financial transactions and illegal activities of banks. It should be understood that when the Central Bank revokes the license, there is no alternative to this decision, all other measures of influence have already been exhausted. And the work to clean up the banking sector should be implemented in order to avoid more serious problems, which is necessary to protect the interests of depositors and creditors. To date, we state that a significant part of this work has already been carried out: in 2013, 32 licenses were revoked. this year it's 80. I want to note that an important stabilizing factor is the stable work of the deposit insurance system for ten years. According to the law, payments to insured depositors begin two weeks after the occurrence of the insured event. The Bank of Russia, together with Rosfinmonitoring, continues to implement a policy aimed at consistentlyexempting the banking sector from clients conducting dubious operations, and terminating the activities of banks whose business model, in fact, is based on conducting such operations. Among the banks whose licenses were revoked in 2013-2014, 76 conducted dubious operations - this was part of the Accounts for 68% of the total number of licenses revoked during this period. A significant part of banks, without waiting for the revocation of licenses, stopped such operations. So, in mid-2013, a high level of risk associated with conducting dubious operations was inherent in 176redite organizations, in the first quarter of this year it was 28 organizations, in the second - 24, according to the results of the third quarter - 14. I emphasize: these are those organizations that are at risk, and we will monitor them and assume that they stopthese operations. The result of supervisory actions was a reduction in the volume of suspicious transactions. We distinguish two types of such operations: illegal cashing out of funds, which decreased by half in the first nine months, and the withdrawal of money abroad throughthe banking system. Over the same period, for 9 months, it amounted to 8 billion US dollars against 23 billion dollars for the same period last year. However, despite the positive dynamics, the volume of such operations is still large. Therefore, work in this direction will continue and we will closely monitor where these operations flow, including into the non-banking sector. The Bank of Russia always acts on the basis of the need to protect the interests of depositors and creditors, including using the reorganization tool where it iseconomically justified. In 2013-2014, decisions were made to reorganize eight banks. We are not acting voluntarily here, but on the basis of objective criteria: the systemic importance of the bank for the economy of a country or region, the economicefficiency of reorganization costs and the lack of large-scale (at the level of the business model) involvement of the bank in dubious operations. Unfortunately, sometimes the management and owners of a credit institution not only do not take measures for financial recovery, but also damage stability with their decisions and actions, and also hide information about the real financial condition of the bank. Unreliable reporting, concealment of information remain one of the most acute problems. Therefore, it is very important to finally applycriminal liability for reporting that hides signs of bankruptcy, and to demonstrate that punishment for inaccurate reporting is inevitable. The focus of supervision is also on the aggressive policy of individual credit institutions in the field of attracting deposits. We believe that banks that attract citizens' funds at rates significantly higher than market rates should also deduct increased contributions to the Deposit Insurance Fund. And here it is important to accelerate the adoptionof the relevant law. We see how difficult the work on legislative acts in the financial sphere is progressing, and we are grateful to the senators for such work. Nevertheless, a number of important problems remain unresolved, including in the field of regulation and supervision, in particularthe activities of rating agencies. We look forward to the adoption of a federal law that will create equal conditions for healthy competition between foreign and Russian rating agencies. In addition, it will allow us to organize supervisionover their activities, so that there is a high-quality and unbiased assessment of our borrowers and issuers. We must create our own independent industry of rating agencies. We consider it important to accelerate the adoption of the bankruptcy law, which will allow usto flexibly use the mechanisms of reorganization, transfer assets and liabilities to healthy banks. We also consider it necessary to legislatively tighten the requirements for the business reputation of bank owners. We support the initiative to allow credit institutions to access information aboutcitizens' progress, including information available in the Pension Fund, in order to confirm the solvency of borrowers. A little more than a year ago, the Bank of Russia became a mega-regulator, and supervision of other segments of the financial market was added to the functions of control and supervision in the banking sector. This is a huge layer of work, tens of thousands of companies: 572 subjects of insurance, 1790 subjects of collective investments, almost 4.5 thousand microfinance organizations, almost 8 thousand pawnshops and so on. For comparison, nude, that we have 842 credit institutions, 790 of them are banks. These new powers required a marked overhaul within the Central Bank, essentially the creation of a new control and supervision infrastructure. The creation of a mega-regulator, that is, the integration of the FFMS, wemanaged 9 months ahead of the deadline that was allotted to us by law. In the work of the mega-regulator, three areas are highlighted: regulation and supervision of financial market participants, market development, protection of the rights of consumers of financial services and minority shareholders. The importance of control cannot be overstated, but it is even more important now to ensure the development of the financial sector as a whole. The funds of pension savings, the reserves of insurers are sources of long-term money for the economy, this is a factor in the formation of domestic andnon-vestor, and the formation of a domestic investor - own, domestic - is of particular importance in conditions of limited access to foreign capital markets. Now these markets are underdeveloped. As of the end of the third quarter of 2014, for example, the ratio of assets of insurance organizations to GDP was 2%, in developed countries it was 30%, pension funds - 3%, in developed countries - 70%. This indicates that these market sectors have a very large growth potential. We believe that the goals and objectives of our policy should be clear and transparent, and now we are working on the draft Guidelines for the Development of the Financial Market for 2015-2017. This document will be, in fact, a strategy for the development of all sectors of the financial market. There will be outlined both the main directions and the main mechanisms. What has been done concretely now. The Financial Supervision Committee (similar to the Banking Supervision Committee) began its functioning. The competence of this committee includes key issues of regulation and supervisionin the financial market. A single inspectorate, the Main Inspectorate of the Bank of Russia, has been established to conduct on-site inspections of both credit and non-credit financial institutions. This provides end-to-end control in the financial market, including reducing the risks of moving dubious transactions from the banking sector to the non-banking sector. In the insurance market, by analogy with banks, the institution of supervision for the 20 largest insurance organizations has been introduced, which makes it possible to identify problems of large insurance organizations at early stages. Supervision of closed-end mutual funds has been strengthened, artificial pricing in this area, which made it possible to "draw" balances with the help of these instruments, has been suppressed. We have strengthened the supervision of the activities of depositories in order to prevent abuses in the accounting of the rights of owners and prevent the presence of fictitious assets in the balance sheets of financial institutions. Since 2015, a guarantee system should be launched in the system of non-state pension funds. Now 44 non-state pension funds have agreed on the corporatization procedure. These are the largest players, which account for 90% of the pension savings market. And now thorough inspections of these funds are being carried out so that only financially stable companies that reliably reflect, among other things, the financial situation are included in the system. Serious changes have also occurred in the field of OSAGO regulation. Within the framework of the powers granted by law, the Bank of Russia has developedthe necessary regulatory acts. In particular, osago rules were established, the maximum size of the basic rates of insurance tariffs, the coefficients of insurance tariffs and requirements for their structure, the procedure for use by insurers in determining the insurance premium, and soon. In the summer, the Bank of Russia conducted on-site inspections of 17 insurance companies with an extensive network for the availability of OSAGO forms. We know that this was a problem when contracts were simply not issued, no contracts were concluded, referring to the lack ofOSAGO bl. The number of complaints about the lack of forms - including, we hope, the results of inspections - decreased by 17%. At the same time, supervision over the financial stability of insurance companies that are engaged in OSAGO has been strengthened. However, there is still a lot to be done in this market, as problems have been accumulating over the years, and the Central Bank will work actively in this direction to ensure that the business model is stable for insurance companies, but above all to ensure theavailability of high-quality reliable services for customers. We have created a special service for the protection of consumer rights in the financial market. We want to make it extensive and expect that the number of complaints will increase as a result of the work of this service. People nowand sometimes just don't complain, because they understand that it's useless, that there will be no response. We expect that as the effectiveness of our work in terms of responding to complaints grows, the number of complaints will increase and we will be able to really work on strengthening control and supervision. In conclusion, I would like to say that, of course, there are many tasks and challenges of this difficult time ahead and we need to use all the chances for our own development that are given. And we proceed from the fact that the financial sector, the financialsector, will develop sustainably and provide financing for economic growth. I want to especially thank the senators for passing the necessary laws. A lot of laws have been passed in previous sessions. In 2014 alone , 42 laws were adopted on our topics, in 2013 - 27 laws, and we hope for further fruitful work.

Title: Speech by The Governor of the Bank of Russia at the XXVI Congress of the Association of Russian Banks
text: Speech by the Governor of the Bank E.S. Nabiullina at the XXVI Congress of the Association of Russian Banks April 7, 2015 April 7, 2015 Good afternoon, dear participants of the Congress! Interaction with the banking community, with the Association of Russian Banks is one of the priorities and an integral element of the Central Bank's work. This interaction allows us to increase the effectiveness of our regulation, and I want to assure you that all the proposals that will be made today, and the questions that will be asked, will be worked out by the Central Bank and will be appropriately embodied in our decisions and regulatoryactions. I want to devote my speech to two issues. The first is our assessment of the current economic situation and monetary policy. The second is the situation in the banking sector. issues of banking regulation and supervision. I will start with an assessment of the current economic situation In 2014, the situation changed significantly for the Russian economy. To the internal structural problems were added significant negative external factors in the form of large-scale price reductions and restrictions on access to external financial resources, and both the economy as a whole and inflation responded to this. The acceleration of consumer price growth since the autumn of last year was primarily due to the weakening of the ruble and restrictions on imports of a number of food products. To contain inflation and inflation expectations, the Bank of Russia raised the key rate throughout 2014. But since the impact of monetary policy on the economy, including price dynamics, is not immediately realized, moreover, since our economy faced, asI have already said, serious external challenges that could not be foreseen, inflation in 2014 seriously exceeded the target and amounted to 11.4%. The tightening of monetary policy, despite the fact that it is unpopular,contributed to the stabilization of inflationary and devaluation expectations of economic entities and maintaining their propensity to save and allowed to avoid a transition to a stagflationary scenario of economic development, which many experts spoke about. The acceleration of inflation at the end oflast year was primarily due to the accelerated adjustment of prices to the changed conditions. This phenomenon, in our opinion, is limited in time. We expect a fairly rapid decline in inflation, if there are no new unforeseencircumstances, and the release in March next year to inflation of about 9% with a further decline. We consider it realistic to achieve the medium-term inflation target of 4% in 2017. At the same time, I would like to note once again, and the Bank of Russia has repeatedly said, that we do not intend to reduce inflation at any cost, and we will do so taking into account the capabilities of the Russian economy. Given that the balance of risks of accelerating inflation and cooling the economy was changing, the Bank of Russia this year twice reduced the key rate, in total n a3 percentage points, to 14.00% per annum. As for our forecast for the development of the economy as a whole, I would like to note that we are usually based on conservative estimates, sometimes weare reproached for this. The baseline scenario is based on the oil price of 50-55 per barrel in 2015 with a possible increase to 70-75 per barrel by 2017, and we base our forecasts on maintaining restrictions on access to external capital markets until the end of 20-17. The adaptation of the economy to new conditions, and these are really new conditions, will be accompanied, unfortunately, by a decrease in output, according to our calculations, by 3.5-4.0% in 2015 and 1.0-1.6% in 2016 and the subsequent fairly rapid recovery grewto 6% in 2017. In the next two years, foreign trade will make a positive contribution to economic growth due to a strong decline in imports, including due to the weakening of the ruble. But consumer demand and investment will still be very weakand. We expect them to revive from the second half of 2016. In many respects, these terms of intensification of investment and consumer activity will depend on the effectiveness of the implementation of government measures to support the economy and especially the implementationof structural reforms. As for the future dynamics of the ruble exchange rate, in addition to geopolitics, it will continue to be influenced by oil prices. However, we do not expect a unidirectional decline in oil prices on the scale that was last year. Last year, the exchange rate was also heavily pressured by the need for substantial payments on external debts in the context of closed foreign markets. This year, current account receipts are comparable to our estimates of payments. In addition, according to preliminary calculations, the volume of payments should be about two times lower. Taking into account the new instruments introduced by the Bank of Russia - operations to provide liquidity in foreign currency on a repayable basis - payments on external debt can be financed without a significant impact on theruble. Thus, the factors that influenced the exchange rate and inflation last year will gradually fade away. By the way, some people associate the strengthening of the ruble in recent months with the artificial quantitative clamping of ruble liquidity, comparing the amount of funds in the framework of weekly repo auctions. I would like to note that, to put it mildly, this is not a completely correct representation. In our opinion, the strengthening of the exchange rate was due to a combination of a number of facts: - stabilization of oil prices; - completion of the peak of payments on external debts; - more even sale of foreign exchange earnings by exporters; - of course, raising the key rate; - development of currency refinancing instruments. We approached ruble liquidity conservatively in December, and you saw then what it manifested itself in - the rates on the money market for several days went beyond ours. interest rate corridor. The adequacy of liquidity can be judged by whether or not the money market rates arein the corridor /B 1 percentage point of the key rate. If you look at this year, the money market interest rate was inside the interest rate corridor. And this means that our transmission mechanism works and there is no artificial clamping ofliquidity. The fact that in recent months fewer amounts have been offered at weekly repo auctions than in December is due to the action of the so-called autonomous liquidity factors, primarily with the large expenditure of funds on the part of the federal budget (andnot to say that the federal budget spends more evenly this year) and a decrease in cash in circulation. according to our estimates, a neutral impact on monetary conditions. Therefore, in 2015 there was no quantitative tightening and this was not the reason for the strengthening of the exchange rate. We should also not expect quantitative easing. Our main tool is the key rate. I would like to talk about quantitative easing. ArB suggests that we implement these programs, and in the speech of Garegin Ashotovich (Tosunyan) this was voiced. I understand the sincere desire to make lending available and spur economic growth. I understand the goals to which this is directed, but I am convinced that many recipes thatare used in other countries will not work in the conditions of our economy and will have the opposite effect. Countries that use such instruments face other challenges that are the opposite of ours. They have low inflation, they even want to increase it, and they have a lotof work. In addition, the effectiveness of these measures for economic growth and credit growth is not yet obvious. This effect has yet to be assessed, including the long-term consequences of such quantitative measures for the world economy as a whole in the formof financial bubbles, underestimation of risks and additional volatility of global capital flows. Indeed, such measures are mainly applied by countries with a reserve currency, which can transfer the consequences of these measures beyond their nationaleconomy. At the same time, the use of quantitative measures in conditions of high inflation and a fairly stable level of employment can lead to capital outflows and additional inflation. Taking into account the consequences of quantitative easing for our country, colleagues propose to strictly control the direction of this relatively cheap money into the economy. That is, money with a low rate should work in the economy without leading to increased inflation and capital outflows. But, colleagues, this means the introduction of additional administrative measures of control over banking activities. I think that banking the community should keep this in mind when proposing quantitative easing measures in the current environment. In my opinion, they still won't work. Our strategic path is stabilization, lower inflation and, on this basis, a reduction in the key rate. You can see that we are following this path and, despite the difficult situation this year, we have already reduced the key rate twice. Now about the situation in the banking sector Despite the difficult external and macroeconomic conditions in 2014, the assets of the banking sector grew by 35.2%, to 77.7 trillion rubles (excluding the exchange rate factor - by 18.3%). This is a fairly high growth rate of assets, higher than in 2013. Interms of the ratio of assets to GDP and loans of the economy to GDP, the targets of the Strategy for the Development of the Banking Sector until 2015 have been achieved. Garegin Ashotovich mentioned this strategy today, we have to update it for a new period. The growth of bank assets continued in January 2015, in February assets decreased, mainly due to the strengthening of the ruble. The total volume of loans to the economy increased in 2014, banks managed to maintain the growth of corporate loans. However, in the first months ofthis year, the increase was 2%, and if we take into account the exchange rate difference, and it is now quite seriously affected, there was a decrease of 1%. The structure of the loan portfolio growth clearly reflects the processes taking place in the economy: it is dominated by fuel and energy companies and otherraw materials industries, the share of agriculture, small and medium-sized businesses is falling. Unfortunately, this indicates a low rate of structural restructuring of the economy. Thus, loans to small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) as of 01.02.2015 accounted for 16.0% of the total corporate loan portfolio of banks, and the volume of loans to SMEs has recently been declining. Therefore, the effectiveness of additional measures (SME Bank programs and programs with the Credit Guarantee Agency) is of key importancee to support lending to small and medium-sized businesses. Loans to individuals increased in 2014, but in January-February 2015 there was a decrease in lending to the population, primarily due to a sharp decline in the growth rate of unsecuredconsumer lending and against the background of a fall in real incomes of the population. An important factor in the growth of lending to the population and the improvement of the quality of the retail portfolio is mortgages. The volume of mortgage debt at the beginning of 2015 amounted to 3.6 trillion, These are serious volumes. In January 2015, for objective reasons, there was a decrease in the mortgage portfolio by 9.8%, in February - by 24%. Therefore, government incentive measures and the real launch of the mortgage program of 12% are very important. The resource base of banks in 2014 expanded largely due to funds raised from organizations. But the deposits of the population, although nominally increased, but with the exceptionof the influence of the exchange rate, they decreased by 2.5% last year. It is encouraging that in the first two months of 2015 there was a revival and the volume of deposits of individuals is increasing, including taking into account the exchange rate difference. Against the background of a slowdownin deposits and limited access to traditional banking sources of external funding, borrowing banks from the Central Bank doubled in 2014 - to 9.3 trillion rubles. By March 1, 2015, the share of Bank of Russia loans in the liabilities of the banking system amounted to 10.1% (a year ago it was 6.7%). The conditions for the work of banks in 2014 were difficult, and this was reflected in the financial result of the banking system. Profit in 2014 is 40.7% lower than in 2013. The main factor in the decline wasthe development of additional reserves for possible losses. For two months of 2015, banks received a loss of 36 billion rubles. Nevertheless, we expect that by the end of 2015 the banking sector will still show a profit of about 100 billion rubles. Of course, we consider the government's decision to recapitalize the banking system, primarily to support lending to the economy, to be timely. Indeed, the banking sector is the first to react to unfavorable external factors, takes the hit. Changesin the economic situation have an impact not only on quantitative indicators, but also on the entire palette of risks in the banking sector. The risk of growth of "bad" debts remains in the foreground. The quality of banks' loan portfolio deteriorated in 2014, mainly inthe retail segment. The share of loans of IV and V quality categories has increased. According to our estimates, sufficient reserves have been created for these "bad" loans. The quality of mortgage loans remains high, despite the difficult conditions and, moreover, it has even grown slightly. Since thebeginning of the year, the share of overdue debt as of 01.03.2015 amounted to 1.4% (as of 01.01.2014 -1.5%). In general, we assess the situation in the banking sector as stable. The Bank of Russia conducts regular stress tests, their results indicate that keyindicators, including the adequacy of total capital in the banking sector, even in the toughest scenario (oil 40 per barrel), remain above the regulatory minimum. This indicates that the banking sector retains a significant buffer of caps. Italy (taking into account the planned measures for additional capitalization) and its ability to withstand serious shocks in the event of deepening crisis phenomena. We continue to be in the zone of high interest rates, and maintaining lending to the non-financial sector is now extremely important. Understanding the level of high interest rates, we have developed special tools, which you are well aware of, for project financing, for small and medium-sized businesses, under the military mortgage program and support for non-primary exports. Limits , which for a long time were not selected, now began to be actively used. But I want to say that they are limited, and we do not plan to significantly increase them. In the banking sector in 2014, a number of innovations were adopted to soften the regulation. This was necessaryfor banks to adapt to the changed conditions. Thus, decisions were made to postpone the entry into force of liquidity standards, including basel III; the possibility of banks calculating foreign exchange assets, revaluation of the securities portfolio. We made it possible to fix ratings for regulatory purposes, etc. These measures were taken quite quickly. We are all well aware that these measures were extraordinary in nature in order to give banks the opportunity to adapt to dramatically changed conditions. And our task now is smoothly and gradually normalizethe regulation. Development of banking supervision In 2014, the policy of recovery and strengthening of the banking sector continued. When organizing this work, the Bank of Russia proceeds from the need to ensure maximum transparency of banks' activities. The Bank of Russia closely monitors banks conducting dubious operations; measures of influence are promptly applied to them, and if violations are not eliminated, licenses for banking operations are revoked. Strengthening supervision of significant banks at the federal and regional levels remains a priority of supervisory work. We have begun to apply methods of consolidated supervision of banking groups, including those involving limiting the risks of credit institutions to the business of owners. This problemis very relevant for our banking system. We are developing the institution of supervision, as well as authorized representatives of the Bank of Russia. The number of banks to which bank commissioners have been appointed increased from 17 to 141 in 2014. We get more analyticaland complete information and consider this as a factor of transparency of banks for the regulator. Nevertheless, the task of increasing the effectiveness of the institution of commissioners as a whole, as well as the effectiveness of supervision in general, remains relevant for us. The Bank of Russia's increased attention remains focused on the aggressive policy of a number of banks in the household deposit market. In the absence of an effective risk management system for individual banks and with low asset quality, such a policy can result in losses and, ultimately, become a problem for depositors and creditors. In this regard, the Bank of Russia is working to assess the policy pursued by banks to attract deposits of the population, including interest rate policy. The creation of a mega-regulator has expandedthe ability of bank supervision to obtain information on the activities of banks, banking groups and financial conglomerates. By the way, about information in general and reporting. Indeed, there are problems and difficulties faced by banks. We intend to actively moveto electronic formats, to restore order, to systematize reporting, understanding that these are increasing costs for banks. I recognize that the problem has not yet been solved. In cooperation with the banking community, we intend to solve it. The increase in the number of revokedlicenses in 2014 is primarily due to the active involvement of some banks in conducting dubious operations, which required strict response measures from the banking supervision. But I want to emphasize that most of the credit organizationsthat fell into the regulator's field of view because of this independently curtailed this kind of activity. The revocation of the license on the basis of dubious operations amounted to 36 banks, or 42% of all license revocations. Part of the revocation of licenses was the resultof financial problems accumulated by credit institutions with the subsequent loss of capital and (or) sustainable insolvency (33 credit institutions, or 38% of the number of revoked licenses). At the same time, some banks hid their real financial situation by submitting significantly inaccurate reports to the Bank of Russia. The Bank of Russia has become more active in applying bailout mechanisms. But what is more important is not so much the change in the proportion of revocation of licenses and the application of financial recovery programs, but the early warning of problems that ultimately lead us to the inevitability of choosing between reorganization and recall. Early warning of problems becomes relevant right now, when a significant part of the work has already been done to withdraw chronicallyfinancially unstable banks from the market. Among the proposals that are being discussed now for more effective reorganization is the creation of a single state bank - a sanatorium. The discussion process is not yet complete; I think it should be done with the banking community. But I will make preliminary remarks. Of course, this idea has advantages: efficiency in decision-making, the absence of complex competitive procedures, the possibility of consolidating several banks, but there are also risks. The first is the risk of additionalnationalization of the banking sector. The share of state-controlled banks in the assets of the banking system is already close to 60%. Another major state player in the banking services market, I think, will be superfluous. And previous experience makes us skeptical aboutthis situation as temporary, that is, to expect that the state sanatorium will fulfill the program of rehabilitation of banks and offer them to the market. So far, at least, we have not been able to implement this. The second risk is the monopolization of the process of financialrecovery of banks. Monopolization of the reorganization process by one state structure can lead to a decrease in competition and interest of private capital in investments in the banking sector. The third risk is overestimation of the cost of financial recovery due to the lack of competition and dependence on one player, so we need to weigh all the benefits and risks in order to make a balanced decision. At the same time, the Bank of Russia is well aware that in the financial market there are difficulties with the withdrawal of owners of private banks from their business if problems begin in it. The use of only a market mechanism, when one bank buys another without state support, carries increased risks due to the lack of transparency of the assets purchased for the acquirer. the current scheme for the completion of banking business through the DIA involves either the revocation of the license or the removal of the old owners and a financial recovery plan already completely at public expense. This topic was discussed at the initiativeof the banking community at the last meeting of the Presidium of the Association of Russian Banks. In our opinion, changes are needed here, the problem really exists. In this situation, we are considering the possibility of proposing to the banking community a new mechanismfor consolidating banks' assets, which simultaneously provides for private investment in the capital of the bank being purchased or being rehabilitated and the allocation of loans from the Bank of Russia without collateral. The cost of such loans should be market-oriented, but the term is not as long as we are now providing for reorganization - up to one year. In order to make such a decision, you need a supervisory assessment of the sanatorium bank, the bank being rehabilitated and an analysis of the transaction itself. We believe that such a mechanism will support the process of market consolidation of the banking sector, increase the interestof private investors to the assets of the banking sector and allow at an early stage to resolve the emergence of problem situations in individual banks. Of course, there may also be risks associated with attempts to lend through the Central Bank to market transactions onacquisitions and acquisitions. Therefore, we intend, in cooperation with the banking community, to work out a mechanism for providing loans to maintain liquidity in such transactions of bank connection. This is designed to create conditions for early warning about A blem of financial stability, primarily in relation to banks whose owners do not want or cannot, for objective reasons, maintain them in working order. The next topic concerns the insurance of deposits of individuals. This is a significant institution forprotecting the interests of depositors in case of problems for banks, but it also needs to be improved. Over the past year, insured events occurred in 61 banks, whose license was revoked. Insurance payments were made in the amount of about 200 billion rubles. Now various options for improving the insurance system are being actively discussed. I would like to emphasize thatwe are not talking about saving money: despite the large payments, the DIA will always have enough resources both from quarterly deductions by banks and due to the possibility of obtaining a loan from the Central Bank. We are talking about something else - about the responsible choice of the bank by the depositor. Some bankers are worried (and quite reasonably) that in the context of the increase in the amount of insurance protection (twice - up to 1.4 million rubles), depositors stopped looking at information about the bank, at its quality and choose the bank only by the levelof interest rates on deposits. that is, when not the entire amount of the deposit is subject to insurance compensation, but only a part of it. Thus, part of the risk will remain on the depositor. In our opinion, it is not worth making changes to the existing procedure and conditions for the payment of insurance compensation at present. We can provoke unnecessary distrust of people's savings in banks. What is needed is to increasethe responsibility of bankers for the quality of doing business and the financial stability of banks, the development of a risk-oriented approach to regulation and supervision and the introduction in practice of a legislative decision on a differentiated system of payments to the deposit insurance fund. From July 1, 2015, the volume of deductions to the insurance fund will depend on the size of interest rates on deposits, and from next year it will be possible to assess the financial stability of the credit institution when determining the amount of such contributions. In ouropinion, this should encourage the management and owners of banks that conduct an aggressive policy in the deposit market to take measures to choose more balanced tactics. On the other hand, the mechanism of rate differentiation will contribute to increasingrevenues to the deposit insurance fund and will become a factor in increasing the systemic stability of the banking sector. The Bank of Russia will continue to use its powers to limit banks' interest rates where necessary. Now we have such powers , and interest rates are limited to 10 banks. In our opinion, it will be possible to return to the question of the expediency of changing the conditions and procedure for insurance payments in the second half of 2016, after the new model of deductions to the Deposit Insurance Fund is fully operational, an analysis of its impact on the interest rate policy of banks will be carried out. It would be wrong, without introducing one approach, to rush to change it. One last thing I'd like to say. We're talking about external challenges,we're talking about the structural problems that the economy faces. Everybody understands that the new conditions are forcing the whole economy to change. It has to respond to new challenges by lowering costs, increasing productivity, that is, becoming more efficient. This fully applies to the economy. Banks must improve their management, risk management, reduce costs, introduce new technologies and products, be customer-oriented, finance investments, small and medium-sized businesses, import substitution projects, while ensuring reliable protection of the interests of depositors and creditors. I am absolutely sure that our banking system can do all this. I wish you success in this work. Thank you very much for your attention.

Title: Speech at the discussion at the American Chamber of Commerce "Key to unlock and drive growth"
text: Speech by the First Deputy Chairman of the Bank of Russia K.V. Yudaeva at the discussion at the American Chamber of Commerce "Keu Io ipiosk apsi sig?je dgo??GY" on September 24, 2015 September 24th, 2015 Performance The Russian economy is currently going througha very interesting period in its development. The stage of initial adaptation of the economy to the changes in the situation in global commodity markets over the past 12 months is coming to an end. The balance of payments has almost completely adapted. The current account balancehas increased to about 6% of GDP, but so far this has been mainly due to a reduction in imports, and not due to the growth of non-primary exports. There has been a change in relative price ratios, and as a result, a new combinationof competitiveness levels (in other words, a new competitiveness map) of various industries serving both domestic and external demand emerges. The economic downturn is still ongoing and, according to our calculations, may continue for several morequarters. or debt restructuring in both the corporate and consumer sectors. All this creates the basis for the return of the economy to growth in the new conditions. The policy of the Bank of Russia is currently aimed at maximizing the adaptation of the economy to new conditions, while maintaining and strengthening price and financial stability, which are the basis for sustainable and balanced growth. The transition to a floating exchange rate has already acceleratedthe initial adaptation of the economy to low commodity prices, has become a key factor in the adaptation of the balance of payments. The introduction of foreign exchange refinancing instruments for banks has allowed reduce financial stability risks during this transition period. Monetary policy measures have so far managed to keep inflation from unwinding further after the jump caused by the depreciation of the ruble following oil prices last year. This policy has also become one of the factors that led to a significant reduction incapital outflows for reasons other than debt repayment. The task for the next 2-2.5 years is to gradually reduce inflation to 4% per annum and keep it at this level. Our calculations show that this goal is feasible and absolutely compatible withthe team, moreover, complementary to the task of restoring sustainable economic growth. Our baseline forecast is based on an average oil price of 50 per barrel. US dollars per barrel in the next three years. We're also looking at two other scenarios, an optimistic one anda risk scenario. The optimistic scenario assumes that prices rise to 60 a barrel next year, 70 per barrel. US dollars per barrel in 2017 and 75 per barrel. US per barrel in 2018. Risk scenario implies a decline in oil prices to the level of 40 per barrel. In the baseline scenario, we expect that the growth rate of the Russian economy will remain negative in 2016 at the level (-0.5-1.0%), in 2017 it will reach small positive values, and in 2018 it may reach 2.5-3.5%. Andthe inflation will decrease to 5.5-6.5% in 2016, reach 4% in 2017 and will remain near the target level in 2018. In the optimistic scenario, economic growth will begin in 2016. In 2018, GDP growth rates will increase to 2.5-3.5% when the inflation rate reachesthe target level. In the risk scenario, unfavorable external factors will lead to a stronger and longer decline in investment and consumer activity. The fall in GDP may deepen in 2016 and continue in 2017. Reaching the trajectory of the riskscenario can be expected only in 2018. At the same time, inflation in 2016 will not decline so quickly, as in other scenarios, but with a high probability will reach the level of about 4% in 2017. I must say right away that the adaptationof economics to the new conditions will happen faster and more painlessly if monetary policy is accompanied by a responsible fiscal policy. That is, if measures are taken to ensure medium-term fiscal stability and increase the efficiencyof budget expenditures. Inflation will be stabilized faster and more painlessly if the rate of indexation of regulated prices and tariffs is consistent with inflation targets. It should also be noted that sustainable economic growth inthe emerging external environment requires structural changes aimed at increasing the flexibility of the labor market and commodity markets, which will make it possible to redirect resources to new growth points as quickly as possible. The difference between the emerging new modelof economic growth and the previous one is, among other things, that growth will have to be based largely on internal rather than external sources of financial capital. This is primarily due to the expected gradual normalization of the monetarypolicy of countries with reserve currencies, the transition of China and some other leading developing economies to economic growth. based on consumption, not exports, as well as with the continuation of sanctions against individual Russian companies and banks. Therefore, the role of the Central Bank as the body responsible for financial stability and the regulator of the banking and financial market is to strengthen the stability of the banking and financial sector, increase confidence in it and promote the developmentof financial infrastructure, financial markets and institutions. That is why the Bank of Russia has recently pursued a policy to strengthen supervision in the banking sector and the financial sector as a whole. introduction of internationally recognized regulatory methods. Notmany words about our work in the field of financial stability. Recently, we have been actively working to strengthen analytics in this area. We are constantly studying possible risks not only directly in the financial sector, but also in the corporate sector due to the presence of significant external debt in this sector. We monitor the risks of systemically important infrastructure companies, primarily NSD and NFCs. At the moment, we are also developing approaches to improve Westudy the situation in individual financial markets in order to identify the need (or lack thereof) for the introduction of macroprudential measures. If we talk about how we see the situation in the sphere of financial stability now, we can highlight the following main points. Firstly, with regard to the risks associated with servicing external debt. I can confirm the previously published information that at the moment the profile of actual paymentswill be quite even. Payments can be fully repaid at the expense of already accumulated assets and current receipts of foreign exchange earnings. Secondly, Of course, this is the main risk at the moment, but the measures taken in previous yearsto increase the stability of the banking sector and the recapitalization of individual banks this year make it possible to ensure that the level of capitalization of the banking sector is maintained at an adequate level. That is, capital in the banking sector as a whole to both to deal with bad debts and to meet the demand for loans. This does not negate the fact that individual weak players may leave the market, but in general the sector remains stable. Thirdly, at the moment, the situation with liquidity, both with ruble and foreign exchange, has improved significantly compared to the period of late last year - early this year. Interest rates in the ruble money market have recently been much less frequent than before, reaching the upper limitsof the percentage corridor of the Bank of Russia and are more often located in the lower part of the corridor. The provision of the market with foreign exchange liquidity can also be evidenced by a gradual decrease in demand for operations. currency refinancing of the Bank of Russia. As for external risks, thefrequency of repetition of episodes of significant fluctuations in world markets and, as a result, in the Russian market remains high. This may be due to a wide range of factors. In particular, it cannot be ruled out that the growth of volatility will accompany therise in interest rates in the United States, despite the fact that the markets have long begun to take into account the high probability of such an event when assessing assets. as well as that the Fed's move to raise rates will mean its confidence in the sustainability of economic growth in the United States. But experience has shown that the Bank of Russia's set of tools allows us to quickly stop the possible negative consequences of the implementation of external risks. We are constantly monitoring such risks and are ready to act actively if externalrisks create threats to financial stability in Russia. In conclusion, I would like to say what opportunities the current situation opens up for foreign investors. The decline in global commodity prices, as well as other global factors, before allits changes in the economic growth model in China, are changing the competitiveness map of the Russian sectors. The potential for the development of import substitution and non-traditional export sectors is emerging, that is, completely new opportunities for the developmentof production in Russia are opening up. At the same time, macroeconomic stability and financial stability are preserved in the country, steps are being taken to gradually and balanced development of the financial market. Such conditions certainly give a good chance for direct investment. Therefore , I am pleased to once again welcome the American companies present here and wish you successful work in Russia.

Title: Statement following the meeting of the Board of Directors
text: Statement by the Governor of the Bank of Russia Elvira Nabiullina following the results Meetings of the Board of Directors December 11, 2015 December 11, 2015 Today, the Bank of Russia decided to keep the key rate at 11% per annum. In my speech, I would like to present our vision of the current situation in the Russian and global economy, as well as the prospects for development for three years ahead. To discuss the factors on which we made this decision and the risks we took into account. The first is the situation in the global economy, and, above all, in the commodity markets. In recent months, the trajectory of oil prices has been between the baseline and riskscenarios, and we can say that the probability of maintaining prices below 50 per barrel has increased. Secondly, the dynamics of the Russian economy in the third quarter was somewhat more favorable than we expected. Third, with regard to consumer growth. Here the dynamics turned out to be somewhat worse than our expectations. Actual inflation is at the level of the upper limit of our forecast. As inflation slows down in accordance with our forecast and subject to the weakening of inflation risks, the Banto Russia will resume lowering the key rate at one of the next meetings of the Board of Directors. I will dwell on the main factors in more detail. I will start with the situation in the global economy and global financial markets and their impact on the Russian economy. External economic conditions and balance of payments External conditions remain challenging. The unfavorable trends that emerged this summer remain. First of all, this is the high volatility in world markets, which is due to the frequent changein our triplets and the expectations of global investors. This situation is associated with the presence of several sources of uncertainty. First, it is the speed of normalization of monetary policy by the US Federal Reserve. Market participants' revision of expectations on the trajectory of the Fed's rate hike leads to a reassessment of the attractiveness of assets. As a result, we observe fluctuations in the global foreign exchange market, instability in the scale and direction of capital flows, fluctuations in the stock and commodity markets. Second, investors continue to be concerned aboutthe growth prospects of developing countries, primarily China. China's slowdown could have a big impact on the global economy, including commodity prices. The growth rate of the world economy as a whole in the coming years will remain low. In our basicgnosis, we assume that the price of oil will return to an annual average of 50 in 2016. Nevertheless, the likelihood that this will not happen has increased and prices will remain below 50 per barrel for a longer period. With all the unfavorable external conditions, it should be noted that the Russian economy demonstrates the ability to quickly adapt to their changes. The adjustment of the balance of payments as a whole occurred at the beginning of the year. And in the third quarter, weexperienced economic stabilization. The economy's ability to adapt has affected the mood of global investors, who have become more positive about the prospects for the Russian economy. Despite the persistence of increased volatility in the global financialand commodity markets, in recent months the risk premium on Russia has decreased markedly, approaching the levels of other countries with a similar export structure. In the third quarter of this year, for the first time since the second quarter of 2010, there was a net inflow of private capital to Russia. Against the background of a decrease in the risk premium, some Russian companies managed to successfully place their bonds on international markets. With this in mind, we lowered the estimate of net private capital outflow for the year from 70 (in the November forecast in the Mainmonetary policy areas) to 58 billion, USD. Compared to the end of last year and the beginning of this year, the exchange rate risks associated with the repayment of external debt have significantly decreased. Our surveys of companies show that the payout profile minus intra-group loans has become fairly uniform, and banks and companies have accumulated a significant stock of foreign assets in liquid form. Current account receipts remain stable, with an estimated current account balance of about 63 billion this year. This is slightly higher than last year. In addition, we will continue to conduct foreign exchange refinancing operations and will respond flexibly to changes in banks' need for foreign exchange liquidity. Given all this, making paymentson external debt will not put additional pressure on the foreign exchange market. including at the end of this year. Despite the increased geopolitical risks and the risks of maintaining low oil prices, in general, the situation with the balanceof payments seems to be quite stable. Economic activity and the labour market Now about the second factor - the main trends in the dynamics of economic activity. In our opinion, we can talk about the completion of the most acute phase of the economic downturn. In the third quarter, the declinein GDP in annual terms was not as strong as in the second quarter. In general, for 2015, according to our estimates, GDP will decline by 3.7-3.9%. This is slightly better than our previous forecast of 3.9-4.4%. However, it is too early to talk about the formation of a stable positive trend. The dynamics of the main economic indicators gives a mixed picture. There are pinpoint signs of improvement, but the basis for economic recovery and, especially, relatively highand stable growth rates in the medium term has not yet been formed. Among the positive trends, I note the following. The first is the dynamics of a number of export-oriented industries. Among them are the extraction of raw materials and the production of intermediate materials (woodworking products, chemical industries). The growth of output in export-oriented industries, in turn, contributed to an increase in the turnover of transport, primarily pipeline and railway. The second is imposubstitution. The prerequisites for it are formed, first of all, by trade restrictions and the weakening of the ruble. Import substitution has become a key factor in supporting output in agriculture and a number of manufacturing industries. First of all, in the production of consumer goods: food, household chemicals, cosmetics, medicines, as well as in a number of related industries. Import substitution processes have made a significant contribution to improving the dynamics of production of capital goods. An increase in output was observed in some sub-sectors of mechanical engineering and electrical equipment, which was facilitated, among other things, by the need to reduce dependence on imports of technologies in the raw materials sectors, as well as in the defense complex.
