At the same time, I would like to note once again that in termsof positive shifts associated with import substitution or export growth occur only in certain market segments, in certain product groups and types of products, and do not yet make a significant contribution to the dynamics of output as a whole. The dynamics of production of foreigngoods and investments in fixed assets allows us to hope that the investment decline has slowed down. However, high uncertainty of economic prospects and weak consumer demand will continue to limit the growth potential of investment actsin the near future. Household consumption continues to decline at an accelerated pace against the background of falling real incomes of the population. The unemployment rate remains virtually unchanged, and wage dynamics are still the main channel for adjusting the labor market to the changed conditions. However, in the near future, in industries with a steady and significant reduction in output, the optimization of labor costs may accelerate. This may lead to a slight increase in the unemployment rate. Along with those Unemployment will continue to be constrained by companies' reluctance to lose skills and demographic trends. In addition to income dynamics, consumption is also affected by changes in the behavior of the population. Under the influence of high uncertainty, peopleare able to save more and take out loans less. Monetary conditions Before turning to inflation, I will focus on monetary terms. In recent months, they have gradually softened, but remained moderately tough. Most of the implementedwounds of its reduction in the key rate of the Bank of Russia have already been "won back" in the dynamics of bank rates, so the rates on loans and deposits in the second half of the year decreased more slowly than in the first half of the year. Some revival of corporate lending continued. The growth rateof lending to non-financial organizations at the beginning of December amounted to 9.5% by the beginning of the year, or 3.3% with the exception of currency revaluation. Support for credit activity is provided by a slight recovery in demand for loans in the face of lower rates, as well as a post-urgent slowdown in the deterioration of the quality of the loan portfolio. A positive contribution is also made by the implementation of the state program of recapitalization of banks. There are positive changes in the structure of lending. Thus, the growth of lending to a number ofsectors, including export-oriented and import-substituting (for example, chemical, food industry), resumed. At the same time, the requirements of banks to borrowers and collateral for loans remain quite stringent. The potential for growth in credit activityis limited by the high level of debt burden in the economy. We predict the preservation of moderate growth rates of credit and monetary aggregates, which will not create significant proinflationary risks on the part of the money supply. A few words about the situation with rubleliquidity. Over the course of this year, banks' demand for liquidity provided through our operations has decreased. This was due to the fact that liquidity in the banking sector came from financing budget expenditures from the Reserve Fund. At the same time, money market rates fluctuated near the key rate. In December of this year, a seasonal increase in banks' need for refinancing operations is expected. This is mainly due to the traditional For this period, the dynamics of cash and budget flows. Given the significant amount of free market collateral from banks, we plan to meet their needs mainly through auction operations. repo. At the beginning of next year, against the background of a seasonal reduction in the need for liquidity, the volumeof pre-delivery of funds at the auctions of the Bank of Russia will decrease. Inflation and inflation expectations Now read more about the most important factor for us - about the main trends in the dynamics of inflation. The growth rate of prices in monthly terms, excluding seasonality,has subsided in November. The gradual slowdown in annual inflation has resumed. However, it is slower than we expected. First of all, under the influence of exchange rate dynamics and inflation expectations. Monthly price growth rates, excluding seasonality, are still at a level higher than comparable periods of 2012-2013. By the end of the year, inflation will be close to 13%, that is, at the upper limit of our forecast. However, the contribution of the exchange rate to inflation is declining. Prices for different groups of goods and services reactto exchange rate dynamics with different strength and speed. In particular, the effect of the exchange rate on the prices of non-food products is longer. The decrease in the transfer effect was to some extent facilitated by the growth in the share of domestic products inthe consumption. We expect a sharp slowdown in annual inflation to 7.5-8% in the first quarter of next year. One of the reasons will be the base effect. According to our estimates, the process of adaptation to the imposed foreign trade restrictions on Turkey will have a negligible impact on inflation as a whole - in the range of 0.2-0.4 percentage points in the coming months. Moderately tight monetary and credit conditions and weak dynamics of consumer demand will be the key factors that will lead to a slowdown in the annual growth rate of prices to 5.5- 6.5% at the end of 2016. For the slowdown in inflation to be sustainable, it is necessary to reduce inflation expectations of the population and producers. Perceptions of future inflation, along with the level of rates, have a big impact on decision-making in the economy. These are the decisions of the population on how to dispose of their income - spend more or save. Business decisions about investment, changes in wages, and so on. Now the inflation expectations of the population and producers continue to beat an elevated level. In November, the inflation expectations of the population grew slightly. People are sensitive to the acceleration in the growth of prices of certain goods, especially consumer goods, even if it is caused by short-term factors. And this is understandable. However , after the actual inflation indicators decline, they reach a fundamentally lower level, there should be a turning point in the dynamics of expectations. One of the risks for our inflation forecast is that such a turning point may not occur immediately or be not sohigh, and inflation expectations will remain at a high level for a longer period. Taking into account the increase in inflation risks while maintaining the risks of cooling the economy, today we decided to keep the key rate unchanged. Once again, as inflation slows down in accordance with the forecast and subject to the weakening of inflation risks, the Bank of Russia will resume lowering the key rate at one of the next meetings of the Board of Directors. Let me remind you that our inflation forecast for the firstquarter of 2016 is 7.5-8%, and for January it is below 10%. Medium-term perspective: highlights In conclusion, a few words about our outlook for the medium term, which will be published today in the Monetary Policy Report. We are considering three scenarios for the development of the situation. The prerequisites for external conditions and the forecast of the main macro indicators in them have not changed significantly in comparison with those given in the Main Directions. In our baseline scenario, we expect the price of oil to be near 50 over the next three years. We continue to consider an optimistic scenario with a faster recovery in oil prices. This recovery is in line with the forecasts of many international organizations, analysts , and oil market participants. In addition, we are considering a risk scenario with the price of oil below 40. The latest dynamics of oil prices suggests that the relevance of this scenario has increased. In the baseline scenario, we expect that in 2016the economy will continue to adapt to new conditions, change its structure, the flow of resources to more productive sectors. According to our estimates, GDP will decline by the end of the year, but not as significantly as this year - by 0.5-1%. In the second half of 2016, we expect a reversal of the trend in the dynamics of inventories. According to our forecasts, the investment downturn will gradually end. In 2017, investment and production activity is projected to recover, primarily in sectors that have the potential to replace imports or competitiveness in foreign markets. Gdp growth rates in 2017, according to our estimates, will go into a positive area. Somewhat later, as we expect, consumption will begin to grow - as the dynamics improve beforethe moves in the context of a revival of economic activity. As for the state of the balance of payments, the current account balance in 2016-2017 will remain quite stable - about 50-60 billion US dollars. Net exports will make a positive contribution to the dynamics of GDP. The volume of payments on external debt will gradually decline. At the same time, repayments on external obligations will decrease faster than the demand for foreign assets will grow. This will cause a decrease in capital outflow to about 50-60 billion US dollars in 2016-2017. Taking into account the level of export earnings and the accumulated level of foreign assets, we expect that the Bank of Russia will not need to increase the provision of foreign currency refinancing. The situation will look differentin the event of a risk scenario. The fall in GDP in 2016 may be about 2-3%. Increased inflationary pressure, primarily from the exchange rate dynamics, will require a tighter monetary policy, that is, a higher trajectory of the key rate than in the baseline scenario. Further deterioration of external conditions, if it turns out to be prolonged, will require additional adaptation of the balance of payments and the economy as a whole. If necessary, we will be ready to use all the tools available to us, including operations in the foreign exchange market, to guarantee the maintenance of financial stability. We consider it possible to ensure not only the stable functioning of financial markets and the banking sector, but also the reduction of inflation to the target value of4% in 2017 with its stabilization near this level in the future. Consolidation of positive trends in the structure of economic activity, their spread to a wide range of goods and services, are the key to the recovery of the economy and its return to sustainable economic growth, regardless of changes in the conjuncture of world markets. The most important condition for the development of these trends is the creation of a predictable economic environment for the population and business, an integral part of which isprice stability. Question and answer session for the media Question (RIA Novosti news agency) Almost a year ago, on the night of December 16-17, the Central Bank suddenly raised the key rate to 17 percent per annum. How would you assess this December: how different are the conditions and situation then from today's situation and do you see similar risks until the end of this year? E.S. NABIULLINA Thanks for the question. The situation this year is fundamentally different from the situation last year, fundamentally. Let me remind you that last year therewas a combination of several powerful (we call them shocks) external shocks. First. A fairly rapid and deep drop in oil prices, which led to a reduction in foreign exchange earnings in the country. Second. Financial sanctions, to which theeconomy has already adapted. And the third. December was the peak of payments on foreign debts. And none of these three factors in the volume, on that scale this year, of course, is not. Despite the fact that the dynamics of prices is now unstable, oilprices are more volatile, but such a scale of decline, of course, is simply unrealistic. Payments on foreign debts this year will be several times less. We have adapted to financial sanctions. And the balance of payments has already adapted to the current conditions. And, probably,importantly, we have moved to a floating exchange rate, which allows us to be quite flexible and allowed us to reflect the changes in the external environment that have occurred during the year. Therefore, of course, the situation is fundamentally different, there can be no repetition of last year. Vopros (Vedomosti newspaper) If I may, I will ask two questions at once: one is very short, the second is longer. Elvira Sakhipzadovna, do you expect that for 2016 lending to individuals will support consumption or, as during this year, will it be a net deduction from consumption due to the fact that people repay debts more than they take new loans? And the second question about the next meetings, at which the Central Bank promises to reduce the rate: the next meetings are how much? How many are there: two or three? E.S. NABIULLINA Ok. Upcoming meetings. When we say "during the next meetings", we are referring to the next three meetings. As for lending to individuals, this year there will be a decline in lending to individuals. Next year, we expect a slightly positive growth rate of lending - about zero, maybe a little more. This is also due to the dynamics of real incomes of the population. We believe that in general, consumption and consumer lending will begin to make a positive contribution to GDP starting in 2017. Question (ITAR-TASS news agency) Elvira Sakhipzadovna, oil continues to show negative dynamics after the OPEC meeting last Friday. What are your expectations from further OPEC decisions and will this continue to have a downward effect onoil prices and, accordingly, on the ruble exchange rate? E.S. NABIULLINA Indeed, OPEC's decision has an impact on oil prices. But I would like to say that the oil market is rather characterized by volatility. And the spread of forecasts is very large: from the fact that prices will continue to fall, prices will stabilize approximately at this level to the fact that prices will rise. By the way, there are more of those experts who believe that prices will rise than those who believe that prices will fall. In our basicgnosis, I repeat, we proceed from the assumption that prices will rise from current levels, and next year they will be somewhere around 50 per barrel in average annual terms, but the risk that prices will be slightly lower does remain. As for the future actions of OPEC, well, it's up to OPEC to decide, but I think it's fundamentally important that there's really a change in pricing in the market, and the motivation for the behavior of the oil market participants has changed, that is, they're not tryingto keep prices at an acceptable level, how much to keep market share. And that changes the situation in the oil market. This is one of the structural factors in the oil market. which we take into account in our forecasts. Question (Kommersant newspaper) The Central Bank has not previously published detailed calculations on the risk scenario. And it is not known whether you will publish, but, probably, we will see it. I would like to ask a question about the assumptions about the Government's budget strategy in this risk scenario. Do you expect that the Governmentwill reduce the level of public debt placement somewhere at the level of 2015 in 2016, or will the Government switch to massive loans? And in this case, how do you assess the assumption that the government will recapitalize Vnesheconombank by placing OFZs, andwill this affect your calculations? E.S. NABIULLINA We will describe the risk scenario in a little more detail in the monetary policy report due to the fact that the probability of it has increased slightly, so you can see it today in the report. The fiscalstrategy is that we still assume that the deficit level in a risky scenario where the price of oil is kept below 40 a barrel, the government will keep the budget deficit at an acceptable level of 3 percent, that is, there will be no additional increase in public debt, because if this happens, it can have a significant impact on inflation. And as one of the inflation risks, we consider a possible easing of fiscal policy. We would very much liketo avoid that. As for the recapitalisation of OFZs, it seems to me that it is better to ask this question to the Government, as far as I know, consultations are still underway. Question (Rossiya 24 TV channel) One of the factors of uncertainty of this meeting of the Russian Central Bank was that it is happening on the eve of the Fed meeting on December 15-16. Maybe somehow move the deadline after the Fed meeting? And does our Central Bank have a plan of action, if the Fed stillhas its own rate, what will we do? E.S. NABIULLINA Our schedule of meetings of the Board of Directors is announced one year in advance and a few months before the beginning of the year. And we will stick to this schedule next year. It seems to me that thisgives more predictability, certainty to market participants when to expect a change in rates. Therefore, under the influence of various circumstances, we are not ready to change this schedule. And as for the Fed's decision, this is one of the factors that we took into account in our forecast, becausemany factors affect our decision-making. And I think the issue here is not so much that raise or not raise the rate at the next meeting of the Fed, because market participants are likely to assess that this will happen. A survey of market participants shows that this can happen. And, in our opinion, the possibility of raising the Fed rate at the next meeting was reflected in the value of various kinds of assets. Where uncertainty remains for investors is in the matterof the Fed's rate-hiking cycle itself. What will be the timetable for the normalization of US monetary policy: will it happen quickly, abruptly or slowly, gradually. And now, if there is a rethinking by investors of the dynamics of raising or raising rates by the Fed, there may be additional volatility. But I do not think that the Fed will raise rates quickly and sharply, because in general, their inflation rates are quite low - below their targeted level. And, it seems to me, there are some concerns, there are expectations, but nevertheless, the decision on December 16 will give more certainty to investors. There will be some volatility in the markets, this is expected, but I do not think that it will be significant. Question (Interfax news agency) I have two questions. On two occasions, the head of Sberban, German Gref, has publicly stated that Russia has experienced the strongest banking crisis in the last 20 years. Do you agree with his assessment? And if not, can you comment, in principle, on your attitude to the fact that the head of the largest Russian bankcan undermine the confidence of depositors? And the second question. The leadership of the Central Bank said this week, which will reduce the share of currency in the liabilities of banks, but did not specify what measures to do this in order to reduce the currency interest rate risks of banking. Can you comment on what the Central Bank will do: to raise FORs for foreign currency deposits or something else? E.S. NABIULLINA Well, first of all, the concept of a crisis is very voluminous, everyone puts their own understanding into it. Despite the different understandings, butin my opinion, there is no crisis in the banking system. The banking system, like the entire economy, is going through difficult times. This is true. But, in my opinion, the banking system has shown the ability to adapt quite quickly to the changed conditions. Because for the banking system at the beginning of the year, conditions changed significantly: and interest rates rose. and currency depreciation. And so the banking sector went through a period of losses and continues to go through a period of growth of problematic assets. But in general, the measures that were taken, our regulatory relaxations, the government program to recapitalize banks, the fact that banks by this time came to a more or less stable state as a whole as a banking system - this allowed this to happen. They can adapt quickly enough to new conditions. You know the latest earnings data. They are already positive: for 11 months 265 billion rubles. This is much more than we predicted at the beginning of the year, we predicted 100 billion, then raised it to 200 billion. This is higher, that is, the banking sector in these conditions finds profitable projects, profitable lending conditions. Credit to the real sector of the economy has begun to grow, albeit at a slow pace, but it is underway. And it's very important, we're seeing this, that banks have startedto choose borrowers very carefully, namely borrowers who demonstrate productivity and efficiency, and I think this is very important, among other things, to stimulate the restructuring of the entire economy. So, no trust can be undermined by words,because citizens are watching what is happening in banks and that the situation in banks is more or less stable. And we see this, by the way, in the dynamics of deposits of the population: deposits of the population are growing. And this is also a positive factor. We're reallydiscussing the issues associated with disincentivizing the currencyization of banks' balance sheets, both in terms of liabilities and assets , a different set of measures. But it's too early to talk about these measures. In any case, if they are implemented, they will be introduced gradually, so that the banking system adapts to them. And now there are just discussions. But we draw attention to the fact that there is such a problem. And it is important to reduce currency risks in the economy as a whole, in banks and in the non-banking sector. Question (Reuters agency) You said that banks may not need currency refinancing next year at all. And if we talk about VEB, if it needs foreign currency refinancing to repay its external debts, is the Central Bank readyto provide it, given that VEB is admitted under Regulation 312? E.S. NABIULLINA We really believe that foreign exchange refinancing will not be required not only next year, but, frankly, this year there will be no need to increase currencyrefinancing. Nevertheless, I will note that we have resumed or decided to resume annual currency auctions not because we believe that there is a lack of foreign exchange liquidity. Just to give additional comfort to the market, including theability to refinance those banks that want to refinance their annual loans. Although we have raised the rate on annual loans by 0.5 percentage points. Nevertheless, this tool remains in our arsenal. And there are conditions under whichthese resources are also provided. VEB has not yet applied for such refinancing, as far as I know. Question (RIA Novosti news agency) Can I ask you one more question, also about VEB? The government is now actively discussing the issue of recapitalization of the state corporation VEB. Does the Central Bank of the Russian Federation consider it expedient to recapitalize this development institution directly from the budget? Is the Central Bank ready to expand its supervisory functions to VEB and how can the recapitalization of VEB affect macroeconomic indicators and the banking sector as a whole? E.S. NABIULLINA Now the development of a solution on these issues continues. But, in my opinion, in any case, this will be done in such a way that macroeconomic stability does not suffer. Question ( Bloomberg) The Bank of Russia in its statement retained the phrase that it would resume the rate cut at one of the next meetings. It can be clarified, given that oil prices continue to fall, that the budget deficit will already be above 3 percent of GDP, because assistance to VEB is included, given the influence of such simultaneous factors that the Central Bank cannot influence, as, for example, it was with Turkey, how likely is it that the Central Bank will reduce the rate in the first half of the year? And when can the rate return to single digits? And one more question, if I may. We have heard throughout the year that the Central Bank coordinates its actions with the Ministry of Finance. Now, given the renewed discussion around the budget deficit, has this coordination been preserved or not? E.S. NABIULLINA As for our provision that we will resumethe rate change at one of the next meetings, I ask you to pay attention to how we say this. We are saying that we will resume the decline as inflation declines in accordance with our forecast (and I reminded you of our forecast, which is there, andyou can compare it with this forecast. as far as actual inflation is in line with our forecast) and with a decrease in inflation risks. Inflation risks include those you have just mentioned. If the situation develops not accordingto our basic scenario, but a little worse, respectively, we will rethink this situation. Budget policy can certainly affect. But we still proceed from the fact that both the Ministry of Finance and the Government believe that they will keep the budget deficit within 3 percent, respectively . We have close coordination with the Ministry of Finance, including coordination in general in the areas of both budget and monetary policy. Monetary policy is strongly influenced by the timing and amount of expenditure of funds from the Reserve Fund. So, of course, we take into account all these volumes, the rate of indexation of social payments - this also affects inflation. So, of course, we coordinate everything and discuss our policies. Question (Reuters) Tell me, please, one of the relaxations that was introduced in December last year and then extended was the preferential rate at which banks recalculated foreign currency assets to calculate capital adequacy. On January 1, respectively, this easing ends. For reserves, as we understood, the Central Bank will no longer extendit, but what about the preferential rate? E.S. NABIULLINA We continue to monitor, constantly monitor how these relaxations affect the balance sheets of banks, and we will, of course, make a decision in the near future, because there is not much time left until January 1. According to our current assessment, banks are quite capable of switching from a preferential to a regular market rate. Question (RBC newspaper) I wanted to ask for details about the risk scenario. You're saying oil is below 40, how much lower? We are talking about 30 dollarsa barrel, about 20? And are there any forecasts for the ruble exchange rate and inflation under such conditions? E.S. NABIULLINA In our calculations (we make model calculations of this risk scenario), we take the price of oil at about 35 per barrel. We do not give forecasts for the exchange rate inany scenarios, you know this - neither in the baseline, nor in the optimistic, nor in the risk scenario, including so that it is not perceived as a certain benchmark for the exchange rate. Our exchange rate is floating. As for other indicators, gdp in 2016is about a 2-3 percent drop, and inflation will be slightly higher - about 7 percent, in our opinion. Question (ITAR-TASS news agency) You mentioned the Reserve Fund, I would like to clarify. The Ministry of Finance this month, in December, plans to sell currencies for 650 billionrubles from the Reserve Fund. The Central Bank will be able to mirror this amount completely with its operations or will it have to spend international reserves after all? E.S. NABIULLINA And what the Ministry of Finance is going to spend this month from the Reserve Fund, this will be spent in rubles. We take this into account in the volumes of liquidity, liquidity forecasts, the needs for refinancing operations by the Central Bank that banks will present. Question ( Bloomberg) I have a question about truckers. Perhaps the answer to this question or the question itself will be more relevant at your next briefing. But maybe you see some risks, predict the contribution to inflation from their actions? E.S. NABIULLINA Wepredict the contribution to inflation of all the more or less significant factors that can affect inflation. You know our estimate of what contribution to inflation the trade restriction with Turkey can have, we have already said - 0.2-0.4 percentage points. Thesame calculations were carried out on the situation with the collection of additional fees from trucks. What can be calculated, namely, the amount of payments that are taken from trucks. In our opinion, this direct effect on inflation will be in the range of 0.1-0.2 percentage points. Of course, we do not calculate the possible risks associated with the functioning of commodity chains and so on. But the direct contribution is 0.1-0.2 percentage points, in our opinion, no more. Question (Wall Street Journal) Tell me, please, is the planto build up reserves up to 500 billion still in force and how is the Central Bank going to do this without harming the ruble exchange rate? And the second question, please, in your different scenarios, do you consider the possibility of lifting sanctions against Russia? E.S. NABIULLINA The intention to gradually and gradually increase the volume of gold and foreign exchange reserves to 500 billion remains with us. And, as we have previously stated, we will do this in such a way as to minimize the impact on both the exchange rate and inflation accordingly. In the risk scenario, we do not assume an increase in gold and foreign exchange reserves. Lifting of sanctions. We do not rule out the lifting of sanctions. But in our calculations and forecasts, we proceed from the fact that the sanctions will not be lifted. Question (Reuters) Tell me, please, and the risky sceneof the aria implies a rate cut? E.S. NABIULLINA The risk scenario, if we take the three-year perspective, assumes the possibility of rate cuts. It's just that the rate cut trajectory will be slower than in the baseline scenario. Question (Interfax news agency) The Central Bank in recent releases mentioned that, despite the fact that the last year it reduced the key rate, deposit rates for individuals remain attractive, which is proved by the dynamics of growth in household deposits. Next year, aboutyour assessment, how much can the dynamics slow down, given the fact that compared to December 2014 and the beginning of this year, the rates have fallen quite a lot? What are the Central Bank's estimates of the growth of deposits in 2016? E.S. NABIULLINA We think that deposits are going to continue to grow, the volume of deposits by individuals in the banking system is going to continue to grow. It's really important for the public to perceive the level of rates, and inflation expectations are very important here. Because when people bring money into the bank, they compare the yield on deposits not with the inflation that was before, but with the inflation that may be in the future. And so it's very important. so that the population believes in a decrease in inflation. And then this perception of positive bets will dryup. I think that the rates in general on deposits and loans in all scenarios will gradually decrease following the decline in inflation and the key rate, while remaining attractive to the population. Question (RBC newspaper) I have a question. The first time you presented a risk scenario, you said that this is a scenario that is unlikely to come true. Now the risk scenario is becoming relevant, oil prices are almost at 35, and will there be some new scenariothat will become a new risk scenario this time? E.S. NABIULLINA No, we are not preparing a new risk scenario. And even this risk scenario, although we say that its probability has increased, but I repeat that we believe that it is less likely than ourbaseline scenario with an oil price of 50 per barrel of the United States. We are not preparing any new scenarios now. Thank you all.

Title: Bank of Russia Governor spoke at the International Conference "Modern Audit: Problems and Prospects"
text: Bank of Russia Governor Elvira Nabiullina spoke at the International Conference "Modern audit: problems and prospects" November 14, 2016 Performance (transcript) Good afternoon, colleagues. Let me give a detailed answer to the question that has been raised quite broadly. To begin with, the modern financial market is a complex organism,the effectiveness of which significantly depends on the quality of the work of many institutions that serve the adoption of investment decisions that generate the movement of capital between countries, industries and economic entities. And the efficiency of institutions in each individual country determines the competitiveness of the local financial market and, accordingly, access to world capital for the subjects of the national economy. The topic of audit quality is given paramount attention today, since for the most part shareholders, consumers of financial services and even regulators do not have the opportunity to independently verify the reliability and completeness of the disclosed information, assess the quality of corporate governance and the operation of risk management systems. Internaland external audit institutions are designed to perform this function in the financial market, a function that provides confidence in the information on the basis of which investors and regulators make their decisions. The Bank of Russia, as the regulator of the financial market, is extremely interested in developing the audit industry, improving the quality of audit work and curbing unfair practices. We want to be sure that if a financial institution has received an auditor's opinion, we can count on it, andwe must be sure that the reporting is reliable. Therefore, for the first time this year, we decided to take the initiative to hold a conference for a comprehensive discussion of the data. problems by members of professional communities. I am glad that thereis such a wide audience here, as I have already said: representatives of the largest banks and financial institutions, and internal audit units, which is very important, and our Russian and international audit firms. I also hope that we will havea constructive discussion of the state, trends and directions of development, the problems of the audit industry, including the problems of interaction between external and internal audit in the financial sector. I would like to thank AntonYermanovich (the Ministry of Finance, which regulates this industry, where many innovations are now being introduced) and Tatyana Alekseevna (the Accounts Chamber, undoubtedly, creates quality standards for external auditing), and our international experts - Robert Hodgkinson (on the problem of external audit) and Mark Karavan (on internal audit issues) for agreeing to participate in our conference. We expect that in a dialogue with participants in the audit services market, regulators will be able to develop optimal approaches to both regulation and supervision, and lay the foundations for the sustainabledevelopment of audit institutions in Russia. It is equally important for us to ensure high quality of work and transparency of both external and internal audit. I want to start with internal audit issues in financial institutions. In general, credit institutionshave competencies in organizing the work of internal audit and control services. Internal audit services of credit institutions successfully accompany the solution of such tasks as the investigation of abuses, support for inspections of external audits and externalaudits, independent assessment of risk management services, verification of the effectiveness of the methodology for assessing banking risks. In many organizations, the activities of internal audit and internal control services meet the requirements of the Russian regulator and are in demand by both owners and management of credit institutions. They build their work on the basis of the best international practices, adapt their activities to economic conditions, business realities, business models of the credit institution itself. Atthe beginning of 2016, 12.5 thousand people worked in the internal control and audit services of credit institutions - this is about 1.5% of the total number of employees of credit institutions. That is, we see that a large number of people are employed in this area. But not all withoutcloud. There are a number of problems that do not allow us to say with complete certainty that the institute of internal audit is fully operational. The following main problems of internal audit can be identified: - the interaction of internal audit services with the bank's management is often very formal; - low quality control. Most units do not have internal documents regulating the assessment of the quality of their work. Less than a third of internal audit units undergo an external performance assessment; - insufficient qualification of personnel of internal audit services in credit institutions. The Bank of Russia will continue to improve and develop its internal control and audit system. Our priorities in this area for responding to these challenges are as follows: - in our opinion, it is necessary to develop unified approaches to the conduct of internal control procedures, including risk-oriented planning, stress testing; - Development of internal control procedures that regulate theorganization of work on the management of the main risks. Here we need common approaches; - common approaches to the procedures and requirements for the preparation of recommendations based on the results of inspections by the internal control and audit services of activities are also needed; - development of unified approaches to control over the elimination of violations identified by internal audit; - improving the quality of interaction of internal audit with the owners and management of financial organizations; - as well as improving the competence of auditors and improving the certification of internal audit staff. The Bank of Russia is working on the creation of a unified system of national standards in the field of internal audit for the financial sector for credit institutions, as well as non-credit financialorganizations, which would be based on the application of the best international practices. Now a few words about external audit in the financial market. Unfortunately, there are frequent cases when audit organizations express in their conclusion an unconditionalopinion on the reliability of the reporting of credit institutions, from which the Bank of Russia is subsequently forced to revoke the license, including due to the significant inaccuracy of the reporting provided. This is a perennial problem, and it is nota purely Russian phenomenon. I will recall at least the story of the auditors Arthur Andersen and the American company Enron. After the high-profile bankruptcy of Enron, it turned out that the company, at the suggestion of its auditor, used a creative approach to the preparation of financial reporting. The case of Enron called into question the credibility of the accounts of thousands of American public companies, banks, insurance companies, financial institutions, in one form or another attracting funds in the financial market. As a result, the Sarbanesa-Oxley Act was passed, which established strict requirements for auditors, which made it possible to restore confidence and maintain the primacy of the American capital market, as we see it. Because the rigidity of the requirements for auditors is a necessary part of the credibility of the capital market. Skeptics talked about the growing costs of companies to ensure the quality and completeness of reporting to such an extent, that the market will leave the U.S. and move to other financial centers where the requirements are not so stringent. However, this did not happen - on the contrary, other financialcenters followed the example of the United States and tightened the requirements for disclosed reporting and the procedure for its audit. The Russian financial market is no exception and also needs to increase the quality of audit services. The scale of the problems of unreliablereporting in the financial sector is indicated by several figures. I will cite them. Since 2013, the licenses of 291 credit institutions have been revoked, and most of them in one way or another had facts of inaccurate reporting. 205 credit organizationsrecognized by arbitration courts as bankrupts from 2013 to 2016, the real value of assets, the interim administrations estimated that they accounted for only 40 per cent of the assets reported by these banks. Audit organizations could provide serious assistance insolving the problem of inaccuracy of bank reporting. But, unfortunately, cases have become more frequent when these organizations do not meet the expectations of financial market participants and the regulator. There are often cases when audit organizations really express in the audit report an unconditionally positive opinion on the reliability of the reporting of credit institutions. Of the mentioned 205 bankrupt credit institutions, 182 are there are about 90%, received unmodified audit reports. In 2016, licenses were revoked from 77 credit institutions, here 58 of them have already been declared bankrupt, and 52 of them, also 89.7%, almost 90%, had audit reports on the reliability of annual statements. A similar situation is developing in the audit market of non-credit financialorganizations. For example, in 2016, licenses were revoked from 17 non-state pension funds, and 8 of them had an unmodified audit report on the reliability of annual statements. In this situation, of course, it is difficult to consider the opinion of an auditor as a supporting market discipline tool that allows financial market participants to have confidence in the reliability of financial reporting. Organizations. I understand that you can't completely put the blame on the auditors alone, because they analyze the reporting that's provided, that's what the auditors tell us. And they're often falsified, it's not always easy to identify. But on the other hand, the ability to identify misstatements is a matter of auditor skill, whichunfortunately may not be enough. And we think it's a systemic problem. In our opinion, increased requirements should be imposed not only on the audit of financial institutions, but also on the quality of audit services providedto public shareholders and organizations whose securities are admitted to trading. The activities of public companies affect the interests of a wide range of investors, ultimately affect the investment climate. For public companies, it is required not only to expandthe audit in terms of compliance with mandatory standards, assessment of internal control and risk management systems, assessment of compliance of activities with the approved strategy, etc., but also a much wider coverage of audit services. Thus, today in our country, an independent audit of financial statements is not the powerful tool for building civilized and effective market relations, as it is recognized in developed countries. Unfortunately, we see that the situationis exacerbated by the recent decline in the audit services market, the prestige of the profession is falling, the number of audit organizations and certified auditors is decreasing. Only in five years, the number of audit organizations and individual auditorshas decreased by more than 15%, and almost a fifth of certified auditors have left the profession, so this should also be paid attention to. Unfortunately, We see that the market is also developing conditions for monopolization of the sphere by individual companies. Theexisting profitability gap creates an advantage for the largest audit organizations, and this does not always contribute to equal, equitable competition in the market. The mechanism provided for by the Law "On Audit Activity" ispractically not used to recognize audit reports in court as knowingly false. The multiplicity of self-regulatory organizations in the market has led to competition between them. Everything seems to be fine, competition, but we see that as a competitive weapon, self-regulatory organizationsuse the worst strategy - minimal demands on results, as a result of which a huge number of unscrupulous and sometimes illiterate auditors got on the market. Therefore, the competitive mechanisms of auditors do not always work well. It has become a negative practice that competitions for external audit are often conducted by executive bodies, rather than boards of directors, and boards of directors and audit committees are not included. This leads to a real conflict of interest inauditing. For several years, together with the Ministry of Finance, we have been working to improve audit regulation. In 2014, additional requirements were established for In 2015, the content of the audit report on the reporting of credit institutions was expanded, including the need to issue an opinion on the implementation of mandatory standards. But, in our opinion, this is only the beginning. We need to think seriously about improving the quality of the audit industry and improving the quality of regulation. By the way, international experts pay attention to this. Unfortunately, I must say that recently the E5AR mission, which analyzed the state of regulation and supervision in the financial market as a whole in mattersof audit quality, independence and qualification of auditors, this year recognized Russia as not fully complying with the Fundamental Principles on the Effectiveness of Banking Supervision Basel Committee on Banking Supervision. What steps are needed to improve thesituation? First, it is necessary to strengthen control over the external auditors of financial institutions. Secondly, it is necessary to introduce specialization in the activities of audit organizations operating in different sectors of the financial market. We believe that the Bank of Russia needsthe authority to maintain the register and monitor the quality of services of audit organizations and auditors who have the right to work in the financial market. That is, only auditors who have passed the selection procedure should be allowed to do this work. Thirdly, it is necessary to increase the requirements for the qualifications of auditors and the system of professional training, the introduction of specialization of auditors through additional training and advanced training. We also believe that it is necessary to consider the organizations of the financial market infrastructure, such as organizers of trading in the securities market, credit bureaus. There should be effective mechanisms for interaction on the exchange of information between the Bank of Russia and the government in order for all this to be effectively implemented. And, in our opinion,changes are required in the legislation on auditing activities. And I hope that today's conference will allow us to discuss in detail the directions of improving regulation so that we can, without delay, proposelegislative changes. We understand that this problem is acute, painful, and is realized not only by consumers of audit information, but also by the auditors themselves. We understand that often the auditor becomes a hostage to a situation where, on the one hand, On theother hand, it is necessary to give an objective conclusion that meets the high requirements of standards, and on the other hand, to show the so-called "prudence", when the market is shrinking, there is intense competition, not always bona fide. But, in our opinion,these problems cannot be dismissed, it is necessary to raise requirements, to create all conditions for bona fide audit companies to compete in the market. All - both investors, consumers of information, and the regulator could fully rely on the auditor's opinion as an independent and professional opinion. Thank you very much.

Title: Speech at a meeting with regional banks at the Federation Council
text: Speech by Elvira Nabiullina at a meeting with regional banks at the Federation Council April 12, 2021 Performance Good afternoon, Valentina Ivanovna! Good afternoon, dear colleagues! Thank you very much for organizing this meeting. We know that the Federation Council always pays great attention to the development of the banking system, especially the working conditions of regional banks, in order to see how banks work in the regions, supporting the economy, supporting our citizens. Although, I must say, with the development of financial technologies, the issues of geographical reference are already becoming less and less important, because banks can provide services thanks todigital ones. remote technologies, regardless of whether where they are registered, where they are. Nevertheless, we understand that banks that operate in the regions (often not very large banks) have different problems, their own business models, and we take this into account. A few years ago, we moved to the so-called proportional regulation. This was in 2018, when banks with a universal license and banks with a basic license were allocated, which primarily work in regions with smallbusinesses, with citizens. But back in 2013, systemically important credit organizations were singled out, which are subject to increased requirements, and we consider this necessary, since 12 systemically important banks now account for 75% of the sector's assets. Further, banks with a universal license are the largest category, there are 230 of them. Of these, 91 banks are regional (their head offices are not in Moscow), and they are directly involved in supporting the economies of almost all regions of the Russian Federation. Sometimes these are the only banks that are ready to support local enterprises, those enterprises that create jobs in the regions, contribute to economic growth. And we understand that in a number of Of course, there are not enough financial services in the regions and a number of settlements, so the issues of financial inclusion and the development of financial services are very important. The size of the assets of regional banks is about 6 trillion rubles (slightly less than 6% in the assets of the entire banking sector). Especially for this meeting, we once again analyzed howthe business models of regional banks are warehoused. I must say that two-thirds of them have universal and corporate business models, 10% mainly lend to individuals. There are also a number of banks - we call them low-crediting - in their loan assets less than 30%," and they mainly earn on the stock market, providing guarantees and settlement operations. You can say, that these banks - they rather have not decided on a business model than chosen a certain path of development. It is important that those regional banksthat have chosen corporate lending as a business model have made an absolutely proportional contribution to their market share in expanding the availability of loans for the economy, including small and medium-sized businesses. Last year, in the context of the pandemic,the growth of lending to enterprises by regional banks was 8.9%, and on average in the sector - 8.8%. That is, in principle, they actively supported business in the regions. Regional banks are also actively involved in project financing of construction. Threebanks around the country that work with escrow accounts are regional banks. This is a positive point, because regional banks mainly concentrate on local markets, raising funds and lending to developers in their region. For regionalbanks that have a universal or retail model, the growth driver is mortgages. 44 regional banks work with mortgages. This is both the most socially significant and, perhaps, the least risky type of lending. The growth rate of the mortgage portfolio of these banks is even higher than the average for the banking sector.
